events.name: Capital of Kai
events.venue: Te Waka Huia Wellington Museum, 3 Jervois Quay, Queens Wharf
events.long_description: How did Wellington become a culinary paradise? Capital of Kai tells the story through 100 years of Wellington's food creatives, restaurant workers, and café culture. It's a love letter to the hospo whānau who have shaped the city. Walk through galleries of heritage treasures: the Green Parrot's working griddle, Hiakai's light-up signage, Il Casino's couch, Shanghai restaurant's 1980s menu, the Matterhorn café's cowbell. You'll see the arc from 1930s British hotel dining (roast mutton, boiled vegetables, milky tea) through European influences brought home by migrants and travellers, and the diverse cuisines - Chinese, Malaysian, Indian, Syrian, Greek, Māori - that define Wellington now. Hungry for more? Feed your curiosity at Capital of Kai.

events.long_description:
New Zealand’s most successful rock series ever returns in 2026, focusing on an electrifying trio of landmark albums. Come Together is bringing three iconic albums to Wellington. This year, they take on Bruce Springsteen’s Born to Run, Radiohead’s OK Computer and Talking Heads’ Stop Making Sense. Each concert will faithfully recreate an album and follow up with a set of classics and deep cuts that span each artist’s catalogue. 
The group is made up of a rotating roster of Aotearoa’s most acclaimed rock musicians. What began as a bold celebration of legendary rock albums has since exploded into one of New Zealand’s most electrifying live concert experiences. The collective includes Jon Toogood, Tami Neilson, Liam Finn, Delaney Davidson, Reb Fountain, Julia Deans, Dianne Swann, Mel Parsons, Ed Knowles, Arahi, Jazmine Mary, Deva Mahal, and many more. Their endeavours have drawn thousands of fans, cementing Come Together as a must-see event on the music calendar.

events.id: Wellington Opera — Manon-St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Wellington Opera — Manon
events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
For its 2026 season, Wellington Opera brings one of the most popular and enduring French operas to life. Manon by Jules Massenet will feature Kiwi-Samoan tenor Pene Pati and Kiwi-Egyptian soprano Amina Edris. Joining this powerhouse duo is another New Zealander, baritone Phillip Rhodes will sing the role of Lescaut. Manon tells the tragic love story of Manon Lescaut and the Chevalier des Grieux. The story unfolds in five acts, exploring themes of love, desire, and the consequences of choices made in pursuit of pleasure. 
Pene Pati is widely known for his Sol3 Mio fame. He is a recent New Zealand Arts Laureate and is the first Samoan tenor to perform on the world’s top stages, including the Opéra national de Paris, Covent Garden, London and the Metropolitan Opera, New York.

events.venue: Circa Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Inside Circa Theatre’s waterfront venue, you’ll find two performance spaces. Both offer a smorgasbord of professional theatre throughout the year. Playwrights from international heavy hitters to brilliant Kiwi voices are represented. It also includes programming from comedies and cabarets to contemporary dance and pantomime. 
Before or after your show, visit the on-site café, brasserie and restaurant, Chouchou. It opens out onto a deck, where you can take in views across the harbour. Look up to admire the art installation above. Called ‘Velarium’, it undulates in the wind, mirroring the water in the harbour. 
Circa Theatre began its life in 1976. A breakaway group of actors and theatre practitioners decided that Aotearoa needed a new and innovative approach to theatre. Five decades later, it is still pushing boundaries, making people laugh and cry, and creating theatrical memories. 
If you don’t have your own Circa memory yet, there’s an opportunity to create one nearly every night of the week.

A Weekend of Qi — with Dr Margaret Macky | Strathean, Kāpiti
Qigong is a practice people discover and then quietly wonder where it's been all their lives. You'll leave this weekend with a practice that actually calms your nervous system — and one that you'll keep using.

Dr Margaret Macky is a retired medical doctor who came to qigong through her own chronic back pain — and stayed for the 25 years since. She has trained with Zhineng Master Wei Qi Feng and taught internationally, but she rarely offers in-person retreats in New Zealand. This July is one of those rare occasions.

The setting is Strathean Retreat Centre — 10 acres of open farmland edged with native tōtara forest near Ōtaki, just 50 minutes north of Wellington. A genuinely quiet place.

Over two days you'll learn the beautiful flowing qi forms of the Zhineng tradition and sit in guided qigong meditation — a practice that works with the body's own energy in a way that's hard to describe and easy to feel. No experience required. No particular fitness level. Just two days away from your usual pace.

If you've been curious about qigong, or you simply need two days that feel genuinely different, this is the one.

Places are limited and the weekend is fully catered — all meals, accommodation, and sessions included. Choose the option that suits you:

About Dr Margaret Macky

Dr Margaret Macky came to qigong in the late 1990s through her own experience of chronic back pain. As a medical doctor, she was well-placed to be sceptical — and well-placed to recognise, once the pain was gone, that something real was happening.
She has since trained closely with Zhineng Master Wei Qi Feng, qualifying as a Mingjue Gongfu teacher — a practice rooted in a deep consciousness state that she describes as qigong's most profound dimension. For four years she has taught an international audience through the World Consciousness Community, with intensive retreats in China and online courses reaching students across the globe.
Now retired from medicine and living near Takaka in Golden Bay, Margaret devotes her time to practice and teaching.

events.long_description:
Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society (Pōneke/Wgtn) #1 - SOLD OUT
SOLD OUT. A few tickets left for the Saturday night.

Standing show (Seating reserved for those who need it: ).

The wave doesn’t conform to the shape of the rock. It smashes it. The sea doesn’t pretend to be hospitable. It summons courage. And a shantyband never licks the captain's boot. They release another EP!

The best shanties invite us to open our hearts along with the bottle. To draw strength from camaraderie and drown our pettinesses. To seek the rough edge of the wave and savour the salt within. And so, the WSSS have issued a call to arms with their new collection: Never Mind the Rowlocks, Here’s the Wellington Sea Shanty Society.

Never fear if you find yourself adrift on a sea of AI slop, lapping at your hull, lulling you to sleep — Lake Davineer, Vorn dont Le Père Était Marin, Young Nic, Tomas el Largo, and Louis Quatorze are back again to fill your sails and slap the codfish slime clean off your cheeks.

Just when everyone is lamenting the empty galleys of the good ship Wellington, and those ol’ scurvy-mongers are promising renewed bounty if you would only tack five degrees to port or starboard come election time, these songs remind us the sea at least will sustain us, and there’s rum and (metaphorical) guns for them that wants to fight.

Lin Seal | Wellington Nautical History Monthly

events.id: Porirua Parkrun-Bothamley Park, Champion Street, Porirua - Mana-Event Finder
events.name: Porirua Parkrun
events.venue: Bothamley Park, Champion Street, Porirua - Mana
events.long_description:
What is Porirua parkrun? It is a free 5km walk or run event - It’s not about coming first or winning. You can go at your own pace and just enjoy being with other people. It is inclusive and the perfect way to start your weekend in the outdoors chatting to people.

The start occurs just upstream of the Bothamley Park carpark. This car park is off Champion street, opposite the intersection with Windley Street. Head to end of carpark where the concrete ends and there is a gate. For location see https://goo.gl/maps/wEohfp9bRu82.

The course is following the old coach road (circa 1870's) established for the early farms in the area. Today this historic track is located within a park, away from cars and now used by walkers, runners and cyclists.

The track is generally 3 metres wide with a gentle gradient and a compacted gravel surface beside the Kenepuru Stream through a picturesque wooded wild valley. (Note there is a pinch point for a short section after the 2km marker where participants need to go single file each direction for approx 30 metres)

The valley runs east-west with mature trees which means this has to be one of the most sheltered places, out of the wind to exercise in Wellington.

What does it cost to join in? Nothing - it's free! but please register before your first run or walk, so you can get your timing results. You only need to register with parkrun once, to participate at any of the parkrun events around the world. Don't forget to bring a copy of your barcode. If you forget it, you won't get a time.

How fast do I have to be? Walking is fine as long as you can finish the 5km. Please come along and join in whatever your pace!

One dog per adult is welcome, as long as it is on a short hand held lead.

Children welcome but those 10 years and under need to be kept within arms reach of a supervising adult.

Note there is no toilets in the park, so go before you go.

We're friendly! Every week we grab a post park run/walk coffee/tea at Get Fixed within Kai Tahi at 20 Parumoana Street, to mix exercise with socialising.

There are volunteering opportunities even week. So those doing Duke of Edinburgh or similar challenges can get volunteer credits. Ensure you contact us well in advance at "porirua@parkrun.co.nz"

Stuck in a rut at work or at home? Need fresh ideas? Facing tough decisions? Join Neil Thornton for this hands-on, fun-filled workshop on Creative Problem Solving and Decision Making.

Creative Problem-Solving Workshop

Course is free for NZ citizens and residents (please bring photo ID when attending workshop). If you are not a NZ citizen or resident a fee of $109 will apply, please phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.

Through engaging puzzles, group activities, and proven creativity techniques, you'll discover how to tackle challenges from new angles and find solutions you might never have considered. Learn to break through mental blocks, generate innovative ideas, and lead groups to make better decisions together. This workshop draws on Neil's background in teaching, test-preparation, and creative thinking to help you unlock your natural problem-solving abilities in a supportive environment.

· Simple techniques to generate ideas individually or in a group: brainstorming, mind-mapping, and more

· Practice solving puzzles that sharpen your lateral thinking skills

· Learn how to overcome blocks and restrictive thinking patterns

· Build confidence in leading problem-solving sessions with others

Neil creates a relaxed atmosphere where everyone feels comfortable contributing ideas and experimenting with new approaches. You'll leave with specific tools you can apply to your own challenges, plus handouts to help you remember what you've learned.

Neil's unique skill as an educator is his rare ability to blend evidence-based teaching techniques with the perfect dash of humor and storytelling, creating a learning environment where complex concepts become accessible and new skills feel immediately applicable to your real-world challenges.

Through engaging puzzles, group activities, and proven creativity techniques, you'll discover how to tackle challenges from new angles and find solutions you might never have considered. Step into the world of crime writing and discover how to build stories that grip readers from page one. Whether you’re brand new to writing or already have a few drafts under your belt, this course will sharpen your skills and push your storytelling further.
 Bring a notebook and pens—you’ll need them.

Writing fundamentals that keep prose tight and compelling.
Crime genres and what makes each tick.
Heroes, villains, and everyone caught between.
Research techniques that make your fiction feel authentic.
Plotting, story arcs, and whether outlines are your best friend—or sworn enemy.
How to craft loglines, taglines, and blurbs that hook readers instantly.

Map out a crime novel or short story.

events.long_description:
Are you looking to polish your CV and cover letter writing skills to nail your next job application? This course provides you with the tools to create a strong and updated CV and cover letter writing, using skills that are personalised to you.

Description
Explore how to appropriately structure and polish your CV and cover letter in order to achieve optimum results. This course prioritises you. Identify your key skills and weave these into your CV and cover letter to land you your next job interview.

Whatever job you are going for, there are key characteristics that should not be missed in your CV and cover letter. The focus of this course is to provide you with the same lens as a recruiter. By learning how your job application is reviewed by a recruiter, you will gain skills to streamline your CV, and improve your cover letter writing. This will increase your chances of being a successful candidate and sets you up to land an interview for your ideal job.

It doesn’t matter what previous experience you have - everyone has a range of skills that they can offer to their future employer. Fortunately, a strong and realistic CV and cover letter will showcase these skills and increase your chances for job success.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Recognise the features of an effective, well-crafted CV and cover letter and apply these to your own job applications;
- Apply different approaches, styles and techniques while writing your CV and cover letter depending on the context and job;
- Help others with their CV and cover letter writing (friends and whānau).

[Note: You must be a NZ citizen or resident to qualify for the free course fee option. A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.

This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.

Cultivating true resilience is an intentional practice of the mind, body, and soul. It is rooted in deep self-knowledge and personal empowerment. In our rapidly changing world, the ultimate question we must ask ourselves is: How can I unlock my unique strengths and capacities to not just survive these demanding times, but truly thrive?
By implementing a "living" practice of mindful strategies, creative expression, and physical awareness, we can empower our thinking, elevate our emotional well-being, and bring a renewed vitality to our life's work.
What to Expect
This workshop offers you a rich tapestry of practical tools, storytelling, and collaborative discussion. Together, we will explore diverse pathways to foster courage, helping you shift from a state of survival to one of thriving—even while navigating the daily pressures of stress, grief, anxiety, or the fear of an uncertain future.
What You Will Take Away:
Mindful Strategies: Daily, actionable practices to anchor your thoughts and reduce overwhelm.
Creative & Physical Outlets: Expressive tools to release tension and process complex emotions.
A Personal Roadmap: A clearer understanding of your innate strengths to help you navigate future transitions with confidence.
Details & What to Bring:
Duration: Full-day workshop
What to bring: A personal journal and your favourite pen or pencil. (However, paper and pen will be provided if you need).
Step out of the survival loop. Join us to reclaim your inner strength and cultivate the courage to thrive.

events.name: Kintsugi Workshop in Wellington // Hutt Art Society Inc
events.venue: Hutt Art Society IncLower Hutt, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop.
After several SOLD OUT workshops in Wellington here is the next one... August 2026
Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)
Saturday 1st August - 11:00am - 1:00pm

Ema Frost is a very clever Kiwi Artist, who has been teaching Kintsugi for 5+ years and regularly travels to Japan to study and learn new techniques. Ema's illustrations and ceramic works sit in many of our countries best galleries, and whose products and merchandise sell in the most stylish design stores and gallery shops. Her style is enchanting - quirky, feminine and colourful, and clearly influenced by her travels throughout the world, usually off the beaten track.
Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.
KintsugiIt's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your knew skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.
What you will take away:A finished artwork pieceA understanding of KintsugiKnowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.
KintsugiIt's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your knew skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.
What you will take away:A finished artwork pieceA understanding of KintsugiKnowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

events.long_description:
The Creation Voyages, from New Zealand Poet Laureate Robert Sullivan’s award-winning children’s book Weaving Earth & Sky is an exciting new performance from the New Zealand String Quartet – Te Rōpū Tūrū o Aotearoa. Through music and storytelling, with imagery by Gavin Bishop, the NZSQ vividly reimagines Aotearoa’s creation myths in an engaging, whānau-friendly performance.

Across 45 minutes, string quartet will meet live storytelling. NZSQ violinist Peter will narrate Ranginui and Papatuānuku’s embrace, their separation and the rise of the Atua, while accompanied by live sound effects and music played by the NZSQ on their unique instruments. Including, Pokarekare Ana, excerpts from Vivaldi’s Four Seasons and Holst’s Planets Suite.

See you at Ruth Gotlieb (Kilbirnie) Library for a voyage back to creation!

events.name: Sunset Guided Tour
events.venue: Stonehenge Aotearoa, 51 Ahiaruhe Rd, Carterton
events.long_description:
Experience Stonehenge Aotearoa at its most breathtaking — as the sun dips below the Wairarapa horizon.
Our Sunset Guided Tour blends astronomy, storytelling, and the natural beauty of twilight for an evening you will never forget.

Led by one of our knowledgeable guides, this 90-minute experience explores how ancient cultures used the Sun to track time and mark the turning of the seasons. You’ll discover the scientific and cultural thinking behind the Henge’s unique Southern Hemisphere design before watching the sunset alignment from inside the stone circle.

Weather permitting, you’ll witness how the setting Sun interacts with the structure — a striking moment that links ancient knowledge with the rhythms of the natural world.

Duration and Schedule
• Allow: Approximately 90 minutes
• Start Time: Begins one hour before sunset
• Availability: Offered any day with advance booking

events.id: Jewellery-making on Thursdays, 8-week block, Level 2+-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Jewellery-making on Thursdays, 8-week block, Level 2+
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Our popular weeknight block classes are the best way for keen makers to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment. This class will be held at our new waterfront location, Market Lane!

The course starts on Thursday 25 June and runs for 8 weeks till Thursday 13 August, 5.30pm-8pm.

This class is designed for students who already have some skills and are ready to develop their craftsmanship in a lively, warm, and supportive environment. Guided by our highly skilled tutors, you’ll build confidence, refine your techniques, and gain the satisfaction of making jewellery that reflects your personal style.

If you’re brand new to jewellery making, we recommend beginning with our Tuesday Evening 8-Week Beginners’ Block, which gives a solid foundation in essential techniques before moving on to this class.

At Level 2, the focus is on precision and technique. Students explore the art of chain making, a classic jewellery making project that develops fine soldering skills and accuracy in construction. This project is an excellent way to build confidence with the torch and create a piece of jewellery that is both functional and beautiful. The finished chain can become a pendant, bracelet, or necklace, or you may choose to adapt it into a design of your own.

At Level 3 and above, the emphasis shifts toward creativity and design development. Students at this stage are encouraged to take on more complex projects, experiment with new and challenging techniques, and bring their own design ideas to life. With the guidance of our skilled and supportive tutors, you’ll learn how to push your skills further, problem-solve during the making process, and refine your eye for detail and design.

Evening classes are not just about the technical side of jewellery making - they are also a chance to slow down, enjoy the process, and be part of a creative community. Many students return term after term, finding the rhythm of regular making both mindful and rewarding.

Please note: this class does not include a materials allowance, giving you the flexibility to choose your own metals, stones, or other materials. You only pay for what you use, making it easier to customise your projects and work at your own pace.

Our booking system asks for full payment at the time of registration (via credit card, PayPal, or AfterPay). If you don’t have access to these options or would like to pay in instalments, please email us and we’ll happily arrange an alternative.

events.name: Sat Afternoon Jewellery Making - Beginners
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Spend your Saturday afternoons immersed in creativity, learning the timeless craft of jewellery-making in our warm, welcoming studio.

This short course is the perfect introduction for complete beginners, guiding you step-by-step through the essential techniques used by jewellers. You’ll start by working in copper or brass, building confidence as you learn to cut, heat, shape and texture metal. From there, you can choose to move into silver and bring your ideas to life in more refined pieces.

A beautiful textured ring band is an ideal first project, but once you’ve mastered the basics, the possibilities really open up—create earrings, pendants, or small bespoke pieces that reflect your personal style. You’ll learn how to solder using a jeweller’s torch, refine your finishing techniques, and polish your work to a professional shine. It’s a hands-on, deeply satisfying process, and there’s nothing quite like wearing something you’ve made yourself.

Materials are purchased as you go, so you can tailor your projects to your budget and ideas. Beginners typically spend around $50–$70 on metals over the course.

This block is ideal for teens and young creatives aged 12 and up.
Please note: anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.long_description:
Forest & Bird - The Future of Conservation Hui
Nature Can't Vote, But You Can
Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington

Who is giving nature a voice this election?

Aotearoa New Zealand's protected conservation land is under threat. Forest & Bird's maps of at-risk land have sparked a national conversation - and this election we have an opportunity to show politicians how many of us value nature. Join us in Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington this August, to hear from conservation experts about what's at stake, and your political candidates on what they plan to do about it.

The Election Conversation - Evening Event
Who: Open to the public
When: Saturday 1 August 2026, 6pm–9.15pm (programme starts 6.30pm)
Where: New Zealand Parliament Buildings, Banquet Hall
Cost: Free
After networking and nibbles from 6pm, the programme features a keynote address on local conservation issues, hear an overview of what's at stake for nature this election - including what the Conservation Amendment Bill could mean for the region, and a moderated political panel with representatives from across the spectrum. Audience questions will be put directly to the panel, giving you the chance to hear how parties plan to tackle the issues that matter most for nature.
Come along, get informed, and be part of the conversation this election.

Mobilise for Nature - Afternoon Session
Who: Priority access for Forest & Bird branches, networks, members, and volunteers - open to anyone who wants to get involved
When: Saturday 1 August 2026, 1pm–5pm (optional networking from 5pm–6pm)
Where: New Zealand Parliament Buildings, Banquet Hall
Cost: Free
Whether you're a long-time advocate or just getting started, this session is for anyone who wants to make a difference for nature this election. Hear from inspiring local speakers - including expert voices on the Conservation Amendment Bill and what's at risk, take part in a practical workshop, and connect with others from across the conservation community. You’ll leave with the tools, skills, and relationships to help support the campaign and strengthen your future advocacy for nature.

Can’t join on the day but want to get involved? – contact us at generalelection@forestandbird.org.nz

events.venue: St Andrews on the Terrace, 30 The Terrace, Wellington
events.long_description:
For its second concert of 2026, Supertonic is thrilled to be joining forces with the renowned Oregon Chorale of Portland for Into the West: A Choral Journey of Voice, Land and Connection. This will be the Supertonic’s first international collaboration with another choir in its twelve-year history. The one-night-only concert, to be presented on Saturday 1 August at St Andrew’s on the Terrace, will see both choirs perform individual sets before joining forces to bring the evening to a memorable close.

Into the West invites audiences on a musical journey celebrating renewal, discovery, and the landscapes—both real and imagined—that shape our sense of home. Drawing inspiration from the Pacific horizon, the programme weaves together New Zealand and Māori folk songs, works by Pacific Northwest composers, global choral favourites, and film-inspired pieces. The result is a concert rich in storytelling and atmosphere, uniting contemporary voices and timeless traditions in a spirit of connection and exploration.

Founded in 1985, the Oregon Chorale is an auditioned community choir based near Portland, Oregon, in the Pacific Northwest of the United States, and is led by Artistic Director Jason Sabino. Guided by its mission to inspire and connect communities through exceptional choral performances and meaningful educational outreach, the Chorale performs a wide range of repertoire, from classical masterworks to contemporary works by living composers.

Supertonic shares Oregon Chorale’s enthusiasm for varied repertoire, striving to push the boundaries of what choral music can be. Since the choir was formed in 2014, it has performed concerts spanning the entire musical spectrum, from Vaughan Williams’ Mass in G Minor, Vivaldi’s Gloria, and Fauré’s Requiem to pop and rock spectaculars celebrating Fleetwood Mac, David Bowie, Elton John, and Queen. For this concert, Supertonic will be directed by Isaac Stone, who is excited to be working with the choir again for the first time since the smash-hit It’s All Coming Back in November 2024.

This promises to be an evening of choral music to remember. Tickets are strictly limited and expected to sell out.

Tickets available from www.supertonic.org.nz from Tuesday 23 June 2026

events.long_description:
Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society EP release tour (Pōneke/Wgtn) #2
The wave doesn’t conform to the shape of the rock. It smashes it. The sea doesn’t pretend to be hospitable. It summons courage. And a shantyband never licks the captain's boot. They release another EP!

The best shanties invite us to open our hearts along with the bottle. To draw strength from camaraderie and drown our pettinesses. To seek the rough edge of the wave and savour the salt within. And so, the WSSS have issued a call to arms with their new collection: Never Mind the Rowlocks, Here’s the Wellington Sea Shanty Society.

Never fear if you find yourself adrift on a sea of AI slop, lapping at your hull, lulling you to sleep — Lake Davineer, Vorn dont Le Père Était Marin, Young Nic, Tomas el Largo, and Louis Quatorze are back again to fill your sails and slap the codfish slime clean off your cheeks.

Just when everyone is lamenting the empty galleys of the good ship Wellington, and those ol’ scurvy-mongers are promising renewed bounty if you would only tack five degrees to port or starboard come election time, these songs remind us the sea at least will sustain us, and there’s rum and (metaphorical) guns for them that wants to fight.

Lin Seal | Wellington Nautical History Monthly

⚓⚓⚓

The scuttlebutt is true...⛵

The most seaworthy sea shanty band in the South Pacific is releasing their long-awaited 4th collection of new and old maritime bangers:
'Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society'.

All aboard as we set sail for the salty horizon. Prepare to be battered once again by the 4-sailor squall of pure shanty.


⚓⚓⚓

WELLINGTON SEA SHANTY SOCIETY

Aotearoa New Zealand's Most 'Sea Worthy' Shanty Group™ have been belting out traditional and original sea songs from Aotearoa, France, Spain, the UK and more, since time immemorial (2012).
The W.S.S.S have toured Aotearoa and France multiple times and are known for their rowdy and participatory live shows. They've performed at Paimpol (one of the world's largest shanty festivals), Splore, Albany Folk Festival (Aus), Quebec Sea Shanty Festival (Canada) and a shipload of other festivals in NZ, France & Canada.

They will be playing new classics from their forthcoming EP 'Never Mind the Rowlocks' as well as your foamy favourites from the 'Sea Shanties of the 70s, 80s, & Today!' EP and their 'Now That's What I Call Sea Shanties' series.

events.venue: Breaker Bay Hall, 150 Breaker Bay Road, Wellington
events.long_description:
The scuttlebutt is true...

The most seaworthy sea shanty band in the South Pacific is releasing their long-awaited 4th collection of new and old maritime bangers:
'Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society'.

All aboard as we set sail for the salty horizon. Prepare to be battered once again by the 4-sailor-squall of pure shanty.

Singalong shanties! Nautical games! Best dressed prizes!

Limited tickets.

Live review from Maryanne Cathro:

"Having been handed a booklet of lyrics... we grab seats around the edge ... It’s all very casual, with the added delight of people dressed as sailors in striped tops and white hats, pirate hats and newspaper hats, and even life jackets! It’s like they know what is about to happen!

As the band takes to the stage... a spotlight falls upon storyteller Louis Tait. Microphone in hand, he starts to weave a tale of the sea, to riffs of music from the band.

Back to those booklets of lyrics – this whole show is a singalong, and it is with great enthusiasm that the first shanty begins...the audience sings and stomps and laughs.

It’s hard to describe the impact of stadium concert-level audience euphoria in a small community hall, yet that is what it is. Bopping bodies, bathed in coloured light, so into the music, which is just fantastic in every way. The dance area is more like an ecstatic mosh pit.

What is it about shanties? They came out of shared singing, and so they lend themselves to this, I guess. But what Vorn Dont le Père Etait Marin and Lake Davineer bring to these songs is a thoroughly modern, old-fashioned sense of fun and magic.

I am reserving specific comment for the currently most famous shanty in their repertoire, ‘The Wellerman’... The crowd goes wild! The stomping probably puts the hall onto Geonet. I would not have been surprised if a giant cracken had appeared and body-surfed the crowd."

WELLINGTON SEA SHANTY SOCIETY

Aotearoa New Zealand's Most 'Sea Worthy' Shanty Group™ have been belting out traditional and original sea songs from Aotearoa, France, Spain, the UK and more, since time immemorial (2012).

events.long_description:
South Summit are soon to release their sophomore album, RUN IT BACK on June 12 and to celebrate, they have announced RUN IT BACK NZ TOUR.
Coming to Aotearoa this July and August the band will take on Queenstown hotspot Yonder on Thursday 30 July, The Loons, Lyttleton on Friday 31 July, San Fran, Wellington on Saturday 1 August and Auckland’s Double Whammy on Sunday 2 August. 
Run It Back marks the band's second album, featuring stand out singles ‘TOP OF THE HILL’ and ‘ON THE DASH’ which have sent strong signals toward the confident evolution of their sound. The twelve-track record  represents a period of experimentation for the band; one where they found themselves pulled towards threads of funk, hip hop and R&B, while also driven by a desire to galvanise their signature blend of reggae and rock.
In 2024, they released their highly anticipated debut album The Bliss, a reggae-infused indie rock record that showcased both tight songwriting and a willingness to experiment across styles. It debuted at #2 on the ARIA Album Charts and propelled the band into a new tier, with heavy Triple J support, major festival slots and international touring, including appearances at Falls Festival, Groovin The Moo, SXSW Sydney, Vivid LIVE Debut at the Sydney Opera House plus a huge Australasian headline tour.
After a recent visit to Aotearoa to play at Six 60’s new Country & Roots Festival Sweet Home Aotearoa, South Summit now return to New Zealand for their third headline tour in the country. These four shows promise the bands’ renowned live charisma and classic fan favourites, whilst welcoming fans into a brand new era. 

San Fran holds a Supervised License, meaning minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue. Minors are of course not allowed to purchase alcohol under any circumstance.

Run It Back marks the band's second album, featuring stand out singles ‘TOP OF THE HILL’ and ‘ON THE DASH’ which have sent strong signals toward the confident evolution of their sound.
The twelve-track record  represents a period of experimentation for the band; one where they found themselves pulled towards threads of funk, hip hop and R&B, while also driven by a desire to galvanise their signature blend of reggae and rock.
In 2024, they released their highly anticipated debut album The Bliss, a reggae-infused indie rock record that showcased both tight songwriting and a willingness to experiment across styles.

events.venue: Whisky & Wood, 60 Cambridge Terrace, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join our constellation and step into the Coven cosmos. This year, The Coven Ball returns for its third revolution and we’re leaving Earth behind.

Stardust invites you into a universe of celestial bodies, alien glamour, intergalactic experiences, and otherworldly energy. Whether you arrive as a being of light, a soft-space siren, or something entirely unknown — this is your orbit, dress to transcend.



What to expect:
A transformed, two floor venue at Whisky & Wood! Including two distinct spaces, our very own dancefloor dungeon with DJs, aliens, and energy all night. And our celestial ball chamber, with lounging areas, low sensory lighting, interstellar entertainment, activities and treats.

Coven kaupapa:
For queer women and gender minorities, spaces like this are rare, vital, and sometimes, life-changing. In a world that constantly centers cishet norms, Coven offers a space where we are the default – where you can fully show up as yourself, be seen, celebrated and surrounded by YOUR community.

For many in our Coven, this is one of the only opportunities we feel comfortable enough to experience nightlife free from the male gaze, tokenism, fear, or the need to shrink ourselves to fit in. It’s a space where sapphic, trans, nonbinary, and gender-diverse people aren’t just welcomed – we are centered. It’s for those who are often pushed to the margins, who rarely feel represented in “inclusive” spaces that still cater to the mainstream.

This night exists because we need it – and because we create it, together.

Coming solo? You’re not alone:
Don’t be nervous if you’re planning to come on your own – Coven is built for connection. Whether it’s your first queer event or your hundredth, you’ll be surrounded by a community that gets it. From the moment you arrive, there’ll be friendly faces, welcoming vibes, and plenty of chances to mingle, and connect. Coven is about belonging – and there’s a place here for you.

events.name: The WBS presents: The Raven Mavens Quartette CD Launch Concert
events.venue: Abandoned Taproom Petone, 38 Fitzherbert St, Petone, Lower Hutt
events.long_description:
The Raven Mavens Quartette return to the Wellington Bluegrass Society for the launch of their eagerly anticipated new CD.

Since releasing their previous album of original songs in 2020 — also celebrated at the Bluegrass Society — the band have continued to delight audiences throughout Wellington, the Wairarapa and the Kāpiti Coast with their distinctive blend of blues, roots, folk and swing influences.

The Raven Mavens have become renowned for their catchy, blues-infused original songs, written primarily by band leader Cindy Muggeridge. Drawing on her deep roots in blues piano, as well as Latin rhythms and rock ’n’ roll grooves, Cindy's latest collection tells stories of life, love and loss, alongside wry social and political observations. In both performance and recording, she is joined by the exceptional talents of Kate Marshall on vocals, violin, accordion and flute; Marian Carter on vocals, saxophone, clarinet and recorder; and Anje Glindemann on vocals, drums and percussion.

The band are also excited to feature two original compositions by Kate Marshall on this new recording, with Kate taking the lead on piano, supported by the other Mavens.

A unique all-female ensemble, the Raven Mavens Quartette gives every member the opportunity to shine as both instrumentalist and vocalist. What began in 2011 as a duo, with Cindy on boogie and blues piano and Marian contributing soulful vocals and clarinet, expanded to a trio with the addition of drummer Anje Glindemann, and later became a quartet when multi-instrumentalist Kate Marshall joined the group.

Each member is a gifted musician and singer in her own right, but together they create a musical chemistry that is greater than the sum of its parts. Their rich combination of voices and instruments produces a sound more often associated with a much larger ensemble. Audiences can expect humour, passion, warmth and exuberance, all in service of songs that remain firmly at the heart of the performance.

Join the Raven Mavens Quartette for an evening celebrating original music, masterful musicianship and the release of a remarkable new collection of songs.

events.id: Kumutoto Kai me te Kōrero-Graze Wine Bar, 95 Upland Road-WOAP
events.name: Kumutoto Kai me te Kōrero
events.venue: Graze Wine Bar, 95 Upland Road
events.long_description:
Kumutoto Awa was one of the living streams of Pōneke long before the city buried it underground in 1866. This four-hour guided hīkoi traces its path from the Kelburn hills to the waterfront, connecting it through kai, kōrero, and the people who are working to restore the place of the awa in the city's future – The Kumutoto Restoration Project. You'll start with a light lunch and cocktail at Graze in Kelburn which will be a collaboration between Chef Max Gordy and the Kumutoto Community Orchard founder and avid forager Milan Magan. You will also meet your hosts Martin and Micheline who will regale you with stories about Wellington's lost streams. From there, the group walks to the only remaining stretch of the Kumutoto stream still visible above ground, where soup waits alongside more kōrero about the whakapapa of the awa. The route then follows the buried path of Kumutoto down the Terrace to Bert's Bar for a final cocktail created with a foraged ingredients from Kumutoto before finishing at the mouth of the awa on the waterfront. All food and drinks across the event are included in your ticket, with ingredients foraged from the Kumutoto Community Orchard and ngahere. Wear comfortable shoes and dress for the weather. The route covers approximately two kilometres and includes steps.
The ticket price includes an optional foraging workshop with Milan Magan. You'll spend an hour in the orchard and ngahere learning about what you'll be eating and drinking the following day. Saturday 1 & 29 August 9-10am.

events.long_description:

Standing show (Seating reserved for those who need it: ).

The wave doesn’t conform to the shape of the rock. It smashes it. The sea doesn’t pretend to be hospitable. It summons courage. And a shantyband never licks the captain's boot. They release another EP!

The best shanties invite us to open our hearts along with the bottle. To draw strength from camaraderie and drown our pettinesses. To seek the rough edge of the wave and savour the salt within. And so, the WSSS have issued a call to arms with their new collection: Never Mind the Rowlocks, Here’s the Wellington Sea Shanty Society.

Never fear if you find yourself adrift on a sea of AI slop, lapping at your hull, lulling you to sleep — Lake Davineer, Vorn dont Le Père Était Marin, Young Nic, Tomas el Largo, and Louis Quatorze are back again to fill your sails and slap the codfish slime clean off your cheeks.

Just when everyone is lamenting the empty galleys of the good ship Wellington, and those ol’ scurvy-mongers are promising renewed bounty if you would only tack five degrees to port or starboard come election time, these songs remind us the sea at least will sustain us, and there’s rum and (metaphorical) guns for them that wants to fight.

Lin Seal | Wellington Nautical History Monthly

⚓⚓⚓

The scuttlebutt is true...⛵

The most seaworthy sea shanty band in the South Pacific is releasing their long-awaited 4th collection of new and old maritime bangers:
'Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society'.

All aboard as we set sail for the salty horizon. Prepare to be battered once again by the 4-sailor squall of pure shanty.


⚓⚓⚓

WELLINGTON SEA SHANTY SOCIETY

Aotearoa New Zealand's Most 'Sea Worthy' Shanty Group™ have been belting out traditional and original sea songs from Aotearoa, France, Spain, the UK and more, since time immemorial (2012).
The W.S.S.S have toured Aotearoa and France multiple times and are known for their rowdy and participatory live shows. They've performed at Paimpol (one of the world's largest shanty festivals), Splore, Albany Folk Festival (Aus), Quebec Sea Shanty Festival (Canada) and a shipload of other festivals in NZ, France & Canada.

They will be playing new classics from their forthcoming EP 'Never Mind the Rowlocks' as well as your foamy favourites from the 'Sea Shanties of the 70s, 80s, & Today!' EP and their 'Now That's What I Call Sea Shanties' series.

events.long_description:
The WBS presents: The Raven Mavens Quartette CD launch concert
The Raven Mavens Quartette return to the Wellington Bluegrass Society on 1 August 2026 for the launch of their eagerly anticipated new CD.

Since releasing their previous album of original songs in 2020 — also celebrated at the Bluegrass Society — the band have continued to delight audiences throughout Wellington, the Wairarapa and the Kāpiti Coast with their distinctive blend of blues, roots, folk and swing influences.

The Raven Mavens have become renowned for their catchy, blues-infused original songs, written primarily by band leader Cindy Muggeridge. Drawing on her deep roots in blues piano, as well as Latin rhythms and rock ’n’ roll grooves, Cindy's latest collection tells stories of life, love and loss, alongside wry social and political observations. In both performance and recording, she is joined by the exceptional talents of Kate Marshall on vocals, violin, accordion and flute; Marian Carter on vocals, saxophone, clarinet and recorder; and Anje Glindemann on vocals, drums and percussion.

The band are also excited to feature two original compositions by Kate Marshall on this new recording, with Kate taking the lead on piano, supported by the other Mavens.

A unique all-female ensemble, the Raven Mavens Quartette gives every member the opportunity to shine as both instrumentalist and vocalist. What began in 2011 as a duo, with Cindy on boogie and blues piano and Marian contributing soulful vocals and clarinet, expanded to a trio with the addition of drummer Anje Glindemann, and later became a quartet when multi-instrumentalist Kate Marshall joined the group.

Each member is a gifted musician and singer in her own right, but together they create a musical chemistry that is greater than the sum of its parts. Their rich combination of voices and instruments produces a sound more often associated with a much larger ensemble. Audiences can expect humour, passion, warmth and exuberance, all in service of songs that remain firmly at the heart of the performance.

Join the Raven Mavens Quartette for an evening celebrating original music, masterful musicianship and the release of a remarkable new collection of songs.

events.name: Produce like a Pro - A Workshop for Theatre and Comedy Makers
events.venue: Toi Aro Arts Centre, 3-6 Market Lane, Wellington
events.long_description:
This full day workshop deep dives into the fundamentals of producing, marketing and touring theatre and comedy in Aotearoa New Zealand. Led by two of the country’s leading independent producers, we’ll take you through a series of practical tips and resources to help you make more professional work, and less stressful production processes.

Whether you have a fresh idea for next year's fringe circuit, or an existing show planning its next steps- we'll cover everything you need to know with plenty of time for tailored feedback and advice.

The Workshop will cover:
- Key producing decisions and creating the right timelines and production plans for your work.
- Assembling the right team, contracting and looking after your people.
- How to manage budgets and expenses without losing your mind.
- An overview of the funding and partnerships landscape in Aotearoa, and how to get the most out of your time spent in this area.
- Identifying your target demographic and the best ways to get in front of them.
- A general guide to marketing and publicity in 2026.
- Touring in New Zealand and beyond.

The workshop can be attended in-person or online. Online attendees will be sent a link in advance of the workshop day (keep an eye on your spam folder, just in case).

Pricing is Pay What You Can from $50, but we reckon it's worth may more than that. Paying what you can afford, helps to make it more affordable for those for whom it's a stretch. If payment is a barrier, we're open to service exchange and other koha options so feel free to get in touch.

ABOUT THE FACILITATORS

NINA HOGG
Nina is a comedian, tour manager, performer and producer based in Pōneke. She has worked as a full-time producer and tour manager for The Theatre in Health Education Trust (Sexwise), The National Theatre for Children and Young & Hungry, managing and/or producing eight full scale national theatre tours.

She also regularly tours her own works around NZ and Australia with her queer comedy duo Ginge & Minge and Mon Platon’s touring production Coro- which toured to the Edinburgh Fringe in 2025. Her accolades include “Best Show” at the Wellington Comedy Awards 2025, “Comic Originality” at NZ Comedy Guild Awards 2025, and “Best Hustler” at NZ International Comedy Festival 2026.

Nina also leads marketing and publicity for PopRox Improv, Mon Platon Productions, Ginge & Minge and currently manages social media for Wellington icon Shut Up and Dance.

AUSTIN HARRISON
Austin is one of Aotearoa's most prolific performers and producers, having worked on over 800 live events. He's won a Wellington Theatre Award, “Favourite Comedian” at Dunedin Fringe 2026, and “Best Newcomer” at NZ International Comedy Festival 2026.

Austin is the Artistic Director of the New Zealand Improv Festival, and lead producer of Mon Platon Productions and Ace-ssential Workers (an independent company telling Aspec/asexual/aromantic stories on stage). He’s toured work from Gore to Whangārei, to the Melbourne International Comedy Festival, Adelaide Fringe and the Edinburgh Fringe.

events.venue: Ngā Pou Ruahine, Level 2, Te Matapihi, 65 Victoria Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
The Creation Voyages, from New Zealand Poet Laureate Robert Sullivan’s award-winning children’s book Weaving Earth & Sky is an exciting new performance from the New Zealand String Quartet – Te Rōpū Tūrū o Aotearoa. Through music and storytelling, with imagery by Gavin Bishop, the NZSQ vividly reimagines Aotearoa’s creation myths in an engaging, whānau-friendly performance.

Across 45 minutes, string quartet will meet live storytelling. NZSQ violinist Peter will narrate Ranginui and Papatuānuku’s embrace, their separation and the rise of the Atua, while accompanied by live sound effects and music played by the NZSQ on their unique instruments. Including, Pokarekare Ana, excerpts from Vivaldi’s Four Seasons and Holst’s Planets Suite.

See you at Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui Library for a voyage back to creation!

events.id: Resonance Tour: LGBTQIA Rainbow Walk Tour through Wellington-Thistle Hall, 293 Cuba St, Te Aro, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Resonance Tour: LGBTQIA Rainbow Walk Tour through Wellington
events.venue: Thistle Hall, 293 Cuba St, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join us on this free 90-minute walk tour of inner city Wellington looking at sites of significance to Wellington’s LGBTI rainbow communities.

While many of the buildings still exist, the inhabitants and their activities have changed dramatically over time. This walk tour gives you an opportunity to be transported back to earlier days to hear stories of courage and resilience while standing in the locations where it all happened.

The tour recounts stories drawn from our other tours - making it a great introduction to our larger series of monthly LGBTI rainbow walk tours in Wellington. It’s mainly on flat accessible footpaths and covers Cuba Street, Vivian Street and Willis Street. We’ll visit Carmen’s curio shop, stop by the infamous Club Exotic, talk about a poetic same-sex romance, visit the site of the discreet Dorian Society and more.


Time/Date: 1pm on Sunday 2 August 2026
Starts: Outside Thistle Hall, 293 Cuba Street
Ends: corner Manners/Victoria Streets
Duration: 90 minutes
Cost / Bookings: the tour is free but you do need to register

PLEASE REGISTER AT https://walktours.nz/book/
(if there are no registrations the tour won't go ahead)

Step aboard for an elegant afternoon unlike any other, where heritage rail travel meets refined indulgence.

Introducing Steam Incorporated’s Signature High Tea Experience — an exclusive journey designed for those who appreciate the finer things. Departing from Paraparaumu and Waikanae, this carefully curated steam excursion offers a relaxed and luxurious escape, all within the space of a single afternoon.

Travel in style behind our beautifully restored steam locomotive, Ab 608 Passchendaele — a remarkable 111-year-old engine that brings history to life. The gentle rhythm of steam and the nostalgia of classic rail travel set the tone for an experience that is as timeless as it is memorable.

With limited numbers onboard, this is a more intimate journey — unhurried, comfortable, and distinctly premium.

Our destination is the picturesque Tatum, where you’ll be welcomed for a classic High Tea in a tranquil countryside setting. Indulge in a selection of finely prepared sweet and savoury treats, accompanied by freshly brewed tea and coffee — the perfect complement to a leisurely afternoon.

This experience has been thoughtfully designed as a shorter, refined outing — ideal for those seeking something special without committing to a full day. Whether you're celebrating an occasion, catching up with friends, or simply treating yourself, the Tatum High Tea offers a memorable blend of heritage, hospitality, and indulgence.

Experience Highlights

Steam-hauled return journey from Paraparaumu & Waikanae to Tatum in the heart of the Horowhenua
Steam hauled by Ab 608 ‘Passchendaele’, a 111-year-old heritage steam locomotive
Exclusive experience with a relaxed, premium atmosphere
Classic High Tea at Tatum, featuring a curated selection of treats
A short-format afternoon escape, perfect for a refined day out

Fares
$149 per person — includes return steam train travel and High Tea experience at Tatum, boarding at either Paraparaumu or Waikanae.

Select your Departure date for Winter 2026:

Sunday 2nd August
Sunday 9th August
Sunday 16th August

Seats are strictly limited to preserve the intimate nature of this experience, and demand is expected to be high. Secure your place today and treat yourself to a truly unique afternoon of steam, scenery, and indulgence.

Limited Mobility Disclaimer
The primary boarding and disembarking point at Tatum, does NOT have a platform. You will have to board from ground level (3-4 steps). Due to the age, design and nature of our heritage carriages, these are not suitable for passengers with limited mobility.

If you have any concerns, please contact us on 0800 783 264 to discuss options with our bookings team!

events.id: Aroha String Quartet-St Andrews on the Terrace, 30 The Terrace, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Aroha String Quartet
events.venue: St Andrews on the Terrace, 30 The Terrace, Wellington
events.long_description:
Founded in 2004, this well-known versatile Wellington-based quartet is Haihong Liu - violin, Konstanze Artmann - violin, Eli Vincent - viola, and Robert Ibell – cello.

Aroha Quartet presents a programme titled “Heart” of heartwarming music from the heart of the chamber music repertoire. It begins with a sparkling piece by the father of the string quartet, Josef Haydn, followed by the Ross Carey’s lovely Toccatina.

American composer Samuel Barber wrote to a friend in 1936 “I have just finished the slow movement of my quartet today (and) its a knockout”. Like a huge inbreath and outbreath, this amazing piece (often performed by string orchestra as the Barber Adagio) is flanked by two wonderful outer movements.

Beethoven’s glorious String Quartet No 10 covers the range of human moods from tranquil calm, to restlessness, heartfelt outbursts and resolute determination. Its nickname, ‘Harp’, comes from the striking pizzicato section in the first movement.

Joseph Haydn, String Quartet in E-flat Op 64 No 6
Samuel Barber, String Quartet in B min Op 11
Ross Carey, Toccatina
Ludwig van Beethoven, String Quartet No 10 in E-flat Op 74 ‘Harp’

events.id: Unwrapping Beethoven with the Elouan Quartet-Martinborough Town Hall, 8 Texas Street, Martinborough-Event Finder
events.name: Unwrapping Beethoven with the Elouan Quartet
events.venue: Martinborough Town Hall, 8 Texas Street, Martinborough
events.long_description:
Unwrapping Beethoven is an intimate musical experience that invites audiences inside the world of
Beethoven’s string quartets. Intertwining performance with conversation, the Elouan Quartet
explores this extraordinary genre - from its structural brilliance to its emotional depth through a
series of musical examples, reflections, and insights from the players themselves.

Rather than a traditional concert, this event weaves together discussion and live performance to
illuminate Beethoven’s compositional voice, the evolution of the quartet, and the interpretive
decisions that bring this music to life.

Along the way, audiences will encounter stories, ideas, and moments of discovery that
deepen their connection to the music and offer a fresh perspective on these remarkable works.

The Elouan Quartet, formed in 2025, comprises New Zealand Symphony Orchestra players with a
special love of chamber music and performing in informal and intimate settings.

Violinist Jessica Oddie studied at the Juilliard School, Yale University, and the Yale School of Music.
She returned to New Zealand in 2020 when she was engaged as Guest Assistant Concertmaster of
the NZSO. She was delighted to join the orchestra as Assistant Principal Second in 2022. Jessica has
recorded albums of chamber music for the Naxos and Tactus recording labels, including the
premiere recording of twentieth-century Italian composer Gino Gorini’s chamber works. She has
performed in festivals including the Venice Biennale, the Norfolk Chamber Music Festival in the US,
the Toronto Summer Music Festival, and in Fontainebleau, France.

Originally from Paeroa, Anna van der Zee is a member of the first violin section of the NZSO. Trained
in Wellington, Germany and USA, Anna co-founded the Tasman String Quartet. The quartet ventured
to Boulder, Colorado for two years to study under the renowned Takacs Quartet. Alongside her work
with the NZSO, Anna runs Karori Classics - a series of monthly chamber music concerts supporting
local charities. She plays regularly in chamber music groups with her NZSO colleagues and is a core
member of contemporary ensemble Stroma.

New Zealand violist Alexander McFarlane is Associate Principal Viola with the New Zealand
Symphony Orchestra. Equally at home in a solo, chamber or orchestral idiom, he has performed
internationally in venues including the Wigmore Hall, the Barbican Hall, the Musikverein in Vienna
and the Concertgebouw in Amsterdam. As a chamber musician, he has collaborated with artists
including Steven Isserlis, Janine Jansen, and the Doric String Quartet, and performed at festivals
including IMS Prussia Cove, Yellow Barn, ‘At the World’s Edge’ Festival, the ‘Mendelssohn on Mull’
Festival, and ‘Musique à Marsac’ in France.

London-born cellist Ken Ichinose was appointed Associate Principal Cello of the New Zealand
Symphony Orchestra in 2014. He is the cellist of the Ghost Piano Trio and also performs regularly
with contemporary music group Stroma. Ken returns to London regularly to perform chamber music
with his siblings and work with orchestras such as the London Symphony and Royal Philharmonic.
Before moving to New Zealand, Ken was a founding member of the Galitzin Quartet with whom he
performed for ten years,

events.long_description:
Produce like a Pro | A Workshop for Theatre and Comedy Makers
This full day workshop deep dives into the fundamentals of producing, marketing and touring theatre and comedy in Aotearoa New Zealand. Led by two of the country’s leading independent producers, we’ll take you through a series of practical tips and resources to help you make more professional work, and less stressful production processes.

Whether you have a fresh idea for next year's fringe circuit, or an existing show planning its next steps- we'll cover everything you need to know with plenty of time for tailored feedback and advice.

The Workshop will cover:
- Key producing decisions and creating the right timelines and production plans for your work.
- Assembling the right team, contracting and looking after your people.
- How to manage budgets and expenses without losing your mind.
- An overview of the funding and partnerships landscape in Aotearoa, and how to get the most out of your time spent in this area.
- Identifying your target demographic and the best ways to get in front of them.
- A general guide to marketing and publicity in 2026.
- Touring in New Zealand and beyond.

The workshop can be attended in-person or online. Online attendees will be sent a link in advance of the workshop day (keep an eye on your spam folder, just in case).

Pricing is Pay What You Can from $50, but we reckon it's worth may more than that. Paying what you can afford, helps to make it more affordable for those for whom it's a stretch. If money is a barrier, we're open to service exchange and other koha options so feel free to get in touch.

ABOUT THE FACILITATORS

NINA HOGG
Nina is a comedian, tour manager, performer and producer based in Pōneke. She has worked as a full-time producer and tour manager for The Theatre in Health Education Trust (Sexwise), The National Theatre for Children and Young & Hungry, managing and/or producing eight full scale national theatre tours.

She also regularly tours her own works around NZ and Australia with her queer comedy duo Ginge & Minge and Mon Platon’s touring production Coro- which toured to the Edinburgh Fringe in 2025. Her accolades include “Best Show” at the Wellington Comedy Awards 2025, “Comic Originality” at NZ Comedy Guild Awards 2025, and “Best Hustler” at NZ International Comedy Festival 2026.

Nina also leads marketing and publicity for PopRox Improv, Mon Platon Productions, Ginge & Minge and currently manages social media for Wellington icon Shut Up and Dance.

AUSTIN HARRISON
Austin is one of Aotearoa's most prolific performers and producers, having worked on over 800 live events. He's won a Wellington Theatre Award, “Favourite Comedian” at Dunedin Fringe 2026, and “Best Newcomer” at NZ International Comedy Festival 2026.

Austin is the Artistic Director of the New Zealand Improv Festival, and lead producer of Mon Platon Productions and Ace-ssential Workers (an independent company telling Aspec/asexual/aromantic stories on stage). He’s toured work from Gore to Whangārei, to the Melbourne International Comedy Festival, Adelaide Fringe and the Edinburgh Fringe.

Edible Weeds Foraging Workshop ~ 2nd August 2026
Sunday 2nd August. Join expert forager Felicity Joy of Wild Botanica for a comprehensive Wild Edible Weeds Foraging Workshop in the beautiful community gardens of Mount Victoria, Wellington.

This inspiring experience will open your eyes to the abundance of edible wild plants growing right under your nose.

We’ll unlock the secrets of foraging, connecting with the land, and turning humble "weeds" into delicious, nourishing food. You’ll gain confidence in identifying common edible plants, learn their botanical names, and understand their medicinal and nutritional benefits. We’ll also explore ethical foraging practices, how to spot toxic lookalikes, and share simple, practical ways to incorporate wild foods into your daily meals.

This isn’t just about food: it’s about sustainability, resilience, and reconnecting with the environment in a meaningful way. You'll leave with a deeper appreciation for the land, new skills to support local food security, and the knowledge to make your own simple meals from wild ingredients.

Class sizes are limited, so book early to secure your spot.

The 2026 NPC season starts here!
Don’t miss the Wellington Lions’ opening clash of the season against our rivals and neighbours, the Hawke's Bay Magpies. Join us for what promises to be a thrilling start to the campaign.

It's Old Timers Day — an opportunity to celebrate the legends who have shaped our game, left a lasting legacy, and made a profound impact on rugby and our wider community.

To honour our Old Timers, we encourage fans to wear their retro or vintage jerseys — whether club, school, or representative and proudly #WearYourHistory.

We will also commemorate the remarkable service of Major William James Hardham VC — Wellington Rugby representative, member of the original Wellington team that won the Ranfurly Shield in 1904, and Victoria Cross recipient. His courage and sacrifice are enduring part of the region's rugby heritage.

We will also recognise the links between Wellington and Hawke's Bay and the Battle of Chunuk Bair, fought on 8 August 1915, one of New Zealand's most significant actions at Gallipoli, where soldiers and former players from both provinces played a pivotal role in one of the defining battles of the campaign.
Be there as we kick off the 2026 campaign and celebrate the people, stories, and traditions that make our game so special.

Pre Game Activations include: William James Hardham, VC Frame Presentation

events.long_description:
Nick Herbison Album Release Tour - Wellington 2nd August w/ Joe Cole
Herbison offers a solo performance in Wellington at Newtowns finest Moon Bar, supported by folk artist Joe Cole. The solo tour marks the release of his self produced album 'Seek and Don't Forget'.



Nick Herbison is a folk-rock artist from Hawke’s Bay, Aotearoa, whose music reflects his philosophical outlook and the internal weather systems he navigates. With acoustic guitar at the core of his songwriting, Herbison crafts introspective, life-affirming songs that explore courage, self-worth, and the ongoing journey toward inner peace. His style has been largely influenced by folk, blues, rock, roots and RnB.



Most recently Nick embarked on a national tour of Aotearoa supporting Melbourne blues troubadour Shaun Kirk during September 2025. Since then Herbison has played as a solo performer at festivals in Auckland and Rotorua (Morph Fest and Sauna Fest).



Herbison's solo performances often demonstrate his sensational ability on the acoustic guitar and his lower toned, smooth vocals. The use of a loop pedal and foot percussion has been a recent addition to his solo set. With influences such as Jack Johnson, Ben Howard, Matt Corby, Ben Harper and Passenger, to name a few, Nick will often include a cover or two during his sets.



'Seek and Don't Forget' is the album that he will be celebrating on his handful of shows around the North Island throughout July and August. Wellington singer songwriter; Joe Cole will support the show with his grandiose style of folk music.

events.name: Next Gen Cook Off
events.venue: LTD., Level 1, 60 Dixon Street
events.long_description:
The first four Mondays in August, an up-and-coming chef takes over the Everybody Eats kitchen at LTD and delivers a three-course dinner built from rescued food, cooking it their way and style. Walk in, take a seat, and let the Everybody Eats volunteers whānau take care of the rest. No bookings. Pay what you can. 
Sixth year running, and the model stays simple: good food, good company, and a room full of people making a difference one plate at a time. Every course uses rescued ingredients, because eating is fundamental and everyone deserves access to something . 

3 August — Oscar Little, Hummingbird
Oscar Little started his culinary career five years ago as a commis chef at Shed 5 and The Crabshack, where he learned what it means to commit to a team. He’s since worked his way up to chef de partie at Hummingbird. Along the way he’s volunteered with Everybody Eats, and it’s that spirit of giving back to the community that drives him to compete this year.

10 August — Brayden Puketapu, Koji
At 22, Brayden Puketapu is already developing a cooking voice that’s distinctly his own. Working at Koji, he’s drawn to the creative challenge of transforming overlooked ingredients and putting his own stamp on both classic and contemporary dishes. His heritage is central to that identity, grounding his food in something personal while keeping it fresh and inventive.

17 August — Eugenous Evan, Rosella
Indonesian-born Eugenous Evan came to Wellington five years ago and hasn’t looked back. After stints at Shepherd, Hillside & Daisy’s, and Supra, he’s now chef de partie at Rosella, where he’s been for just over a year. For Eugenous, cooking is an act of care: a way to share something of himself with every person who sits down to eat.

24 August — Aryan Dhankhhar, Mosaic Venues (Mr Go's, Kisa, Ombra, Parla)
Aryan Dhankhhar’s love of food started young, holding weekend cooking competitions with his sister and himself in their family kitchen in Haryana, India, with their mother as judge. Since then he’s built a career spanning hotels, restaurants, and catering, working across techniques from sous vide to traditional barbecue. A highlight: leading the team at Wilson Barbecue during Wellington On a Plate 2024, where they set a world record selling over 6,000 burgers in a single day. Now at Mr Go’s, he brings that same drive and precision to every plate.

Next Gen Cook Off is proudly supported by The Gas Hub.

events.id: Once Upon a Time in Wellington-Supra, Level 1, 31 Dixon Street-WOAP
events.name: Once Upon a Time in Wellington
events.venue: Supra, Level 1, 31 Dixon Street
events.long_description:
We are hosting some very special guest chefs over a 2 week period, with each chef joining us for a 2 night collaboration. Their identities won't be reveiled until the day before via Instagram. Speculate, believe the rumours, start the rumours for all we care! Three local legends, one from outside Wellington, and a roster that reads like the highlight reel of modern cooking in this country. It will be a small a la carte format during our usual trading hours.  Walk ins are encouraged but bookings for groups of 4 or more it is highly recommended. The menus will be small and à la carte throughout. 
Guest #1 (4-5 Aug) The Taipan
Our first guest is a previous collaborator, you know him, you love him, we love him. If you've eaten his food before, you know subtlety isn't on the menu. Expect bold and aggressive flavours, and probably some offal. 
Guest #2 (7-8 Aug) The Kodiak Bear
Lover of restaurants and a wizard with words on paper. We are very excited to introduce this guy and give him a creative platform to show Wellington something special from a unique perspective. 
Guest #3 (12-13) The Suzumebachi
Joining us from the Hawkes Bay, This man brings a tempered approach to cooking from his time cooking in Japan. Now an established award winning chef in New Zealand, and someone we consider at the pinnacle of modern cookery in this country. Expect Japanese flavours and techniques utilizing the some of the best produce NZ has to offer.
Guest #4 (14-15) The Bighorn Ram
With many curls in his horns, this guy has been pivotal and arguably one of the most important chefs Wellington has ever known, setting the stage for many of us who followed. An award winning chef who pioneered modern cuisine in this City, you wont want to miss this. Expect a measured and wise approach to fun flavour combinations with precision.

events.id: Karori Friendship Club-St Ninian's Uniting Church, 208 Karori Road, Karori, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Karori Friendship Club
events.venue: St Ninian's Uniting Church, 208 Karori Road, Karori, Wellington
events.long_description:
Tuesday mornings just got better!

If you enjoy a good chat, a decent cuppa, and the kind of laughter that makes you forget the time, the Karori Friendship Club is for you. We meet at St Ninian’s, 208 Karori Road, Karori, from 10 am to 12 pm, and for a koha you’ll be treated to morning tea and genuinely friendly company.

It’s a wonderful fit for seniors, people new to Karori, or any ESOL learners who would like a relaxed place to practise their language skills and settle into the community. Some weeks, there’s a board game or a puzzle on the go. Most weeks, it’s simply good conversation, shared stories, and the kind of connection that brightens your whole day.

No pressure, no fuss — just a warm welcome and a seat at the table. Come and see what makes this little Tuesday gathering such a special part of our community. You don't have to live in Karori to come; we have members from all over Wellington.

Ph: 476 7137 for more info or check out our website.

events.id: Book Group: The Last of the Mohicans by James Fenimore Cooper-The Library, 1/53 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Book Group: The Last of the Mohicans by James Fenimore Cooper
events.venue: The Library, 1/53 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Celebrating its 200th anniversary this year, James Fenimore Cooper's 1826 novel is an unforgettable portrait of fierce individualism and moral courage, set against the bloody French and Indian War. The events of the book take place in 1757 in a very early America - in what we now know as Upstate New York - and only two decades before the Revolutionary War. The Last of the Mohicans has been described as a trailblazing text that helped establish early Americans’ shared sense of identity and purpose.

James Fenimore Cooper was one of the first and greatest literary giants of the New World, read in America and Europe, and stands alongside Nathaniel Hawthorne and Edgar Allan Poe as one of the forefathers of American literature.

Do you keep meaning to read more of the great classics? At Wellington Classic Literature Club, we read works that have stood the test of time, whether they were written in 1780, 1880 or even 1980. We meet on the first Tuesday of the month.

RSVP
Bookings essential. Get your free ticket by clicking 'Register' above. Limited places.

If you've signed up, but things change and you're not going to be able to make it along, please email classiclitwgtn@gmail.com as we may be able to make more spaces available for others.

VENUE
We meet in the ‘Games Room’, The Library bar's private area overlooking Courtenay Place. After you enter the bar, head to your right (up the step) and through a smaller space with booths to the large carpeted space beyond (behind the big wooden sliding door).

ABOUT US
Wellington Classic Literature Club has been running for more than a decade - since the start of 2013 - and we have a great bunch of regulars as well as readers who join us for particular books or simply when it suits.

events.name: Waenga
events.venue: Wairarapa Events Centre, Holloway St, Carterton
events.long_description:
Created by Hariata & Tamati Moriarty and directed by Jim Moriarty, 'Waenga' centres on a young wahine Māori who is arrested and finds herself in a police holding cell. Alongside her journey is Peyton, who is coming to understand what a Tangata Tiriti partnership is and Grayson, a young Māori lawyer navigating his role in the system.

Performed by an ensemble cast, including well known rangatahi Hariata and Tamati Moriarty, the play is presented in Te Rākau’s unique Theatre Marae framework, creating space for collective reflection and shared experience.

Te Rākau is the longest running Māori theatre company in Aotearoa founded in 1989.

Recommended age 12+ contains swearing and depicts some violence. Children under 12 can accompany for free with a paying adult.

events.venue: Tāne Whakapiripiri - Ōtari Visitors Centre, 150 Wilton Road, Wilton, Wellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join Julia Kasper, Lead Curator Invertebrates at Te Papa, as she talks about Subterranean ecosystems - some of the least explored habitats on Earth. Globally, scientific knowledge of cave and groundwater invertebrates remains fragmentary, with most regions having only sporadic surveys or taxonomic treatments. Many cave systems host highly specialised faunal assemblages - troglobionts, stygofauna, and other obligate subterranean species - that often display extreme adaptations such as reduced pigmentation, elongated appendages, or complete loss of eyes.

The Subterranean Critters: Understanding cave Biodiversity in Aotearoa (SCUBA) project brings together the expertise of a wide range of researchers and cavers to better understand the biodiversity and ecology of faunal communities in caves in Aotearoa New Zealand. Novel sample collection, combined with reviews of the literature and presently available natural history collection holdings, will enable species discovery and improved understanding of the distribution and conservation status of cave taxa, as well as the abiotic factors that influence their distribution, ecology, and abundance.

Located in Tāne Whakapiripiri, Ōtari Visitor Centre. Gold coin donation. No need to book, just turn up!

This seminar is part of the Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush Trust’s annual seminar series. This year, they are on the first Tuesday of the month, March – November, to celebrate 100 years of Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush.

Ōtari 100: Celebrating 100 years of native plants, conservation, and community. 1926-2026.

events.venue: Noble Rot Wine Bar, 6 Swan Lane
events.long_description:
You're invited to an evening shaped by ceremony, tradition, and a touch of intrigue. Inspired by the wines that grace state banquets and formal royal occasions of the British Royal Family, this intimate gathering draws from producers associated with the Royal Household. Bottles will be chosen for their pedigree, poise, and quiet authority. For one exclusive evening, Noble Rot’s cellar reflects the mysterious spirit of Buckingham Palace’s own, offering a rare opportunity to taste wines in the style of those served to the Monarchy and its most esteemed guests.
You’ll be welcomed with a glass of Champagne from one of the Family’s favoured Royal Warrant houses, before indulging in a luxurious 5-course degustation with paired wines fit for a King and Queen. As each special bottle is revealed, the expert sommelier team will guide each pour, sharing the provenance of the producers and the historic royal occasions where these styles have been served.
