events.venue: The Treasury, level 3, 1 The Terrace, WellingtonWellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview
Governing in 2026: populism, geopolitics, and AI in a tumultuous world
Join us for the next lecture in our current seminar series
Populism, geopolitics, and AI are transforming government across the world. Civil servants are having to update, re-envision, and rewire their work using new kinds of communication, technology, and policy skills.
This talk, by Oxford University’s Professor Ngaire Woods, will draw lessons from the experiences of other governments in setting out elements of a roadmap for a high-performing civil service.
About this event
This will be a hybrid event. Please use this site to register if you plan to attend it in person.
If you would like to attend it virtually, please use THIS LINK to register.
About the presenter
Professor Ngaire Woods is the founding Dean of the Blavatnik School of Government and Professor of Global Economic Governance at Oxford University. She is a leading scholar of global economic governance, international institutions, globalisation, and development.
She has held senior advisory and governance roles across public policy, education, international development, and business, including with the World Economic Forum and G20-related panels.
Ngaire was educated at the University of Auckland and Balliol College, Oxford, where she studied as a New Zealand Rhodes Scholar. She is also a Fellow of the Academy of Social Sciences, an International Honorary Member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, and an Honorary Fellow of the Royal Academy of Arts.
About this seminar series
New ideas, robust evidence, and insights from leading thinkers are crucial to strengthening the Treasury’s economic analysis and policy advice. Our new guest lecture theme — Navigating Global Shifts: Resilience, Challenges and Opportunities for New Zealand — invites us to reflect on how Aotearoa New Zealand can navigate an increasingly complex and interconnected global environment.
This series explores the major global forces that shape our economic landscape, including evolving trade relationships, geopolitical developments, and the global movement of people, capital, and ideas. Through these discussions, we aim to deepen our understanding of how New Zealand can build economic resilience, respond effectively to uncertainty, and harness our regional and international partnerships to support economic performance, productivity, and our living standards.
Our speakers explore strategies for mitigating the impacts of global disruptions — from pandemics and climate‑related events to geopolitical tensions and supply‑chain shocks – while also examining potential opportunities presented by rapid technological shifts, digital economy, and global innovations, to name a few. The series considers the role of government in supporting economic transitions, strengthening national resilience, and ensuring that New Zealand remains well‑positioned to meet emerging global opportunities. By bringing together diverse perspectives, this series seeks to inspire new ways of thinking about New Zealand’s economic future and to support informed, forward‑looking policymaking.
Please note that the views, opinions, findings, and conclusions expressed in the Treasury Guest Lecture Series are those of the individual presenters. They do not necessarily reflect the views of the New Zealand Treasury or the New Zealand Government.
For updates and our latest research visit: www.treasury.govt.nz

events.long_description:
Created by Hariata & Tamati Moriarty and directed by Jim Moriarty, 'Waenga' centres on a young wahine Māori who is arrested and finds herself in a police holding cell. Alongside her journey is Peyton, who is coming to understand what a Tangata Tiriti partnership is and Grayson, a young Māori lawyer navigating his role in the system.

Performed by an ensemble cast, including well known rangatahi Hariata and Tamati Moriarty, the play is presented in Te Rākau’s unique Theatre Marae framework, creating space for collective reflection and shared experience.

Te Rākau is the longest running Māori theatre company in Aotearoa founded in 1989.

Recommended age 12+ contains swearing and depicts some violence. Children under 12 can accompany for free with a paying adult.

events.long_description:
Kathryn Berkett - WHAT’S GOING ON?!
This fundraiser is a little different... and I reckon it's one you won't want to miss!

As some of you know, our whānau is part of the Maidstone Intermediate AIMS Games Rippa Team this year. To help get our team to Tauranga, we're doing a bit of fundraising along the way. Rather than another sausage sizzle, we wanted to bring our community something a little different....an evening that not only supports our tamariki, but also gives you practical, valuable insights to take home and use in your own whānau.

We've been incredibly lucky to secure the amazing Kathryn Berkett to present one of her most popular talks:

🧠 What's Going On? Navigating the Adolescent Years

If you've ever looked at your pre-teen or teenager and thought...
🤯 "What the hecka is going on in that brain?!"

...this night is for you.

Kathryn is one of New Zealand's leading neuroscience educators and has an incredible way of making sense of what is happening in young people's brains. She'll unpack why our rangatahi think, feel and behave the way they do, while sharing practical tools and strategies that parents, caregivers, teachers, coaches and anyone working with young people can put into practice straight away.

(No promises they'll suddenly start washing the dishes... but you'll probably understand why they don't! 😅)

📅 Wednesday 5 August
🕡 6.30pm
📍 Maidstone Intermediate Hall
🎟️ $20 per ticket

Every dollar raised goes directly towards supporting the Maidstone Intermediate AIMS Games Rippa Team on their journey to Tauranga.

Kathryn's book, What's Going On in There? – The Neuroscience of the Adolescent Brain, will also be available for purchase on the night, with a portion of book sales being donated to the team.

If finding a babysitter is the only thing stopping you from coming, bring the kids along. We'll have the school library open with adult supervisors so they can hang out while you enjoy the session. We'd just ask that this option is only used if it's genuinely needed.

🎟️ Grab your tickets here:
👉 https://events.humanitix.com/what-s-going-on-navigating-the-adolescent-years

If you cant make it but know someone raising a tween or teenager (or about to!), please share this post. The more people we can get through the door, the more we support our team—and the more whānau in our community get to hear Kathryn's incredible insights.

Ngā mihi nui for your support!

Chow celebrates the most powerful recommendation of all: the one shared across a family table.

Jimmy Mahakit (Isaan, Thailand) and Kunpheng “Ricki” Zhu (Jiangsu, near Shanghai) have each spent a decade as Sous Chefs at Chow. For one night, they cook together, presenting dishes learned at home through observation, taste, and guidance at the stove. These are recipes passed down through families, remembered rather than written. This is word of mouth in its purest form.

Food  is made to be shared.  What begins as dinner evolves into a true Chow party, with matched cocktails flowing and a DJ building the energy.

Your ticket includes a shared dinner and matched cocktails. Additional drinks will be available for purchase.

events.name: Beyond Behaviour: Supporting Neurodiverse Young People
events.venue: 142 Saxton Road EastNelson, Nelson
events.long_description:
Overview








Unlock fresh insights, practical strategies, and a deeper understanding of neurodiversity through this thought-provoking training
Beyond Behaviour: Supporting Neurodiverse Young People
Unlock fresh insights, practical strategies, and a deeper understanding of neurodiversity through this engaging and thought-provoking learning experience. Brought to you by Nelson Tasman Youth Workers Collective, this workshop is for anyone who works with, supports, influences, or cares for young people. Whether you're a youth worker, social worker, teacher, mentor, coach, parent, caregiver, or community practitioner, you'll gain valuable tools to strengthen relationships, foster belonging, and better support neurodiverse rangatahi to thrive. If supporting young people is part of your world, this is a learning opportunity you won't want to miss.

This interactive workshop explores the intersection of neurodiversity, trauma-sensitive practice, and effective youth development. Participants will gain a deeper understanding of how trauma impacts the nervous system, and how power, privilege, communication styles, and adult behaviour can either support or hinder a young person’s sense of safety and connection. The workshop provides practical strategies for showing up as a safe, responsive adult, with a focus on both verbal and non-verbal communication.

The second part of the workshop focuses on practitioner wellbeing, helping participants recognise the importance of boundaries, sustainability, and preventing burnout in youth-focused roles. Through guided reflection, a meditative boundary-setting exercise, and an art-based activity, participants will develop a personalised visual resource that helps them identify and manage their own energy levels. Attendees will leave with greater self-awareness, practical tools, and a stronger foundation for supporting neurodiverse young people while sustaining their own wellbeing.

Made possible thanks to support from Department of Internal Affairs and Rata Foundation. Free for Nelson Tasman Youth Workers Collective Members.

Meet your kaiako;

Elana Cohen
Elana is a local occupational therapist with 22 years of experience working with neurodivergent people. Her practice is focused on empowering people to know themselves deeply and equipping the adults around young people to best set up supportive environments for youth to thrive. She is affirming of neurodivergent identities and trauma-sensitive. In addition to her Masters degree in occupational therapy, Elana has done advanced training in trauma, attachment, autism, and sensory processing and regularly presents on these topics.

Meagan Goodman
Meg (they/she) had the privilege of growing up on a small island in the Pacific Northwest of the US where they spent their growing up years playing in nature. Meg moved to Aotearoa in 2011 and deeply resonates with holistic approaches to wellbeing such as Te Whare Tapa Whā. Meg has worked in a diversity of roles within the public health sector, including establishing a youth mental health service across Te Tau Ihu (Top of the South Island). Meg is an active researcher and has focused on topics such as Rainbow youth experiences of accessing mental health services in the Nelson/Tasman region, and exploring the community construct of Queer Joy in an international mixed-method study. Meg is passionate about supporting people in the queer and neurodivergent communities and applies an intersectional lens to understanding experiences of distress and trauma.

events.id: Men's Circle: Breath, Presence & Connection-Bhakti Lounge WellingtonWellington, Wellington-Event Brite
events.name: Men's Circle: Breath, Presence & Connection
events.venue: Bhakti Lounge WellingtonWellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview



A supportive men’s circle for breathwork, honest conversation and meaningful connection in a space of trust and respect.
Men's Circle: Breath, Presence & Connection

An open space for men to come together, connect, and simply be. Whether you're moving through a challenge, seeking deeper connection, or wanting space to reflect, you are welcomed here.
Through breathwork, honest conversation, and shared presence, we create a space where men can show up authentically and be heard without judgment. There is no pressure to speak or be anything other than yourself. This circle is built on respect, trust, and genuine connection, offering a chance to slow down, listen, and remember that you don't have to do life alone.
Structure of the Circle:
Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.
Opening Breathwork: We begin with a guided breathwork practice to help everyone arrive, settle into the space, and connect with themselves and the group.
Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the person holding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.
Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is optional, and passing is always respected.
Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking, interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.
No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicited advice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.
Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.
Circle Agreements
Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fostering trust and brotherhood.
Focus on the Present: Share what's alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.
Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements to promote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."
No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicited advice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.
Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group but keep others' details private.

Please note our events now start at 6pm. Please try to be on time.

Optional Plant-Based Dinner
After the circle, stay for a wholesome plant-based dinner and dessert ($20 or $10 for students). Sharing a meal is a simple way to extend the sense of community and connection. This gathering is offered on a non-profit basis.

Meet Andre and Sri Jiva, your hosts

Andre has been immersed in men’s work since the age of 13, when he first experienced a rite of passage in Golden Bay. That formative experience sparked a lifelong connection to circle work, which he later deepened by returning as a mentor. Over the years, Andre has come to value the power of sitting in a circle, of men coming together in honesty, vulnerability, and presence to witness and support one another. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and pranayama (breathwork) facilitator, Andre also brings his passion for ecstatic dance, philosophy, and authentic connection into his offerings. He is deeply inspired by the question of what it means to be human, how we can more fully experience our aliveness, our depth, and reconnecting with the beauty of life together.
Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

events.name: Reiki Alchemy for Energy Retrieval
events.venue: Bhakti Lounge WellingtonWellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview
Reconnect with yourself through a gentle Reiki journey of healing, grounding and soulful restoration.
Reiki Alchemy for Energy Retrieval
Reiki Alchemy for Soul Retrieval is a gentle, grounded workshop for calling your energy back. The parts of you that went missing in survival mode, over-responsibility, heartbreak, burnout, people-pleasing, or prolonged stress.
In this space, we treat “soul fragments” as protective adaptations, not pathology. We move slowly, with consent, and with the nervous system in mind. You’ll be guided through a somatic + energetic journey to meet a part of you that’s ready to return, and you’ll receive hands-off Reiki to support safe integration.
No prior Reiki experience is required. Come exactly as you are.
What to expect:
Arrival + consent-based orientation (you’ll always have choice)
Breath arrival + gentle body scan to settle your system
Energetic hygiene + boundaries (cord awareness, closing practices, no fear-based language)
Guided “soul retrieval” visualisation (felt-sense + imagery) to meet a younger/exiled part
Hands-off group Reiki transmission for integration + wholeness
Quiet reflection + journaling (optional sharing)
Grounding tea + closing ritual
You might experience:
A deeper sense of calm and internal steadiness
Feeling more “in your body” and present
Less inner fragmentation (less push-pull, less self-abandonment)
Softer jaw/shoulders and more spacious breath
Clearer decisions and boundaries
More capacity to receive love, support, and rest
Emotional release that feels safe and integrated (not overwhelming)
Please bring:
Warm layers + socks (warmth supports safety)
Water bottle
Optional: blanket + eye mask/scarf
Journal + pen
Optional: a small meaningful object for the altar (token, crystal, photo)
Pre-class prep
Eat a light meal ~2 hours before.
Hydrate well throughout the day.
Limit caffeine 4 hours prior (if you’re sensitive).
Avoid alcohol/recreational substances for 24 hours.
Arrive 10 minutes early to settle.
If there’s anything you want me to know beforehand, email hi@lynofuro.co.nz.
Contraindications and safety:
Reiki is gentle and typically safe, but it does not replace medical or mental health care. This workshop is not recommended if you’re currently in acute crisis or unable to stay resourced in your body. You can opt out, pause, or modify at any time. Seated and side-lying options are welcome.
Aftercare:
After the session, your system may feel deeply rested or tender. For 24–48 hours, support integration by:
Drinking plenty of water
Eating nourishing grounding food
Taking a slow walk or gentle movement
Journaling any insights (even a few lines)
Keeping the evening spacious (less stimulation, more softness)
After the Reiki session, share in a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert, included in your ticket, a warm way to close the evening together.

Meet Lynn, your host:
Lynn Tiang is an Integrative Somatic Coach, breathwork facilitator, and Reiki practitioner. Lynn supports people who are high functioning on the outside but chronically tense, exhausted, or “stuck” on the inside. Often after seasons of corporate burnout, chronic stress, or prolonged over-responsibility.
Lynn’s work blends three pillars:
Somatic breathwork to help regulate the nervous system, soften protective patterns, and restore a steadier baseline
Reiki to support energetic clearing, heart coherence, deep rest, and integration (hands-off, consent-based)
Coaching to translate insight into grounded change — so what opens spiritually becomes real in relationships, boundaries, and daily choices
Lynn’s approach is trauma-aware, practical, and spiritually spacious. The focus isn’t on forcing catharsis, it’s on creating enough safety for your system to unwind, receive support, and remember your natural capacity for calm, clarity, and connection.
August 1:1 Integrative Somatic Coaching (2 spots only)
If you felt a “yes” in your body during this workshop, you’re invited to go deeper. I’m opening 2 private 1:1 Integrative Somatic Coaching spots in August for clients ready for nervous system regulation, somatic inquiry, breathwork, and grounded coaching support.
To enquire, email hi@lynofuro.co.nz with the subject line: August 1:1.

events.id: Raising Great Kids In An Overindulgent World-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Raising Great Kids In An Overindulgent World
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Parenting today delivers unprecedented challenges – are you wondering what went wrong and somehow ended up living with a child you don’t recognise as should be belonging to you? Get a new perspective, an easy-to-understand model to follow and tools to help you to raise likeable and respectful children in an age of over-indulgence.

This workshop will be a confronting one that will expose you to the risks that children face in this modern overindulgent world. Many have become used to being the constant centre of attention and are unable to delay gratification and aren’t competent in everyday skills.

They have few self-care skills and skills relating to others, can’t take personal responsibility and don’t know what is enough or what is “normal” for others – these children end up having a difficult time of it in life and you will too.

You’ll take away new insight and knowledge plus strategies that you can apply that very night to help your child to be a responsible, likeable and respectful person.

By the end of the session, you’ll be able to:
- Reflect on the current context parents are faced with today
- Find the relevant research
- Practise the parenting tools and discuss the model
- Know where to go to get support

Aimed at parents, grandparents and caregivers of children of all ages.

Presented by Madeleine Taylor.

events.venue: Moon, 167 Riddiford Street, Wellington
events.long_description:
Thursday Laughs brings some top quality Kiwi comedy to the heart of Newtown

Featuring - Tom Sainsbury ( as seen on Small Town Scandal)
Snapchat dude Tom Sainsbury has entertained Kiwi audiences online, on stage, and on screen. As seen on Small Town Scandal, Wellington Paranormal, 7Days, Snack Masters NZ and more.
Famous for taking the mickey out of politicians like Paula Bennett and Simon Bridges, as well as his parallel life as Gingerbread the cat, Tom will be plumbing the depths of our quirky culture.

With Alayne Dick
Alayne is a Te Whanganui-a-Tara based performer and writer. Alayne recently debuted her first stand-up comedy hour, Purple is the Gayest Colour, in the NZ International Comedy Festival. She has previously won an SYNZ Tour Ready Award at the NZ Fringe Festival, and was then nominated for best spoken word at the Sydney Fringe Festival.

And Newtown's own, Neil Thornton
Neil is a fierce and funny comedian who has performed all over the world: New York City comedy clubs, the Edinburgh Fringe, and once at a gay nudist resort. In New Zealand he's headlined at The Classic Comedy Club and performed in hamlets in the middle of nowhere South Island for confused sheep farmers. He appears occasionally on the "The Project" and was featured on the TV3 comedy special "After Hours.

events.id: Talk Truffle To Me-Intercontinental Hotel Wellington, 2 Grey Street-WOAP
events.name: Talk Truffle To Me
events.venue: Intercontinental Hotel Wellington, 2 Grey Street
events.long_description:
Executive Chef Carl Maunder has spent two decades with truffles: exploring, refining dishes that let them truly shine, building an entire culinary philosophy around one ingredient. 

Indulge in five courses built around Périgord and Bianchetto truffles at the height of their season. Hand-prepared scallops with truffle, beef fillet Rossini reimagined, house-made truffle brie. Every course carries the same special ingredient, yet every course reveals something different about this heady ingredient. Carl shares insights throughout the long lunch: why this preparation, why this wine, what makes a truffle matter enough to shape a chef's craft. You'll taste the earthy weight of it, catch the aroma before the plate lands, understand the precision behind each dish. Each course is paired with a beverage chosen to meet the truffle's character.

events.name: The Flipper
events.venue: LTD., Level 1, 60 Dixon Street
events.long_description:
Bright lights, laminated menus, and paper-lined trays. Nate Auld, head chef at Mr Go's, rewinds the clock at LTD. with a 1990s New Zealand–style fish and chip shop, seen through a knowing lens. It's nostalgic and a little tongue-in-cheek: a highbrow, lowbrow take built for people who grew up on battered everything. 
Book a table or walk in for a one-hour sitting between 5–10pm and order from a succinct menu that treats the classics with care, without taking them too seriously. Mussel fritters that actually crunch, battered or crumbed fish done properly, hot dogs in their finest fried form, pineapple fritters dusted in cinnamon sugar, not shit chips, plus proper seasonings with lemon and housemade sauce. Drinks are there to smash back: Spritzes, crisp whites, and Waikato from the chilli bin. Dishes and drinks range from $6–$16.

events.name: Beast Feast
events.venue: Volco - Egmont Street, 11 Egmont Street
events.long_description:
Offal has a reputation it doesn't deserve. At Volco, the kitchen eats it every day, rotated through the menu, balanced carefully, treated right. For this five course feast each course will feature secondary cuts from chicken, pig, and lamb. Expect fried chicken gizzard, beef fat salted caramel, and the kind of food that will have you questioning if these truly are "off cuts". 
This five-course tasting menu celebrates the cuts that are often talked about between chefs, the ones that butchers used to give away and are now being sought out by adventurous eaters. Alcoholic and non alcoholic drinks available for purchase on the night.

events.id: Midwinter Lunar New Year-Dragons Chinese Restaurant, 25 Tory Street-WOAP
events.name: Midwinter Lunar New Year
events.venue: Dragons Chinese Restaurant, 25 Tory Street
events.long_description:
Warm yourself in the heart of winter with a vibrant Lunar New Year feast. Let the Dragons team bring colour, flavour, and good fortune to a midwinter banquet designed to brighten the season. 

The table seats ten, your neighbours, your friends, strangers who are about to become familiar. Everyone stands to toss the Yu Sheng prosperity salad high into the air, and the chaos and laughter start. Then ten courses unfold: eight savoury dishes, each one imbued with symbolic meaning. Golden chicken for family unity. Whole fortune duck for fidelity. Crispy fish for abundance. Long-life noodles for longevity. It's food, luck, and togetherness served at once and you'll leave feeling blessed not only for the meal, but for this convivial and communal celebration. 

Your ticket includes the full ten-course shared banquet, a lion dance performance, and beverages throughout: welcoming tea, and three beers per guest.

events.long_description:
Coffee doesn't just have to be your morning flat white. KAIOTA's team is taking the ritual you know, that daily catch-up, that business meeting moment, and threading it through six courses where coffee flavours weave its way through the whole menu (but don't worry the caffeine stays low). You'll move through appetiser, entrée, main, palate cleanser, main and finally dessert, each one infused with the depth and subtlety of coffee in a different way. events.long_description:
Overview
Empower Her, female networking group that offers a welcoming and safe environment for women of all business backgrounds and experiences
NELSON - Moutere Hills Restaurant and Cellar Door
Monthly Topic: Magnetic Offer Creation
Hosted by: Lilly Minnich
Most women are not struggling to sell because their offer is wrong. events.id: Lost Wax in Three - Mitsuro Hikime Wax-Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki-Event Finder
events.name: Lost Wax in Three - Mitsuro Hikime Wax
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Discover the magic of Mitsuro Hikime — the beautiful Japanese technique that uses a special stretchy wax to create flowing, organic textures unlike anything else in jewellery-making.

Special Introductory Price!

Over three inspiring sessions, you’ll learn how to transform this fascinating material into stunning wearable pieces using the traditional lost wax casting process.

Mitsuro Hikime wax behaves very differently from standard jeweller’s wax. Warm and pliable, it can be stretched, twisted and pulled into delicate ribbons and natural textures that resemble flowing water, bark, roots or molten metal. The results are beautifully organic and wonderfully unpredictable, making every piece completely unique.

During the first two sessions, you’ll learn how to handle and shape this traditional Japanese wax, exploring different techniques to create rings, pendants or small sculptural objects full of movement and texture. Once your designs are complete, your waxes will be professionally cast in the metal of your choice.

There is then a one-week break before the final session to allow time for casting. In the third class, you’ll learn how to cut, file, sand and finish your cast pieces, transforming them into polished jewellery ready to wear, gift or treasure.

This course is suitable for complete beginners as well as more experienced makers wanting to experiment with this exciting and expressive technique. More advanced students are also welcome to use the sessions to develop independent projects in a supportive studio environment.

Included in the class fee are all Mitsuro Hikime waxes, consumables, sandpaper and courier costs.

Please note that casting and metal costs are not included, as these vary depending on the size of your piece and the metal selected. Small castings generally cost around $6.65–$12, with metal costs ranging approximately from $8–$30 depending on whether you choose red bronze, white bronze or silver.

This class is great for young folks aged around 12 and up. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

Join us for a powerful climate documentary screening and discover how we can protect our planet for future generations.

Join the Nelson Youth Council for an inspiring screening of A Life on Our Planet, presented by renowned broadcaster and natural historian Sir David Attenborough. Through breathtaking footage and powerful storytelling, the film explores the impact humans have had on Earth's ecosystems while offering hope and practical solutions for creating a more sustainable future.
Following the screening, attendees will have the opportunity to reflect on the film's key messages, discuss climate change with others, and explore simple actions that individuals and communities can take to make a positive difference.
Whether you're passionate about the environment or simply curious to learn more, everyone is welcome to attend this engaging and thought-provoking event.

Learn about the causes and impacts of climate change.
Discover practical ways to reduce your environmental footprint.
Be inspired by real-world solutions that are helping protect our planet.
Connect with others who care about creating a more sustainable future.
Who Can Attend?
This event is open to everyone—students, families, young people, adults, and members of the wider community. No prior knowledge of climate change is required.
Why This Matters
Climate change is one of the greatest challenges facing our generation. Understanding its causes and impacts is the first step toward creating meaningful change. By coming together to learn, discuss, and take action, we can all play a part in building a healthier, more sustainable future for people and the planet.

events.long_description:
FRENZ PRESENTS: Funk The Band, Yawner, Louie Flack.
Join us at San Fran on August 7th for a night filled with Funk, R&B, Jazz and House.

Funk The Band are a Wellington based group whose performance is guaranteed to entertain. They’re a fantastic force that blend a sweet mixture of classic soul funk and new-age jazz fusion. After their debut show in late 2025, they have been honing in their craft and getting ready to burn down the house.
Yawner is a R&B/Alternative project hailing from Wellington, New Zealand, led by Eden Brown (vocals) and Jamin Forlong (guitar). Formed in late 2024, the group has honed a sound that’s rooted in R&B, indie and jazz, and has now unveiled their work in two studio singles ‘Subside’ and 'Monkey Say' ahead of their forthcoming 2026 EP. Focusing on a heavy-hitting but soothing craft, they’ve organised an enormous live set which is not to be missed.
Growing up around a lot of music at both festivals and at home naturally Louie Flack has become infatuated with the idea of the floor, posturing himself as a slightly obsessive collector of music. As much as Louie’s collection centers a hefty amount of house music, he also plays soul, raregroove, jazz, disco, afrobeat, world and synth based music like post punk and Italo disco.

San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

Elvis has left the building and he's now in Titahi Bay, running a wedding chapel just for you. This is a truly unique experience where you can either live out your dream of getting married in a Las Vegas wedding chapel either just for fun, or legally. Arrive in a convertible Cadillac with bubbles in hand, step into a sanctuary where the King himself is celebrant, MC, photographer, and musical send-off rolled into one gloriously ridiculous evening.

After the ceremony (legally binding or symbolic, your choice), newlyweds are seated for a refined take on Elvis's signature sandwich: peanut butter mousse, candied bacon, and banana on brioche. Tater tots on the side. A slice of red velvet wedding cake to cut and share. Elvis karaoke and Elvistravaganza festivities carry the night forward, because what else would you do after getting married in a chapel run by the King?

Wedding packages vary; you can have an Elvis commitment ceremony just for fun, a vow renewal for a bit more seriousness (with a bit of help beforehand) but also
an Aoteroa New Zealand Legal wedding/union is available - ticketholders will be contacted to make confirm all the details are just right - and will get extra pre-time with the celebrant to get all the proper legal details done.

Wedding tickets are per couple and include: transport in the Cadillac, glass of travelling bubbles, wedding ceremony and certificate, breakfast, wedding cake, photographs, wedding album, sandwich, sides, cake slice, and one cocktail or non-alcoholic alternative. Additional alcohol is available for purchase.

events.name: Unwrapped
events.venue: Pātaka Art + Museum, 17 Parumoana Street, Porirua City Centre
events.long_description:
Unwrapped: Whittaker’s since 1896 invites Chocolate Lovers behind the scenes to discover how a local maker became a global name. Set within the wider history of cacao production, the exhibition traces Whittaker’s story—from J.H. Whittaker’s founding vision and the iconic products that followed through to the company’s ongoing commitment to quality, beans-to-bar manufacturing and ‘Good Honest Chocolate’ values.

The exhibition unwraps the story of New Zealand’s Most Trusted Brand and features objects to delight all the senses. Visitors will encounter nostalgic memorabilia and classic advertising, a scent station that reveals chocolate’s layered aromas and artworks made in collaboration with contemporary creatives.

2026 marks 130 years of Whittaker’s. What began as J.H. Whittaker’s small family business in 1896 has grown into a world-class chocolate manufacturer, still proudly family-owned four generations on and based in its original Porirua factory.

events.long_description:
Critically acclaimed stand-up comedian, actor, writer, and TV personality Alan Davies is heading to Wellington in 2026. His new show, ‘Think Ahead’, marks his first visit to Aotearoa in a decade. Like the latest instalment of his memoirs, White Male Stand-Up, the performance covers his extensive career, and the highs and lows he’s experienced. Alan says the show is about a late middle-aged stand-up comic. He thinks he’s Marty McFly, but he’s older than Doc Brown. He spends more time in the pharmacy than the gym and is subjected to relentless eye rolls from his kids. 
Davies is a staple of British television. He’s known for his performance as the eponymous hero in the long-running TV series Jonathan Creek, and as a permanent panellist on QI. His talk show, Alan Davies: As Yet Untitled, recently reached its seventh season. He is also one of the UK’s best-loved comedians.

events.long_description:
The delivery is razor sharp, and the comedy is not so much deadpan as bedpan. Nurse Georgie Carroll is back with a brand-new show. For Infectious, Georgie turns 20 years as a frontline surgical nurse into a stand-up that’s full of laughs, shocks, and heart. She is known as a natural storyteller whose style is authentic, fearless, and deeply human. It blends personal anecdotes, healthcare absurdities, and everyday family chaos into sharp, relatable observations. It’s big-hearted, no-nonsense, and riotous. 
Beyond the stage, Georgie Carroll is also an author whose writing captures the same warmth and humour that define her stand-up. Her stories celebrate resilience, laughter, and the humanity within healthcare, inspiring audiences across professions.

events.name: Madeira My Dear
events.venue: Noble Rot Wine Bar, 6 Swan Lane
events.long_description:
Madeira has been too often overlooked. It sits in grandmother's cabinet waiting for cooking or forgotten entirely. But Madeira is built to last, it's a quietly complex wine that deserves discovery. Noble Rot will spend an afternoon proving it to you.
The afternoon begins with a welcome cocktail before settling into a three-course long lunch served sharing style at the table, in the traditional Mediterranean spirit. Generous plates are designed to encourage conversation and a slower pace. Across the meal, guests will taste six Madeiras, exploring the spectrum from dry and saline expressions through to richer, caramel-toned styles, with insight into grape varieties, ageing methods, and the oxidative character that gives Madeira its unique flavour profiles and remarkable longevity.
Your ticket covers a themed arrival cocktail, three generous sharing courses, and six Madeira wines paired throughout the afternoon.

events.long_description:
Rodney Scott has been cooking whole-hog barbecue over coals since he was eleven years old. By seventeen, he was working the pits full time. What began as a kid helping out at his parents' roadside business eventually became one of the most celebrated careers in American barbecue. In 2018, Scott was named Best Chef: Southeast by the James Beard Foundation, the second pitmaster ever to win a James Beard chef award. He has appeared alongside Anthony Bourdain in Parts Unknown, and in 2020 was profiled on an episode of Chef's Table: BBQ, showcasing his South Carolina whole hog style. 

Boneface Brewing in Upper Hutt will be transformed for the occasion: American cars out front, whole hogs slow cooking over a fire pit, long trestle tables set up beer-hall style inside, live music, flash tattoos, and a specially brewed Boneface collaboration beer made for the day. Scott will be cooking his signature whole hog alongside a second protein, two hot sides, two cold sides, bread, and condiments. Staff will be dressed for it. So should you!

Your ticket includes food and entertainment. Beverages and flash tattoos are payable on the day.

This International Chef Collaboration is proudly supported by the New Zealand Government’s Events Boost Fund.

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overcoming Imposter Syndrome for Creatives
There is a widespread ‘lack of confidence’ epidemic among creatives, and if you have ever felt like your work is not good enough, hesitated to submit your art to competitions, or doubted your skills when applying for creative jobs, you are not alone! Creatives often feel imposter syndrome most acutely. Unlike other industries, those in the creative field produce something new every time, and sharing this with the world can be daunting, even for established artists.
 This pervasive self-doubt, known as imposter syndrome, affects countless artists and creators, often holding them back from realising their full potential. This concise workshop is designed to help you uncover the roots of this inner voice of insecurity and provide you with effective tools to overcome it. Through engaging activities and practical exercises, you will learn how to transform self-doubt into a source of strength, empowering you to confidently share your unique talents with the world.
 What you won't find in this masterclass: This is not a session about general self-growth or self-confidence, and it does not include positive affirmations or self-talk. All the information provided is based on scientific research and is applicable to all creative sectors.
Bring along some examples of your work on the day (eg a painting, a photograph of your work, etc).
 By the end of this workshop, you’ll be able to: 
Identify and challenge the origins of your imposter syndrome.
Apply practical techniques to silence your inner critic.
Share your creative work with increased confidence.
Turn self-doubt into a motivational tool.
Recognise and celebrate your achievements as a creative professional.

events.name: Retirement Reinvented
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Retirement Reinvented
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
In your middle years, working, retired or somewhere in between? What’s next? Life is about much more than work or leisure, but most of us have given little thought to what “retirement” might mean.
It’s difficult to speculate what may happen in the future – but we can be proactive and take control.
This course offers insights into how to make the most of our time once we’re less focused on career and/or childrearing. It covers many of the issues people face when considering a move from current employment to a different lifestyle that includes more time to do the things we’ve always promised ourselves we’d do – “when we retire”.
After the workshop, you’ll be able to identify a number of common issues and potential ways to manage them when considering and planning your “rejuvenation”, rather than a retirement. We won’t cover financial planning, but will focus on some of the personal growth opportunities for living and making a conscious contribution to your community.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.
By the end of the day, you’ll have:
Developed your own perspective on ageing and retirement in the 21st Century and identified what’s important to you

events.name: Retirement Reinvented
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Whether you’re already retired, or planning ahead, this practical workshop will help you to reflect, re-envision and re-vitalise your life and develop a plan for your future, on your own terms. (NZ citizen and residents free with ID, all others pay $109).

In your middle years, working, retired or somewhere in between? What’s next? Life is about much more than work or leisure, but most of us have given little thought to what “retirement” might mean.

It’s difficult to speculate what may happen in the future – but we can be proactive and take control.
This course offers insights into how to make the most of our time once we’re less focused on career and/or childrearing. It covers many of the issues people face when considering a move from current employment to a different lifestyle that includes more time to do the things we’ve always promised ourselves we’d do – “when we retire”.

After the workshop, you’ll be able to identify a number of common issues and potential ways to manage them when considering and planning your “rejuvenation”, rather than a retirement. We won’t cover financial planning, but will focus on some of the personal growth opportunities for living and making a conscious contribution to your community.

By the end of the day, you’ll have:
- Developed your own perspective on ageing and retirement in the 21st Century and identified what’s important to you
- Completed a personal life audit exercise and considered your strengths
- Explored possibilities in the major aspects of your life and identified potential challenges and strategies for overcoming them
- Developed a blueprint to maximise the best years of your life and developed a “future proofing” downsizing plan
- Considered options to include a sense of purpose and explored and implemented choices that provide you with that sense of purpose
Bring a pen and paper.

1 day, Sat 9:30 AM – 4:00 PM
Wellington High School
Presented by Angela Robertson

events.id: Colourful Enamel Jewellery Day-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Colourful Enamel Jewellery Day
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Learn to create beautiful enamelled jewellery with Lisa Sinclair.

Join us for a full-day enamelling workshop where you’ll explore colour, texture, and fire to create vibrant enamelled jewellery in copper or silver.

This hands-on class focuses on the fundamentals of enamelling, showing you how to apply, fire, and layer enamel to achieve rich, expressive surfaces. You’ll make a simple yet beautifully textured pendant or pair of earrings, then learn how to add a pop (or flood!) of colour to bring your piece to life.

Beginners to metalwork are very welcome - pre-formed shapes are available so you can focus on experimenting with colour, pattern, and mark-making. If you have some metalworking experience, you’re encouraged to take things further by creating and texturing your own metal forms before enamelling.

This is a playful, creative workshop and an ideal class for anyone who loves working with colour, surface, and experimentation - whether you’re new to enamels or keen to deepen your skills.

What you’ll learn:
The basics of enamelling on copper and silver
How to prepare metal for enamelling
Applying enamel using different techniques
Firing enamel and building up layers of colour
Creating texture and pattern in metal
Tips for achieving clean, vibrant enamel finishes

The class fee covers enamel materials but NOT metals. Students can choose from a range of pre-cut copper blanks or use their own copper sheet. Findings and chains are available to purchase at a range of good prices to suit all budgets.

Kids aged approximately 12+ are welcome. Any participant under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

For health and safety reasons, students must wear sturdy closed-toe shoes.

events.id: Exploring Figure & Form-Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Exploring Figure & Form
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
In this course you will study the human figure through clay sculpting from a live model. You will explore the fundamental proportions of the figure; the underlying rhythms to a particular pose that make it look dynamic and alive; and how to recreate the subtleties of the models character. The close observation of volume, curves and angle relationships will sharpen your attention to detail, improving your overall observational skills and enhancing your artistry across all subjects and styles.

This course prioritises hands-on skill development over producing a finished project. Students will focus on mastering sculpting techniques, materials and equipment rather than leaving with a ready-made sculpture.

In this course you will -

- Learn how to imbue a sense of the models personality into your sculpture
- Learn the fundamental proportions of the human figure
- Learn different approaches to rendering the surface of your sculpture
- Explore traditional working methods in sculpting

Course fee includes model, tutor, use of clay, necessary tools & equipment. Please note the following:

- If at the end of the course, you choose to keep your sculpture, there is a $25 additional charge for the clay.
- You also have the option fire your sculpture in the Inverlochy kiln at the end of the course for an additional $60. The sculpture will be ready for collection 3-4 weeks later depending on drying conditions. The $60 extra fee includes the clay, firing and a two hour workshop learning how to hollow out and prep your sculpture for firing. Date, time and payment to be organised at your final class.

This four week course runs on Saturdays, 8-29 Aug, 10am-1pm

events.id: Portraits in Pastels - Painterly Effects-Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Portraits in Pastels - Painterly Effects
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Painting with pastels is a direct, dry, and vibrant medium that mixes directly on paper, allowing for immediate colour application without palettes. Key techniques include layering, blending with fingers or tools, and using side strokes for broad areas.

In this workshop we will:

- Learn about pastel as a medium
- Experiment sketching with various coloured pastels
- Explore different amounts of pressure and its outcomes in mark making
- Learn about using fixative to prevent smudging

Basic materials are included.

Thirty minute lunch break. Bring a packed lunch to have in the historic Inverlochy house or explore the local Te Aro cafes.

Image on website by Susanne Jungersen.

events.id: Découvrez Orléans - Workshop & Tasting-Alliance Française Welington - French Cultural CentreWellington, Wellington-Event Brite
events.name: Découvrez Orléans - Workshop & Tasting
events.venue: Alliance Française Welington - French Cultural CentreWellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview



Join us and learn more about this beautiful town!
🌿 In the heart of the Centre-Val de Loire, along the banks of the Loire river, lies Orléans. A historic city of medieval streets, grand cathedrals and a legacy that helped shape the destiny of France.
This is the France of Jeanne d'Arc: the young heroine who, in 1429, freed the city from siege and helped turn the tide of the Hundred Years' War so decisively at the Battle of Patay that the French expression "mettre la pâtée" (to thrash someone) is said to trace back to it. Wander through the medieval old town, admire the soaring Cathédrale Sainte-Croix, the statues honouring Jeanne d'Arc, the lively place du Martroi and its historic carousel.
Join Lou for a fun and immersive workshop (en français !) and step into the history, traditions and art de vivre of Orléans from the famous Fêtes de Jeanne d'Arc to the Festival de Loire, and the region's culinary treasures: the wines of the Centre-Val de Loire, Orléans mustard, and the beloved Pithiviers.
And of course, we'll wrap up with a tasting of delicious traditional treats from the region!
🗯️ French A2/B1 level required
🗓️ Saturday, 8 August 2026, 11.30pm-1pm
📍 Alliance Française Wellington (78 Victoria Street, Wellington)
🎟️ $30 for AF members & $35 for non-members

events.name: WELLINGTON BREATHWORK EVENT
events.venue: Courtenay CreativeWellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview


Come for the breathwork. Leave with the breakthrough.
A transformational live experience combining breathwork, nervous system power, guided journaling and coaching, created to get you out of your head, into your body, and into the next version of you.

Join Jacqui Sive, Owaken certified breathwork facilitator and veteran coach, for an afternoon of deep nervous system release and rewiring, personal transformation, and embodied breakthrough.
Throughout the afternoon, Jacqui will guide you through a practical, supportive process to help you quiet the mental noise, identify the patterns that have been holding you back, and create space for a real shift in how you feel, think, and move forward.

This is for you if you’re ready to:
stop overthinking and actually feel the shift
release the old story from your body, not just your brain
reconnect with your power, clarity, and aliveness
be guided through coaching, journaling, and breathwork in one potent experience
walk out feeling like, “Oh. I remember who the hell I am.”
Breathwork is a practical way to release built-up tension, overwhelm, and limiting beliefs, so that everyday life feels more manageable & your creativity can FLOW. If you're feeling blocked or stuck, it's your nervous system on high alert, and in breathwork we get to dissolve limiting beliefs and tap back into your power.
CHANGE THE WAY YOU THINK
Limiting beliefs and self-doubt aren’t just thoughts you need to “fix.” They’re patterns held in your body, your nervous system, and your subconscious, often shaped by past experiences, conditioning, and the ways you learned to stay safe, liked, or in control. When your body is in protection mode, your mind follows.
Breathwork shifts this from the inside out.
By working directly with the breath, you calm the nervous system, open the body, and access deeper subconscious layers where beliefs actually live. This is where stored emotion, old fear, and energetic tension can begin to move, without needing to relive or analyse the past.
This is why people often experience rapid shifts through breathwork. You don’t become someone new. You remember yourself underneath the fear, the doubt, and the conditioning.
During this experience, people may move through emotional release, physical sensation, energetic activation, nervous system recalibration, grief release, insight, breakthrough, clarity, peace and profound reconnection to self. Every experience is unique, but many people leave feeling lighter, clearer, stronger, more open, more grounded and more fully alive.

We’ll begin by sharing cacao and coming together in community, creating space to arrive, connect, and gently open into the experience together.
Then, we move into grounding and nervous system preparation so your body feels supported and ready for the journey. From there, you’ll be guided through a powerful active breathwork experience using breath, music, emotional release and live support in the room. Afterwards, we move into integration, grounding and reflection so your system can land the experience and fully receive what has shifted.
This event may deeply support you if you’ve been:
carrying stress, emotion or pressure for too long
feeling stuck, flat, disconnected or shut down
trapped in overthinking and disconnected from your body
navigating change, grief, burnout or inner tension
craving clarity, release, reset or reconnection
doing inner work but still feeling blocked in your body or patterns
No prior breathwork experience is necessary. Beginners are absolutely welcome.
People often leave feeling lighter, clearer, emotionally released, physically grounded, more energised, more open-hearted and more deeply connected to themselves. Sometimes transformation is not about becoming someone new. Sometimes it’s about releasing what has been sitting on top of who you already are.

IMPORTANT:
Please bring a yoga mat, blanket, pillow or cushion, water bottle, journal, and comfortable clothing you can fully relax in. Creating physical comfort helps the nervous system feel safe enough to open and go deeper into the work.
This is your invitation to breathe, release, move what’s been stuck, & come fully home ot yourself with more clarity, more power and more life inside you.
Please note that breathwork may not be suitable for people who are pregnant or experiencing certain medical or psychiatric conditions including epilepsy, severe cardiovascular conditions, schizophrenia, psychosis or recent major surgery. If you have questions about whether this experience is suitable for you, please reach out privately. Your safety is deeply important to us.
Read less

events.long_description:
Overview

An afternoon to boldly lean into your deepest desires & bring them forward with clarity, decisiveness & momentum.
We are so excited to bring you this She Rises experience, curated especially for the Lions Gate portal, one of the most powerful energetic windows of the year. It is a time to boldly lean into your deepest desires and bring them forward with clarity, decisiveness, and momentum.
This is for the woman who holds it all together. You have built the career, managed the household, and shown up capable for everyone who needs you. You are the creative life force that keeps everything running.
But when you are the anchor and the visionary for everyone else, it is easy for your own dreams to get lost in the shuffle. You rarely stop long enough to ask what you actually want.
On Saturday 8th August, we gather at the peak of Lions Gate (8/8), when the star Sirius rises alongside the Sun in Leo. This brings a season full of courage, leadership, and the demand to be seen in your authentic power.
This afternoon is your intentional pause. It is a chance to step out of the busyness, put down the responsibility, and get honest about what you are really building, so you can lead from clarity instead of exhaustion.
The Experience
Guided by Self-Leadership Coach Sina Mikaio, we will move through three powerful pillars to harness the Lions Gate energy:
Movement (The Release) - Before we can build, we must make space. Through gentle somatic movement, you will arrive in your body, quiet the external noise, and physically release the accumulated tension and pressure you no longer wish to carry.
Mindset (The Courage) - With the noise quieted, we will use guided reflection to examine the heavy expectations, perfectionism, and "good girl" habits that keep you playing small. You will shed the masks you wear for others and reconnect with your deepest truth.
Manifestation (The Illumination) - True manifestation is not magic; it requires both clarity and aligned action. You will step into the high-frequency energy of 8/8 to articulate exactly what you are calling in for your life and leadership. You will leave the room not just with a wish, but with a grounded, courageous commitment to take concrete steps toward your intention.
We don't just hope for things to happen. We get clear, and then we take decisive action.
What's Included:
A fully guided experience of movement, mindfulness, and self-leadership.
A safe, intimate, and non-judgmental container of like-minded women.
Nourishing light refreshments to support your physical body.
A toolkit of grounding rituals you can practice at home.
This room is for the visionary, the high-performer, and the quiet anchor who is ready to tune into her highest frequency and lead with her purpose, presence, and power.
Event Details
Date: Saturday, 8th August 2026
Time: 1:00 PM – 4:00 PM
Location: Space Studio, 8 Lookout Road, Mount Victoria, Wellington
Ticket Options:
Early Bird $89 until Sunday 31st July
General Admission $99
Sovereign Access $149 - 5 spots only
Includes your She Rises ticket plus a personal Soulful Strategy Session with Sina.
The afternoon will stir something in you. Ideas will surface. Clarity will come. Insights you've been circling for months will finally land.
The Sovereign session is where we take all of that and make it real.

events.id: Discover Te Muna - Explore the Wines-Escarpment Winery, 275 Te Muna Road, Martinborough-Event Finder
events.name: Discover Te Muna - Explore the Wines
events.venue: Escarpment Winery, 275 Te Muna Road, Martinborough
events.long_description:
Born from passionate vignerons who embrace the challenge of extreme weather conditions, Te Muna valley's unique microclimate and soil structure result in exceptional wines with distinctive style.
Join us for an interactive tasting led by wine writer and educator Joelle Thomson, as we explore a curated selection of Te Muna wines from a variety of producers.

You will be picked up from the Square in Martinborough and driven to the stunning Escarpment vineyard. Joelle will guide you through a tasting of twelve of Te Muna wines. The experience concludes with a relaxed opportunity to revisit some of your favourites while meeting several of the producers, before being transported back to the Square.

Tickets are strictly limited to 18 people.

events.id: Nishi-dham Hatya Rahasya-St Teresa's Parish Karori,Karori Road, Wellington, New Zealand-All Events In
events.name: Nishi-dham Hatya Rahasya
events.venue: St Teresa's Parish Karori,Karori Road, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Nishi-dham Hatya Rahasya
2026 Natokbaaj production coming up – mark the date in your calendar!

We’re back again this year with something new! For the first time, Wellington Natokbaaj is going to produce a murder mystery, Nishi-dham Hatya Rahasya (‘Murder at Nishi-dham’).

The plot is adapted from a novel written by the Queen of Crime, Agatha Christie. We have transported the story to the small town of Birpur in the pre-mobile, pre-Internet era of the 1980s. Our two quirky detectives – Tuni and Bulu – solve a murder occurring at the dilapidated mansion ‘Nishi-dham,’ owned by the enigmatic young woman Billie Mullick.

True to the Natokbaaj pledge, we have aimed to blend pure comedy into the narrative; hoping to bring to you an enjoyable experience of fun and excitement with a dash of fear. Come clue-hunting with us!

events.name: Cooking Classes
events.venue: Sheila's Indian Kitchen, Ashton Fitchett Dr, Wellington
events.long_description:
Authentic Indian cooking classes in Wellington with panaromic views over Wellington Harbour.

In each class, you will learn 4-5 recipes like: potato stuff roti, roasted eggplant curry, wholemeal, roti, naan; shahi paneer; dhal, samosa; palak paneer; gourmet chickpeas; vegetable korma; gulab jamun; kheer; mango lassi; masala chai, and many more...

The classes start at 6 pm or 10:30 am on weekends and weekdays with a 2-hour session followed by a dinner or lunch afterwards. The ingredients, copies of recipes, organic karma drink will be provided with a full course meal in a banquet setting. Custom made classes available for gluten free, dairy free and any other food intolerance and dietary requirements.The ingredients, recipes, complimentary organic karma drinks will be provided with a full course meal.

There are 2 to 8 people in each class in purpose built cooking studio. Also a private cooking classes available.

The menu for the class can be:

1) Spicy potato stuffed paratha and roti, rajasthani tomato relish, aalu matter or spicy peas- potato curry, roasted cumin yogurt raita and fresh mint- coriander chutney.

2) Shahi Paneer (cottage cheese cubes with spices and rich tomato-cashew gravy), garlic coriander naan, cumin jeera basmati rice and sweet fragrant rice pudding with cardamom. Also I will teach how to make fresh paneer.

3) Roasted eggplant curry, plain whole wheat chapatti or roti, jeera aaloo or potato curry, Tuar dahl (split yellow lentil) and Basmati rice with homemade pickle.

4) Palak paneer (creamy spinach curry with cubes of paneer), jeera rice (basmati rice with fragrant spices, panjabi chhole or spicy chickpeas curry and mango lassi. Also fresh paneer making.

5) Khadi (chickpeas fritters in yogurt and chickpeas flour soupy gravy), Aloo-Gobhi (cauliflower and potato curry),  savoury wraps with herbs and spices, fresh pickle and basmati rice.

The total cost is $130 per person, this includes ingredient cost. (As an alternative we also sell cooking class gift vouchers.The food options are unlimited and the class provides fresh and best ingredients)
Please contact for booking: indiancooking@xtra.co.nz

So just bring your taste buds! and Enjoy!!

events.long_description:
BEETHOVEN IN KELBURN

An Evening of Chamber Music

Join Koru Trio for an evening of wonderful music in the beautiful surroundings of St Michael’s Church, Kelburn.

We’ll be performing one of Beethoven’s most loved chamber works, the magnificent Archduke Trio—a piece full of soaring melodies, warmth, humour, and brilliance. To begin, enjoy Beethoven’s charming Romance in F Major for violin and piano, a work of lyrical beauty and elegance.

Koru Trio brings together three Wellington musicians who share a love of chamber music and the joy of performing it for others. Whether you are a devoted classical music enthusiast or simply curious to hear live music in an intimate setting, we would love you to join us.

KORU TRIO
Rachel Thomson - Piano
Anne Loeser - Violin
Sally Isaac - Cello

ENTRY BY KOHA
Suggested contribution:
$20 Adult | $10 Student

events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
TEAM MOKSHA PRESENTS
MOKSHA -5 Year Anniversary Gathering
08 AUGUST 2026 | VALHALLA, WELLINGTON
Tickets here
Five years.
Honestly, it's hard to believe.
What started as a small dream between a few friends has grown into something far bigger than we ever imagined.
Over the last five years, we've shared dancefloors, sunsets, sunrises, laughter, hugs, friendships, and countless unforgettable moments together. We've watched strangers become friends, friends become family, and a community grow around a shared love for music, connection, and freedom.
Our recent gathering, AARANYA , reminded us once again how special this community truly is. Seeing so many beautiful souls come together, dancing under the open sky, sharing smiles and creating memories, filled our hearts with gratitude.
To every artist who has played our stages.
To every volunteer who has helped behind the scenes.
To every person who bought a ticket, shared a post, invited a friend, or danced with us until sunrise...
THANK YOU !
Team Moksha wouldn't exist without you.
As we step into our fifth year, we wanted to celebrate this milestone together.
On Saturday, 08 August, we return to Valhalla Wellington for a special anniversary gathering.
No egos.
No expectations.
Just good music, good people, and the energy that happens when our community comes together as one.
Expect a carefully curated journey through sound, immersive visuals, and the unmistakable atmosphere that has always made Moksha feel like home.
Whether you've been with us since day one or you're about to join us for your very first event, this night is for you.
Let's celebrate five years of music, friendship, growth, and community.
And let's create a few more memories together.
We can't wait to see your faces on the dancefloor again.
With love,
Team Moksha
Five years later, the music still calls us together.
Welcome home.

events.long_description:
Burgin Kerr Norman Play The Shed
Doors open 7pm for a 7:30pm start. The Shed is an unlicensed seated venue.

Irishman Andrew Kerr (ex. Jacky Tar) and Alan Norman (The Warratahs, The Rag Poets) are now a trio after being joined by Paddy Burgin (The Wooden Box Band, The Zimmermans), and his magical guitars. Paddy, a world-renowned luthier, was a member of The Scarborough Connection, who featured on Andrew and Alan’s critically acclaimed 2023 release ‘For the Record.’

A swampy melting pot of country, folk, americana and blues, they combine a mutual love of story-telling and rhythmic grooves with narratives about the human experience. They perform predominantly original material, with contributions from each member, calling on a wide range of instrumentation including piano, acoustic and Weissenborn guitars, accordion, bodhran, and percussion. They have been performing regularly in the Greater Wellington area and South Island over the past 18 months, most recently at Vogelmorn Upstairs, where they played to a full house.

“…..one of the year’s best albums in Americana/folk….a thoughtful, passionate, and musically rich collection that holds up under repeated listens….” Anne Hollister

www.theindiesource.com

events.long_description:

- Learn how to imbue a sense of the models personality into your sculpture
- Learn different approaches to rendering the surface
- Explore traditional working methods
- Discover your own personal style in the art of sculpture

events.name: Sea Glass Jewellery Workshop
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Design and create a unique ring with foraged sea glass ‘gems’ while learning and developing core jewellery fabrication techniques. An opportunity to engage in creative recycling by turning seaside flotsam into precious wearable treasures. Experiment with ring textures and forms in silver, brass and/or copper, then set your unique glass ‘gemstone’. Finish up with your choice of polish, including high lustre gloss, steel brushed satin, or darkened antique finishes.

If you can, please beachcomb and bring along some sea glass options - ideally around 1cm wide, and with a flat back. Glass provided if you are in need.

Techniques:

- Create a ring with one bezel set foraged sea glass ‘gem’
- Use jeweller’s callipers to measure and prepare metal
- Use jeweller’s saws or snips to cut and shape metal
- Use files and sanding to refine and smooth metal edges and surfaces
- Use jeweller’s flame torches to solder join metal pieces
- Use Dremel & bench polishers to refine & finish metal casts into wearable jewellery

Materials: Sea Glass, Copper, Brass, Sterling Silver

Project : 1 Ring with sea glass

Includes Silver, Brass and Copper options

events.id: Sparkly Tapered Rings In Three-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Sparkly Tapered Rings In Three
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Make a stunning heirloom-worthy ring over three sessions!

An excellent, fun class if you have already taken one of our Stacking Rings or Textured Earrings classes and fancy adding to your jewellery collection.

You will learn to create a tapered pattern for a ring to fit your finger. You will get to practice in copper or brass first then make your masterpiece in solid golden bronze. You will measure and cut the bronze, then apply a beautifully shiny, sparkly hammered finish using carefully polished hammers. Then you’ll be guided through soldering and forming up your tapered band, before carefully cleaning it up and applying the finishing touches to make this a ring that will be coveted for generations.

All materials supplied, optional upgrade to solid sterling silver - silver sheets in a range of thicknesses are available for purchase in the workshop.

*If you really love your bronze or brass ring and want to elevate it with a thin sterling silver liner, a 4 or 6 week block is ideal to take your piece to the next level.

Included in the class fee are copper for practising on, and sterling silver bar to create your twist ring and all consumables such as sandpaper, solder and chemicals. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

Kids aged 12 (or so) are welcome to attend the class, but any person under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.id: Advanced Stone Setting: Stepped Bezel in 3 sessions-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Advanced Stone Setting: Stepped Bezel in 3 sessions
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
This workshop is ideal for intermediate-advanced students who have already learned basic soldering and how to bezel set cabochon stones.

A stepped bezel is a beautiful way to set faceted stones, creating a clean, elevated frame that both protects and highlights the gem. In our three-part Stepped Bezel Setting Class, students will learn the complete process of designing and fabricating stepped bezels using sparkling cubic zirconias in copper.

Designed for jewellers looking to refine their fabrication and setting skills, this hands-on workshop explores how to create clean, professional stepped bezels for faceted stones. Students will learn techniques for measuring, constructing, soldering, and setting with accuracy, while gaining a deeper understanding of stone fit and bezel design.

This is a technique class where you will learn techniques to practice in your own time or in regular block classes.

This class will run over 3 separate 3hr sessions and is working towards creating a simple band ring with a stepped bezel.

Session 1 will cover the technique, demonstrations and the basics of measuring and preparing the setting. Students will design their piece and begin the construction.

Session 2 will pick up on the setting techniques, reminding and refining essential steps in the process. Students can expect to be soldering in this class.

Session 3: Troubleshooting can be covered in this class, as well as learning to clean up the settings. Students may begin a second setting that they can continue in their own time.

We will be working in copper for this class ( silver is available for purchase, but we recommend making your first project in copper first). Students should expect to have at least one completed set project and possibly some other practice pieces begun by the end of the three classes.

What is provided: class fees cover your practice metal (copper) and stones (CZ) and detailed handouts that are useful for you to take away to refer to when practicing and honing your skills.

events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Join us for this fabulous introduction to working with colourful molten glass at the Winter Special Price!

This class is a great way for absolute beginners to get a taste of working with glass to produce beautiful beads that can be used in a myriad of ways, including making a unique gift for your loved one (or yourself!).

As one of the earliest forms of human adornment, beads have long functioned as a way to express individuality, and what better way to do that than to learn to make your own unique beads?

Students are shown correct lampworking techniques to produce several decorative beads in just 3 hours! How many beads you make is up to you; some students make up to 10 while others make fewer using trickier techniques.

Kids over 12 (or so) are welcome to take the class, but anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.name: Mental Health and Wellbeing
events.venue: Otaihanga Boating Club, 19 Makora Road, Otaihanga, Paraparaumu
events.long_description:
We warmly invite whānau, carers, community members, and anyone interested in mental wellbeing to join us for an afternoon with Dr Katrina Coleman.

Dr Coleman is a registered nurse, researcher, and health leader with over 20 years’ experience supporting children, families, and communities across Aotearoa. She currently works with Te Whatu Ora’s Mentally Well Team and is passionate about strengthening access to support and improving outcomes for whānau experiencing mental health challenges.

Her work and research focus on the impact of adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and the importance of early support, prevention, and community connection in building long-term wellbeing.

This session will be an opportunity to:
Hear practical insights into supporting mental wellbeing

Learn about strengthening whānau resilience and connection
Share kōrero and ask questions in a safe, welcoming space
Explore ways communities can better support those facing mental health challenges
Everyone is welcome. Your ticket will cover a session with Dr Katrina Coleman and afternoon tea.

events.name: Aroha String Quartet
events.venue: Waikanae Memorial Hall, 7 Pehi Kupa St, Waikanae
events.long_description:
Programme:
Haydn: String Quartet, Opus 64, No 6
Samuel Barber: String Quartet in B minor
Ross Carey: Toccatina
Beethoven: String Quartet, Opus 74 "Harp"

The Aroha String Quartet are popular regular visitors to Waikanae. This time they are joined by a new member, violist Eli Vincent. Australian born, he performed in Germany for some years before joining the NZSO in 2022. Outgoing violist Zhongxian Jin leaves the quartet to allow time for his teaching commitments in China. The remaining long-standing members of the quartet are Haihong Liu and Konstanze Artmann (violins) and Robert Ibell (cello).

The concert opens with a delightfully lyrical quartet by Haydn, Samuel Barber's string quartet follows. Barber is well known for his famous Adagio for Strings but many are unaware that this was originally the slow movement of his only string quartet, written in 1936. Barber arranged the Adagio for string orchestra the same year and later arranged it again as his much-loved and deeply moving choral work Agnus Dei.

After the interval New Zealander Ross Carey's charming Toccatina leads the way to Beethoven's popular Opus 74 quartet, known as "The Harp" because of the striking pizzicato effects in the first movement. A beautiful Adagio and lively Scherzo follow before the quartet ends with a widely varied Theme and Variations movement.
Door sales will be available for the concert or tickets can be purchased from Waikanae New World and Moby Dickens Books in Paraparaumu Beach. For enquiries visit www.waikanaemusic.org.nz

events.long_description:
Auditions: Accomplice
Rehersal Dates: Tuesday/Thursday 7pm, Sunday 4pm, Dates from 23 August.

About the Play
Accomplice is a witty, fast-paced thriller filled with twists, deception, and dark comedy. The show requires quick timing, strong character work, and actors who enjoy playing with suspense and surprise. The less the audience sees coming, the better.

Casting 4 adult roles, all requiring sharp comedic instincts, strong stage presence, and versatility. (Ages listed are playing ages, not required actor ages.)
Derek (30s–50s): Charming, confident, sly. A smooth talker with a calculating streak.
Janet (30s–50s): Intelligent, elegant, and capable of matching wits with anyone.
Jonas (30s–50s): Somewhat eccentric, playful, and unpredictable.
Melinda (30s–50s): Witty, resourceful, and quick on her feet. This role includes a scene with top nudity, facing away from the audience.
Note: This production involves physical comedy and moments of staged intimacy, including one scene with nudity as mentioned above. All work will be choreographed respectfully with performer comfort in mind.

Audition Requirements
• Prepare a short comedic or dramatic monologue (1–2 minutes).
• Cold reads from the script will be provided.
• Auditions will be held in groups.
• Bring any schedule conflicts between 23 August and 7 November.

Rehearsals run Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday, beginning 23rd August. Additional calls may be scheduled closer to opening and keep the weekend of 24 and 25 October free for production weekend.

Book your audition slot here: https://www.wellingtonrepertory.org.nz/auditions/
