events.long_description:
Deep Listening Soundbath at Erskine Chapel
For the first time, a Deep Listening Soundbath inside the sublime acoustics of Erskine Chapel

Tickets available here: https://events.humanitix.com/deep-listening-sound-bath-at-erskine-chapel/tickets

Limited door sales for $50

*Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable. Dress comfortably*

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1.5hr-hour sound bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs and taonga pūoro, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs and other instruments can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the sounds, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1.5hr-hour soundbath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life.

There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

*THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY**

Disclaimer
Sound baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.
Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first

About Us

Alistair is a practitioner of ngā taonga pūoro. He has performed, composed, and collaborated with many of Aotearoa's finest artists, across genres of music and alongside various artistic disciplines since 1999.


Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 35+ years musical experience. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice

events.long_description:
Overview




Join us in Poneke for our first ever entirely lady led BIMinNZ!
Join us on 11 August at the Victoria University of Wellington School of Architecture for the first-ever lady-led BIMinNZ. This special evening brings together three outstanding speakers from across New Zealand's built environment to explore the future of digital delivery through the lenses of digital twins, reality capture, and innovation on complex infrastructure projects. From strategic asset management to cutting-edge reality capture technologies and the delivery of Scott Base in Antarctica, this event will showcase how digital thinking is transforming the way we design, construct, and operate our built environment.

This event will take place within the ground floor atrium space of Te Herenga Waka - Victoria University of NZ Te Aro Campus

Anna Whitmore - Allora
Anna Whitmore will present on how applying systems thinking to capital delivery can improve project outcomes by designing digital twins alongside physical assets from the outset. She will explore the importance of establishing a clear vision to align stakeholders, secure sponsorship, and support the people and change aspects of digital transformation.

Kirsty Mackie - Global Survey
Kirsty Mackie is a reality capture specialist from Global Survey. She will explore the latest innovations in reality capture technology, specifically focusing on how SLAM technology is transforming the industry. Expect an overview of the technology and its different applications.

Hanna Hawke - LT McGuinness
Hanna Hawke from LT McGuinness will share insights from her recent work on the Scott Base Redevelopment in Antarctica, exploring how reality capture and digital innovation are supporting one of the world's most remote and challenging construction projects.
Read less

events.name: Heal the Cause, Not the Symptom
events.venue: Bhakti Lounge WellingtonWellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview
Explore the links between astrology, emotions and wellbeing, and discover a holistic perspective on health and inner balance.
Tuesday Wellbeing Seminars:
Heal the Cause, Not the Symptom: An Evening on Astrology, Emotions & Where Disease Really Begins
Have you ever noticed how the body seems to be trying to tell us something, yet our first instinct is often to reach for a pill or a cream instead of listening?
After working one-on-one with hundreds of people, many experiencing a wide range of physical health challenges, I've noticed that emotional patterns, lifestyle, and living out of alignment with one's nature often play a significant role in wellbeing. Skin issues can sometimes reflect unresolved emotions or feeling like things are "getting under your skin." Persistent tension in the legs may be connected to a lack of stability or healthy boundaries. Anger can manifest as inflammation, while fear may be carried in the gut or the joints. These patterns aren't the whole story, but they can offer valuable insights into what the body may be asking of us.
My study of astrology and ancient wisdom traditions has only deepened this understanding. These teachings explore how different planets and zodiac signs are associated with different parts of the body, and how living out of alignment with our nature and purpose may be reflected in our physical and emotional health.
Perhaps that's the deeper meaning of disease: dis-ease—a state of being out of ease, carrying stress or unresolved emotions that the body hasn't yet found a way to release.
Join us at Bhakti Lounge for an evening exploring these fascinating connections. We'll look at which planets and signs govern different areas of the body, why certain health challenges may arise where they do, and how addressing the underlying emotional and energetic patterns can complement caring for the body, rather than simply focusing on managing symptoms.
The seminar will be followed by a delicious plant-based dinner together, all included in your ticket!
Meet your host Gopi
Gopi helps spiritually minded professionals achieve clarity and overcome challenges on their path through his unique integration of hypnotherapy and palmistry. During his former life as a monk, he delved into the timeless wisdom of astrology, palmistry, and the ancient knowledge of the mind and consciousness, gaining deep insights into human psychology. He combines these powerful teachings with modern, effective tools as a certified practitioner in applied hypnotherapy, along with the knowledge he gained through his diploma in psychology and counseling.

Read less

events.venue: Nayland CollegeNelson, Nelson Region
events.long_description:
Overview
Join the Nelson Youth Council to make reusable beeswax wraps, reduce waste, and learn sustainable everyday habits.
🐝 Event Overview: Beeswax Food Wrap Workshop
Hosted by: Nelson Youth Council
Arrival Information
Please arrive at the Nayland College Reception (Front Office). A Nelson Youth Council volunteer will be there to welcome you and guide you to the workshop room.
We recommend arriving 5–10 minutes early to allow enough time for check-in before the workshop begins.
Join us for a fun, hands-on workshop where you'll learn how to make your own reusable beeswax food wraps while discovering how small lifestyle changes can make a big difference for the environment. This interactive event encourages people of all ages to reduce their reliance on single-use plastics and adopt sustainable alternatives they can use every day.
🌿 What to Expect
When attendees arrive, they'll be welcomed by Nelson Youth Council members and introduced to the purpose of the workshop. A short presentation will explain the environmental impact of plastic food wrap, how beeswax wraps work, and why reusable products are an important step toward a more sustainable future.
Participants will then move to workshop stations where they'll:
Choose from a variety of 100% cotton fabrics.
Learn about the ingredients used, including beeswax, pine resin, and coconut oil.
Watch a live demonstration before creating their own beeswax food wraps.
Leave with two handmade wraps and the knowledge to make more at home.
Throughout the event, the youth council members will be available to assist participants.
♻️ Why It Matters
Every reusable beeswax wrap can replace hundreds of pieces of single-use plastic wrap over its lifetime. By teaching this practical skill, the workshop helps reduce household waste, encourages environmentally friendly habits, and empowers the community to make simple but meaningful changes.
📍 Event Atmosphere
The workshop will have a welcoming and creative atmosphere with:
Hands-on activity stations
Friendly Youth Council members
Examples of finished beeswax wraps
opportunities to connect with others interested in environmental action

Create interesting designs in wax, then send them off to be professionally cast in metal. Once your pieces are back, you will be taught how to cut, file and shape them into wearable pieces.

events.name: New Zealand String Quartet presents: Transform | Wellington
events.venue: Prefab Hall, 14 Jessie St, Wellington
events.long_description:
The New Zealand String Quartet presents their 2026 Season: Storytellers.

Across a three-part Wellington series, we'll explore three distinct programmes: Origins, Transform and Legend. We’ll boldly explore more compositional voices than ever before, beginning with classical masterworks that resonate through the centuries, through to modern-day Grammy winners and the distinctive voices of Aotearoa. The three string quartets of Benjamin Britten form the heart of our 2026 Season, to mark the 50th anniversary of the composer’s death.

Storytellers showcases a rich cross-section of our society and celebrates the art of storytelling through music. Join us in 2026 as together we explore these musical stories.

Programme for Transform:
Henry Purcell - Fantasias
Anthony Ritchie - Perpetual Motion and Last Dance from String Quartet No.3, ‘In Time’
Fanny Mendelssohn - String Quartet in E flat major
Interval
Salina Fisher - Heal
Benjamin Britten - String Quartet No. 2, in C major (Op. 36)

‘Transform’ opens with Henry Purcell's intricately wrought Fantasias, which served as inspiration for Benjamin Britten. Following is Anthony Ritchie, one of Aotearoa’s most eminent composers, celebrating playful melodic lines and infectious rhythm in Perpetual Motion and Last Dance from String Quartet No. 3. Fanny Mendelssohn’s only string quartet showcases her poetic, passionate and introspective voice, too long overlooked in the shadow of her brother, Felix. Salina Fisher’s soothing tribute to grief and loss in Heal serves as a poignant companion to Benjamin Britten’s second string quartet. Written in the immediate aftermath of the Second World War and widely regarded as one of the most extraordinary pieces of the twentieth century, Britten offers a powerful reflection of his inner feelings and a moving tribute to his compositional idol, Henry Purcell.

Explore the rest of the Wellington series:
Origins| Wednesday 6 May, 6:30pm | Prefab Hall, Wellington
Legend | Wednesday 28 October, 6:30pm | Prefab Hall, Wellington

events.name: Westpac Smarts: Beyond the AI Hype
events.venue: Westpac BuildingWellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview




Beyond the AI Hype: A 90-Day Practical Framework to Automate the Drudge and Protect Your Relationships.
Every Wellington business leader is hearing the same message: "Adopt AI or get left behind." But if you run a mid-market firm, a family business, or a non-technical organisation, the reality looks quite different. You do not have a corporate-sized budget, and you do not have an in-house Chief Technology Officer (CTO) to navigate the noise.
The good news? The best AI tools are no longer reserved for enterprise giants. The challenge is knowing exactly where to start to see a measurable return on investment without risking your most valuable asset: your customer relationships.
Join Asa Cox, CEO and Founder of Arcanum AI, for a highly practical session designed specifically for non-corporate business owners. Asa views AI not as a replacement for human capability, but as an "e-bike" the technology provides the propulsion, but your team still steers the route.
In this session, you will discover:
The 90-Day SMB Framework: A step-by-step roadmap to move from "we should look into AI" to clear operational deployment.
Eating the Drudge, Keeping the Relationship: How to deploy AI as a researcher, translator, and workflow amplifier to eliminate painful administrative boilerplate, while freeing your team to focus on client-facing, high-value work.
The "Goldilocks" Use Case: How to identify problems that are big enough to deliver real ROI (in finance, operations, or quoting), but small enough that they do not disrupt your core business.
No CTO Required: Practical steps to implement secure, private AI solutions using your existing staff and basic digital hygiene.
This is not a high-level futurist presentation or a generic tutorial on how to use ChatGPT. It is a down-to-earth briefing for business leaders who want to cut through the hype, reduce operational friction, and drive profitable growth.
Event details:
12:00pm - Networking
12:15pm – Presentation
1:15pm – Wrap-up
Chamber members and Westpac customers: Free entry
Non-members: $10.00 donated to Life Flight Trust through the Westpac Chopper Appeal.
Hosted at the Westpac Building, Wellington
(Level 10, 1 Victoria Street, Wellington)

events.long_description:
Overview

Join NZ cricket legend Grant Elliot for some inspiration, a bit of networking and a drink.
This month:
GRANT ELLIOTT is a renowned former cricketer, having played over 100 games for the Blackcaps. Grant enjoyed success on the international stage particularly with white ball cricket.
Widely regarded by his teammates as a hard worker and a reliable player who always put the team first, Grant was written into New Zealand cricketing folklore books when he hit the winning 6 which propelled the Blackcaps into their first ever World Cup final!
An entertaining and insightful speaker, Grant shares his knowledge of team culture, motivation and exactly what it takes to create a high performing team.
Currently working as partnership manager for Life Flight, he has had over 18 years experience in the corporate world. Merging these two sectors is his passion as he believes sports culture plays a big part into creating a high performing corporate culture.

Overview


An immersive sound bath weaving timeless stories, live music and deep relaxation into a journey of reflection and calm.
The Inner Journey: Story-Led Sound Bath

Across cultures and throughout history, stories have guided people inward, offering wisdom, comfort, and connection. This immersive sound bath blends ancient poetic narratives with the soothing sounds of harmonium, flutes, crystal bowls, and gentle voice to create a space of stillness, reflection, and deep listening.
Mats, blankets and cushions are provided but feel free to bring anything else to aid your comfort.

Please note our events now start at 6pm. Please try to be on time.
A plant-based dinner & dessert follows the event - all included in your ticket!

Meet Smita, your host:
From a young age, Smita was drawn to music as a means for reflection and self-expression. During her music studies at university, she was introduced to taonga pūoro, and this sparked a personal journey of reconnection to te ao Māori and her own whakapapa. Following university, she lived in an ashram for several years where she was introduced to the wonderful practice of bhakti yoga. She now lives with her husband in the Wellington region, where they regularly participate in kirtan (mantra music meditation) at Bhakti Lounge.
Meet Alexandra, your host:
Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from artists such as Deva Premal, The Flying Mystics, Stevin McNamara, and the Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.

Women's Circle: Uninterrupted Feminine Wisdom

A gentle and intuitive gathering for women to slow down, connect, and be heard. This is an open and nurturing space where you are invited to show up as you are, free from expectation or judgment. Through meaningful conversation, creativity, reflection, and shared presence, we honour the wisdom within each woman and create space for authentic connection, self-expression, and belonging.

Please note our events now start at 6pm. Please try to be on time.
There will be a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert to close the night in a grounded and connected way.
Meet Rasesvari, your host

Rasesvari (pronounced Rah-say-shwari) has always remembered feeling connected to healing, the inner world, and what helps people feel well and in alignment. Growing up, she spent many hours tucked away in libraries, reading about philosophy, plants, and anything that felt meaningful or life-giving.
Her path took a few turns away from the usual route, leading her to spend six years in an ashram setting focused on self-development and spiritual life. During that time, she explored meditation deeply and had space to focus on her own healing. This naturally opened the door to learning about Traditional Chinese healing, Ayurveda, sound healing, bioresonance, and a lot of self-study along the way.
Her loving aim is simple: to create spaces where people can finally feel comfortable in themselves again and and have room for their own growth and healing.

events.venue: The Rogue & Vagabond
events.long_description:
Local saxophonist Alex Trask presents original music from his various projects, including a recent recording, his first album, and the Lighthouse Trio setlist. Inspired by folk music from around the world and infused with jazz performance practice, these tunes have a simplicity in common. Free improvised sections contrast carefully arranged melodies, allowing creativity and structure to coexist. The fiddle-esque melodies and straightforward harmonies create an open and inviting sound that changes depending on the musicians on stage. Hiding amongst these tunes will be some swing compositions and arrangements of favourite melodies.

Free entry!

Personnel:
Alex Trask - saxophone
Michael Costeloe - trumpet
Duncan Haynes - piano
Seth Boy - bass
Abey Baillie - drums

Photo by Oscar Laven

Logan Brown is turning 30 this year, and owners Steve Logan and Shaun Clouston are marking the anniversary by inviting thirty lucky guests for eight courses of the most memorable dishes from three decades of exceptional cooking.
Since it opened Logan Brown has welcomed more over 500,000 guests and employed almost 900 staff. The menu will reach back through those eras. Steve and Shaun will be on the floor throughout, introducing each course and sharing the moments, good, bad and ugly, that shaped the restaurant.

Your ticket includes a welcome glass of champagne, eight courses, and six wine matches.

events.name: Atomic!
events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Sing, dance, and lose yourself in a monster setlist of era-defining songs. Led by powerhouse vocalist and Musical Director Julia Deans, Atomic! brings together a who’s-who of Aotearoa’s most celebrated musicians. Together, they take on songs from the iconic catalogues of Blondie, Eurythmics, Pretenders, Kate Bush, Florence + The Machine, Madonna, and more. The set list spans generations and is reimagined with the kind of energy only New Zealand wahine musicians can deliver. Julia is joined by Boh Runga, Dianne Swann, Vera Ellen, and Jazmine Mary. They are backed up by an all-femme band including Karen Hu (drums), Rebel Reid (guitar), Louisa Nicklin (bass), and Ilayda Tunali (keys). 
Now in its 3rd year, Atomic continues to bring high-energy rock in a distinctly Kiwi way. As Julia Deans says, “It’s about celebrating the artists who shaped us — and doing it together, on our own terms. It’s powerful, it’s joyful, and it’s loud.” Bring your dancing shoes and be ready to blow the roof off The Opera House.

events.name: Little Grimley
events.venue: Boathouse Theatre,12 Horton Street, Blenheim, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Little Grimley
The Marlborough Repertory Society is delighted to bring two of David Tristram's much-loved Little Grimley comedies to the Boathouse Theatre this August.

The Little Grimley Amateur Dramatic Society has seen better days. Membership is dwindling, audiences are disappearing, money is running short, and the future of the society hangs by a thread. Yet despite every obstacle, chairman Gordon (Paul Southey) and his long-suffering committee, Margaret (Amanda Tollemache), Joyce (Aley Matthews), Bernard (Peter Morice) remain determined to keep theatre alive in their tiny village.

In Last Tango in Little Grimley, the group faces a financial crisis and comes up with a fundraising idea that is guaranteed to attract attention—whether anyone wants it to or not. What follows is a series of increasingly outrageous plans, misunderstandings, and theatrical disasters that prove desperation really is the mother of invention.

Then, in The Fat Lady Sings in Little Grimley, the society finds itself battling declining audiences, artistic ambition, and the ever-present challenge of putting on a show with limited resources and unlimited optimism. As always, Gordon and his team tackle every setback with unwavering enthusiasm and spectacularly questionable judgment.

Packed with sharp wit, larger-than-life characters, and the wonderfully familiar chaos of amateur theatre, these two award-winning comedies celebrate the passion, determination, and sheer stubbornness of community theatre groups everywhere. Whether you've ever trodden the boards, worked backstage, served on a committee, or simply enjoyed watching things go gloriously wrong, you'll find plenty to recognise—and laugh at—in Little Grimley.

Directed by Abby James, with Assistant Director Bridget McNamara, this production promises an evening of laughter, mayhem, and theatrical misadventure. Book now and discover why, in Little Grimley, the show must go on—even when it really shouldn't. A Community Theatre production of Last Tango in Little Grimley and The Fat Lady Sings in Little Grimley by special arrangement with Samuel French Ltd and The Play Bureau".

events.name: Classical by Candlelight
events.venue: The Runholder, 89 Martins Road
events.long_description:
Candlelight is the only way to experience centuries-old music properly, and The Night Watch, Wellington's premier early music ensemble, know this. So for one night only, in collaboration with National Candles, in a concert steeped in candlelight, this is your chance to go back in time. Keep your phones pocketed and let the modern world recede for a few hours.

Bringing together Australasia's top specialists in early music, The Night Watch perform on period instruments: harpsichord, viola da gamba, and others from a tradition that predates the modern orchestra entirely. The evening features countertenor Austin Haynes and soprano Carleen Ebbs, two of New Zealand's top vocalists. Heard live in a candlelit room, you'll experience this music beyond anything a recording could do. The candles themselves are courtesy of National Candles, one of New Zealand's oldest candle makers, handcrafting their wares for over half a century.
At The Runholder in Martinborough, a three-course family-style menu built for sharing and unhurried conversation. The food is warm and generous: rich winter flavours.

Your ticket includes a welcome drink on arrival and three courses. Additional drinks are available to purchase on the night.

events.name: Lost Wax in Three - Hard Wax - Friday Nights!
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Over three sessions, create stunning jewellery using the age-old lost wax technique. This is an excellent opportunity to treat yourself to some creative fun on a Friday night!

In weeks one and two, you will learn how to work with jeweller's hard wax to create beautiful textures in metal that can be used to create amazing rings or objects. Your waxes will be sent away for casting in the metal of your choice.

Then there will be a week's break before the third session, to allow time for everyone's waxes to be cast. The third session covers how to trim, clean and finish your casts, turning them into original jewellery ready to wear!

More advanced students can use these sessions to complete projects in a class setting.

Included in the class fee are all your different types of waxes, sandpaper and courier costs.

Not included are the casting and metal costs which vary from student to student depending on what sized ring they want to make and the type of metal you choose. Small castings can cost around $6.65 - $12 and might cost between $7 to $30 in metals depending on if you use red bronze, white bronze or silver.

This class is great for teens and kids over 12 or so. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.id: Pour, Explore & Capturing the Cosmos-Parehua Country Estate, New York Street West, Martinborough-Event Finder
events.name: Pour, Explore & Capturing the Cosmos
events.venue: Parehua Country Estate, New York Street West, Martinborough
events.long_description:
Partnering with Wairarapa Dark Sky, Parehua Resort and Night & Light photographer Glen Butler - this hands-on astrophotography workshop will have you capturing the magic of our Dark Sky Reserve.

On arrival you will enjoy a glass of wine and platters while hearing a little about the Wairarapa dark sky reserve. We will then be joined by Glen Butler from Night & Light photography who will provide a presentation on ideas and theory for astrophotography and nightscape imaging. After getting gear set up we will wrap up and head out for a practical guided field-based session giving you the ability to confidently get your own images.

What you need to bring:

- Camera: Any DSLR or mirrorless camera capable of full manual exposure setting
- Lens: A fast wide-angle lens (focal length between 14 and 35mm) with a wide aperture (like f/2.8)
- Sturdy Tripod
- Red-Light capable headtorch
- Charged battery (extras if you have them)

By the end of the evening you may even have an image you can enter into the Wairarapa Dark Sky Reserve Astrophotography competition seeking to find winning shots for the 2027 calendar!

Rain date: 16th August.

events.id: How do I learn? A lecture by Kimberley Moulton-Aho RurukuWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
events.name: How do I learn? A lecture by Kimberley Moulton
events.venue: Aho RurukuWellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview


Curator Kimberley Moulton reponds to how do I learn? in her lecture as part of AGENCY: A curatorial intensive in three questions.
This lecture is presented as part of AGENCY: A curatorial intensive in three questions How do I learn? How do I act? How do I imagine? presented by Artspace Aotearoa and Te Pātaka Toi Adam Art Gallery. Read more about the full symposium programme.
How I Learn: Restoring the Spirit of Collections and Place, an Indigenous space-time curatorial methodology.
There is a continuum of knowledge that manifests through contemporary practice and when artists and community activate object, space and place. These objects and sites can act as mnemonic portals of which we can walk between Ancestral space and today. In this lecture I will consider Indigenous temporality in relation to place and Ancestral belongings in museum collections and the role of contemporary artists in re-storying these spaces beyond the historic past and colonial centre. This Global Majority inter-cultural and space-time dialogue will consider an approach to curatorial work through my framework of restoring the spirit and consider deep-time relational ecologies and materialities that guide me in my practice. Sharing examples of recent projects that meet at the intersection of contemporary art, historical archive and place I will consider the way in which I learn from Country, community and collections.
Workshop participants already have a reserved place at this lecture and are not required to RSVP.
AGENCY: A curatorial intensive in three questions How do I learn? How do I act? How do I imagine? is presented by Artspace Aotearoa and Te Pātaka Toi Adam Art Gallery and supported by Chartwell Trust, Goethe Institut, National Services Te Paerangi, and Toi o Aotearoa Creative New Zealand Te Manu Ka Tau International Delegates Programme.

Biography
Dr Kimberley Moulton is a Yorta Yorta woman from Australia and a curator and writer. Kimberley is a respected international curator working across modern and contemporary art and historical collections. Leading research and curatorial practice in the field of connecting knowledge, histories and futures at the intersection of historical collections and contemporary art, her work centres regenerative re-worlding of art histories and ecological, cultural and relational Indigenous and Global Majority creative practices. She is currently Senior Curator Exhibitions at RISING, the Melbourne international arts festival and most recently held tenure as the Adjunct Curator Indigenous Art Tate London (2023-2026). She has a PhD in curatorial practice from Monash University Melbourne and in 2023 was appointed Curator Emeritus, First Peoples at Museums Victoria.Working with artists to amplify underrepresented art histories, her practice foregrounds connecting communities to collections, through rematriation and re-spiriting collections and place beyond the colonial past. This work has positioned Moulton at the forefront of local and international curatorial and writing praxis which supports contemporary art across multidiscipline areas to re-frame a new dialogue between object, place and community. Kimberley’s research interests include Indigenous rematriation, Ancestral belongings and restitution, Indigenous space-time cosmologies and embodied knowledge in contemporary art practice.Along with her curatorial work Kimberley is currently Deputy Chair of the Board for Australia’s leading regional art gallery, Shepparton Art Museum and Director of the board for the Adam Briggs Foundation.

events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Create your own ring stack from copper, brass, and sterling silver in this fun and rewarding jewellery workshop.

Guided by experienced and supportive tutors, you’ll be introduced to the fundamental skills of jewellery making while creating a small collection of rings to take home.

During this 3-hour class, you’ll learn how to measure your finger, cut metal to size, and add textures and patterns using hammers and punches. You’ll also be shown how to solder your rings with a jeweller’s torch, before finishing them with filing, sanding, and polishing techniques.

By the end of the session, you’ll have crafted a thick sterling silver ring and a stack of copper or brass rings, including two plain round wires to texture as you like, and a choice of decorative brass pearl wire or square wire.

This class is ideal for beginners, groups of friends, or visitors wanting a memorable creative experience. Many students find jewellery making a mindful activity, offering a chance to slow down, work with their hands, and enjoy the rhythm of making.

The class fee includes all materials and consumables, such as solder, sandpaper, and polishing materials. Extra silver and other metals will be available for purchase in the studio for those who would like to expand their collection or upgrade one of their brass or copper wires to a second silver one.

Children aged 12 and over are welcome. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.long_description:
vegetable.machine.animal Album Release
vegetable.animal.machine album release! with UMU and Silicon Tounge.

vegetable.machine.animal (vma) is an interspecies improvisational trio from Te Whanganui-a-Tara/Wellington, Aotearoa New Zealand. Led by drummer Kieran Monaghan [he/him] (ex-mr sterile Assembly), vma transforms the electrical signals of living plants and fungi into sound, fusing modular synths and live percussion in performances that are spontaneous, rhythmic, and unpredictable. This is music as a living system - a real-time collaboration where non-human organisms shape the sonic outcome alongside human performers. No two sets are the same. A Visiting Scholar at Te Kōkī / New Zealand School of Music, Monaghan brings decades of experience across punk, free jazz, and experimental scenes, with vma performing at festivals, residencies, and venues across Aotearoa and internationally.

https://skirtedrecords.com/v-m-a/

-

UMU is improvised dance music duo of hardware synths and electronic drums.

-

events.name: Tulsa Meets Martinborough
events.venue: Union Square, 10 Memorial Square
events.long_description:
From cattle country to oil fields, from dive bars to dinner tables. Tulsa's food tells the story of America's heartland. General Manager Adam Cruz continues his "meets Martinborough" series by bringing the bold, smoky soul of Southern cooking to the Napoleon dining room's intimate fireplace. 
Five courses trace a culinary exploration: start with a Reuben egg roll (sauerkraut, corned beef, Russian dressing), move through fried pork ribs that legend is made of, followed by biscuits swimming in sausage gravy, and then slow-smoked BBQ pulled pork served with cornbread, fried okra, and black-eyed peas — sides that honour the agricultural plains. Strawberry pecan pie closes out the night. Each course pairs with a Martinborough beverage: hand-crafted brews from Martinborough Brewery, award-winning Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from Palliser Estate, a botanical gin from Margrain, and a Noble wine to finish with pie. 
Your ticket includes five courses and four standard drinks (low and non-alcoholic options available).

Whether you're preparing for a long-course event, building fitness through winter, or simply keen to spend a quality day training alongside fellow club members, Winterman is all about getting together, challenging yourself, and enjoying some solid miles with good company.

Start from Freyberg
Follow the new cycleway to Eastbourne and return
Continue over Wainui Hill
Out along the Coast Road to the turnaround point
Return to Freyberg
Approximately 90km total
21km Run
Around the bays
Including the Mt Victoria climb on the return
Finish back at Freyberg

Skip the swim or swim later

Ride only to Eastbourne (60k roundtrip) for a shorter bike option
Choose a flatter, shorter run around the bays

"Everything starts with awareness and a good plan." This isn't your typical financial budgeting session where I tell you to stop buying coffee. It's about understanding the psychology behind how you spend or save, and discovering how we can make preparing for our future easier and more enjoyable. Once you understand how you regard money, you can take control of yours!

Managing finances should be empowering and enjoyable, yet traditional methods often make money a stressful, taboo topic—even with your closest loved ones. In this workshop, we're not here to tell you to cut your budget or skip your favourite treats. Instead, we’ll come together to design a financial plan tailored to your unique needs, making you feel confident, excited, and in control.

In this workshop, you’ll explore the psychology of money and how it influences your financial decisions. Through real-life case studies, step-by-step guidance, and collaborative exercises, you’ll design a financial system that suits your lifestyle, reduces stress, and helps you achieve your goals.

If you want to simplify your finances and live without the worry of every dollar spent, then this is the workshop for you!

events.name: Oil & Cold Wax Landscapes Workshop
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Discover the rich possibilities of oil paint and cold wax medium in this one-day workshop exploring atmospheric and expressive landscape painting.

Through a series of guided exercises, you'll learn how to build layers, create texture, and develop a sense of depth and distance using colour, tone and mark-making. The emphasis is on capturing the essence and feeling of landscape rather than detailed realism, allowing plenty of scope for personal interpretation.

During the workshop you will explore:

- Layering techniques using oil paint and cold wax medium
- Creating atmosphere and depth through colour and tone
- Building texture to suggest landforms and natural elements
- Using tools such as palette knives, brayers and squeegees
- Balancing abstraction with recognisable landscape forms

Suitable for beginners through to experienced artists, this workshop is ideal for anyone wanting to loosen their approach to landscape painting or explore the unique qualities of oil and cold wax.

Guided drawings to help you draw on nature for inspiration and support.

Join us for a DRAW IT OUT drawing for wellness workshop. Practice the ‘art’ of drawing and writing for wellness. This 1.5 hour workshop takes you through guided cues (similar to meditation or journaling) to draw out where you are at, draw out how you are feeling, and draw out your own inner guidance.

events.id: How do I act? A lecture by Clémentine Deliss-Aho RurukuWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
events.name: How do I act? A lecture by Clémentine Deliss
events.venue: Aho RurukuWellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview


Curator Clémentine Deliss reponds to How do I act? in her lecture as part of AGENCY: A curatorial intensive in three questions.
This lecture is presented as part of AGENCY: A curatorial intensive in three questions How do I learn? How do I act? How do I imagine? presented by Artspace Aotearoa and Te Pātaka Toi Adam Art Gallery. Read more about the full symposium programme.
In her talk, Clémentine Deliss will present the Metabolic Museum-University, a transversal curatorial model for remediating contentious or forgotten collections. To illustrate her modus operandi, she will introduce her forthcoming exhibition the “Département des Pièges” (Department of Traps) that opens in November 2026 at the new museum in Brussels, Kanal-Centre Pompidou. The title of the exhibition pays tribute to the Département des Aigles, the fictional museum of modern art by Marcel Broodthaers, the leading Belgian Surrealist and Conceptual artist of the 1960s. Deliss’ exhibition is designed as a study space for visual thinking, an environment that merges the museum with the university. At the centre of the room is a large table in the shape of a lung surrounded by chairs. Artefacts from ten Brussels’ museums are placed in proximity to artists’ prototypes and sculptures by Guillaume Bijl, Kasper Bosmans, Aline Bouvy, Pélagie Gbaguidi, Otobong Nkanga, and more. Works by Belgian and international artists spanning the 17th to the 21st centuries line the wall and include Dutch still life painter Jan Weenix and Luke Willis Thompson. The common thread to all exhibits is the concept of the trap and the lure. The exhibition asks us to imagine new relationships between collections that suspend colonial divisions and speak about today’s worlds.
Workshop participants already have a reserved place at this lecture and are not required to RSVP.
AGENCY: A curatorial intensive in three questions How do I learn? How do I act? How do I imagine? is presented by Artspace Aotearoa and Te Pātaka Toi Adam Art Gallery and supported by Chartwell Trust, Goethe Institut, National Services Te Paerangi, and Toi o Aotearoa Creative New Zealand Te Manu Ka Tau International Delegates Programme.

Biography
Clémentine Deliss works across the borders of contemporary art, curatorial practice, and publishing. She studied art practice in Vienna, and later social anthropology in Vienna, Paris, and London, and received her Ph.D. from the School of African and Oriental Studies, University of London. As an artist-curator, her practice is characterized by an early concern for international artist-led dialogues, team constellations in curating, and new approaches to museology.She is currently Curator at Large at KANAL-Centre Pompidou. Since 2024, she has been KANAL-Guest Professor at the Royal Academy of Fine Arts in Brussels, and since 2021, Global Humanities Professor in History of Art, at the University of Cambridge. Between 2010–2015, she was Director of the Weltkulturen Museum in Frankfurt/Main, where she instituted a new trans-disciplinary lab to remediate collections within a post-ethnological paradigm, working with a wide range of artists, lawyers, and writers.Her book “The Metabolic Museum” (2020) published by Hatje Cantz, came out in Russian translation in 2021 (Garage Museum), and in Spanish in March 2023 (Caniche Editorial, Madrid). Her book “Skin in the Game. Conversations on Risk and Contention” was published in December 2023 by Hatje Cantz/KW to accompany the exhibition at KW. Since 1996, she has produced the independent artists’ and writer’s organ “Metronome”, twice officially invited to documenta, first in 1997 (dx) and then in 2007 (d12). She lives in Berlin and has joint German and British nationality.

events.id: Tudor Consort presents Prophetiae Sibyllarum-St Paul's Church, 1 Langdale Ave, Paraparaumu-Event Finder
events.name: Tudor Consort presents Prophetiae Sibyllarum
events.venue: St Paul's Church, 1 Langdale Ave, Paraparaumu
events.long_description:
The Tudor Consort is thrilled to present Orlande de Lassus' Prophetiae Sibyllarum, one of the greatest works of the sixteenth century.
The twelve motets that comprise the work are written in a style known as ‘musica reservata’ or ‘musica secreta’, featuring highly chromatic chord progressions for greater emotive and expressive effect. In the very first bars Lassus breaks the rules of accepted harmonic practice to produce the sort of music that will not be written again for hundreds of years.
As the name suggests, this style of music was considered very specialised and just for performance to an educated and initiated audience. Prophetiae Sibyllarum is seen by many as the apex of this style, blending expressionism with breathtaking beauty.
This incredible work provided the basis of our sold out performance of Michael Norris’ SoundCathedral at the Aotearoa Festival of the Arts, and we can't wait to perform it in its entirety.
We round out the programme with our favourite Tudor works by Tallis, Byrd and Gibbons, alongside Ross Harris’ Vobiscum in aeternam which was written for The Tudor Consort in 2011.
This will also be our final solo concert in the Lower North Island this year, we hope to see you there!

events.long_description:
Sound Healing Experience at Lotus Yoga Centre
We invite you to a special evening of Sacred Harmonic Sound with multi-instrumentalist Claudio Escutia. This immersive sound journey offers a deeply restorative experience that invites you to settle into stillness, reconnect with the heart, and explore a sense of inner spaciousness through vibration

About the event
Claudio skilfully layers the sounds of gongs, crystal and Tibetan singing bowls, Native American flutes, and other traditional instruments, enhanced through high-quality audio equipment so the sound can be both heard and felt throughout your body.Harmonic sound and vibration offer the nervous system a chance to truly rest. In this state of relaxation, the thinking mind softens, and we find connection to citta — the heart-mind. From this place, silence arises naturally through the vehicle of sound.This experience is open to everyone. No previous yoga or meditation practice is needed.


What to bring:Bring your own yoga mat or camping mattress, small pillows, eye pillows and blanket to assure comfort.

Booking is essential — spaces are limited and this event often fills quickly.

About ClaudioClaudio is a multi-instrumentalist musician originally from Mexico City and now based in Wellington. Born into a family of musicians, he began playing music at a young age and later studied classical guitar. His journey led him to Montreal, where he explored jazz, world music, and spiritual sound traditions.

Extensive travels in Asia and Europe deepened his connection with Indian music and yogic philosophy. He studied Tibetan singing bowls in Kathmandu and Varanasi, and has since worked with a wide range of instruments including the sitar, esraj, bansuri, harmonium, flutes, gongs, and voice.

Claudio’s work blends technical skill, deep presence, and a profound respect for the healing power of sound.

General admission : $45

events.id: How do I imagine? A lecture by Megan Tamati-Quennell-Aho RurukuWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
events.name: How do I imagine? A lecture by Megan Tamati-Quennell
events.venue: Aho RurukuWellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview



Curator Megan Tamati-Quennell reponds to How do I imagine? in her lecture as part of AGENCY: A curatorial intensive in three questions.
This lecture is presented as part of AGENCY: A curatorial intensive in three questions How do I learn? How do I act? How do I imagine? presented by Artspace Aotearoa and Te Pātaka Toi Adam Art Gallery. Read more about the full symposium programme.
Drawing on Māori philosopher Māori Marsden’s definition of ihi as ‘a psychic rather than a spiritual force,’ the presentation explores how transcendent or autonomous power can operate within curatorial practice as a catalyst for cross-cultural solidarity. As well as discussing the concepts evolved for Ihi, Tamati-Quennell will consider how her curatorial methodology of foregrounding Indigeneity and First Nations art, not as peripheral inclusions but as central and generative forces, offered alternate modalities and frames to the globe spanning exhibition of the Sharjah Biennial.
The presentation also contemplates the wider curatorial structure of Sharjah Biennial 16, to carry, developed collectively by the five curators – Alia Swastika, Amal Khalaf, Natasha Ginwala, Zeynep Öz and Tamati-Quennell – through five interrelated exhibitions: Rosestrata: Trajectory/Translation, Throwing Shells, The Ancestral Well: Pulse to Terrain, Yaz and Ihi. Polyphonic, pluri-centric and porous in its structure, Sharjah Biennial 16, to carry enabled each curator – all women of colour – to speak from distinct positionalities while remaining connected within a shared curatorial ecology.
Central to the consideration of the broader curatorial context are the questions conceived collectively, which underpinned the project; *What does it entail ‘to carry’ your home, ancestors and political formations with you? What do we carry when it is time to travel, flee or move on? What are the passages that we form as we migrate between territories and across time? What do we carry when we remain? What do we carry when we survive?
Within Ihi, these propositions resonated through ideas of carrying land, history, grief, ruptured and unsettled pasts, embodied and reclaimed knowledges, speculative futures and more, intrinsic within First Nations cultures, but which also extended meaningfully across the wider constellation of works within Tamati-Quennell’s exhibition.
AGENCY: A curatorial intensive in three questions How do I learn? How do I act? How do I imagine? is presented by Artspace Aotearoa and Te Pātaka Toi Adam Art Gallery and supported by Chartwell Trust, Goethe Institut, National Services Te Paerangi, and Toi o Aotearoa Creative New Zealand Te Manu Ka Tau International Delegates Programme.

Workshop participants already have a reserved place at this lecture and are not required to RSVP.

Biography
Megan Tamati-Quennell is a leading curator and writer. She has a 36-year curatorial career specialising in modern and contemporary Māori and Indigenous art. Megan is the longest serving curator in this field receiving a CNZM in 2024, for her contribution to Māori and First nations art. She is of Te Ātiawa, Ngāti Mutunga, Ngai Tahu, Kāti Māmoe and Waitaha descent. Megan has held curatorial positions at the National Art Gallery, Te Papa Tongarewa and the Govett-Brewster Art Gallery and has worked as an independent curator at the Sharjah Art Foundation and in Busan, South Korea. She currently holds the position of Curator, Modern and Contemporary Māori and Indigenous Art at Te Papa. Recent career highlights include co-curating Sharjah Biennial 16, to carry, 2025 and Emily Karaka: Ka Awatea, A New Dawn, the first major survey exhibition of senior Māori painter Emily Karaka, 2024. Megan is a PhD candidate in Fine Arts, in an Indigenous-led programme at Monash University, Melbourne, Australia.

Read less

Magnus Lindberg Violin Concerto No. 2 (NZ Premiere)

Aotearoa New Zealand’s dramatic landscapes chime in kind with a country half a world away: Finland. In this concert, Arctic North meets Pacific South in a programme of heart-stirring Finnish works that resonate with audiences here.

Pietari Inkinen leads the Aotearoa New Zealand premiere of Finnish composer Magnus Lindberg’s Second Violin Concerto, with NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen as soloist. This duo of Finnish talent are the perfect team to evoke the work’s “massive, expansive ... panoramic vista ... of dark clouds over forests and lakes, of repressed passions and baleful desires” (Financial Times).

We pair this contemporary Finnish masterpiece with a past master. Sibelius’ Pohjola’s Daughter and Lemminkäinen Suite were both inspired by the ancient epic the Kalevala. The latter describes the mythological adventures of the wizard Väinämöinen, the hero Lemminkäinen and their entanglement with the primordial forces of nature, death and magic.

Wade Reeve: A master of guitar accompaniment, Wade’s intuitive playing seamlessly blends melodic, harmonic and rhythmic grooves, providing the backbone for an evening of musical exploration.

This is not your typical recital, but more of a musical living room session – intimate, authentic, and deeply grooving.

Opening act: Johnny Naisbitt – a singer/songwriter and guitarist from Kāpiti who plays regularly at venues in the wider Wellington region.

With thanks to Watson Integrity for their generous sponsorship of the Soundscape Series 2026!

A curated series of intimate live music experiences showcasing the depth, texture and emotion of sound. Each performance invites you to immerse yourself in a new soundscape, informed by genre, sonic craft, and music as an art form. Designed for music lovers who want more than a background soundtrack, this series celebrates live performance with a diverse range of acclaimed performers.

Saturday 15 August — Lisa Tomlins & Wade Reeve

Saturday 19 September — Ossia

events.long_description:
Late Night Knife Fight is the monthly improv battle where three teams face off in a fight for glory, honour, and the audience's favour. The winner returns in the headline spot next month; the losers wail and gnash their teeth.

We'll bring the knives; you bring the judgement.

HEADLINING THIS MONTH: THE NATURAL HISTORY BOY (MATT POWELL)

The first rule of Knife Fight is... book early!
Upcoming teams, full title history and more at Knife Fight's website.

"Being handed a knife as I enter, albeit a plastic one, I could not help but get the feeling that this was going to be a more hardcore night of improv than I had experienced in a while (Late Night Knife Fight) has real potential to become a Wellington institution." - Art Murmurs

"Fundamentally precious" - Theatreview

Late Night Knife Fight is a joyful proving ground for improvisers creating new work and ensembles, offering development, coaching, and collaboration across companies and styles. An opportunity to catch the next big thing in improv before it takes flight, work developed at LNKF has gone on to full seasons and festivals, with Ginge and Minge (Spectacular Organised Chaos Fringe 2025, Breakthrough Comedian Wellington Comedy Awards 2024), Two Dope Teens (Best Improv Nelson Fringe 2018), The History Boy (Tahi 2026), Magnus Steele, and more in development.

Part of The Sublet - a bi-monthly(ish) improv takeover at BATS

Presenting our first Girls Torque here in Aotearoa. Celebrating the wāhine DJs of Te Whanganui-a-Tara. Expect quality selectors playing on the classic Torque Sounds rig that you've heard all over Pōneke and beyond.
Girls Torque is the modern revival of a night that made its mark in London rave scene back in 2004 at the legendary venue; Fridge in Brixton. Two decades on, the scene has transformed. The talent is undeniable, the ranks are deep, and the dancefloor belongs to everyone.This is not a nostalgia trip. It's a resurrection: same name, same energy, new city, new era!
On the line up we have:
M.CAP
Fortuna
Malware
Claire-voyant
Fluffcore
Kicking things off at 9pm with an assortment of electronic music to keep you dancing deep into the night!
Each of the DJ's on this lineup have their names woven into the fabric of Wellington's club scene, each making waves in their own way;
• M.Cap is the founder of 'Nine Oh Nine' who facilitate girls & Femmes only DJ workshops.
• Fortuna is the founder of 'Fortunes' known for their deep/prog/melodic house & techno events.
• Malware is the Co-founder of Venom Events who focus on Techno events here in Pōneke.
• Claire-voyant is one of the founders of Torque Sounds and the original Girls Torque event back in London.
• Fluffcore is the Co-founder of TGF known for their dark techno events.
Come and kanikani to your hearts content amongst friends Saturday August 15th at Valhalla.
Tickets available now via events.humanitix.com/girls-torque

Paraparaumu Community Conversation #1
I’d love for you to join me in Paraparaumu on Saturday 15 August at 3pm at the Paraparaumu Memorial Hall for a community conversation about the future of our electorate and our country.

This event is an opportunity for you to hear a bit about who I am, why I’m standing, and what I believe our electorate deserves. But just as importantly, it’s a chance for me to hear directly from you about what matters most to you and your family.

We’ll talk about the issues shaping everyday life across Kapiti, from good local jobs and access to quality healthcare, to affordable homes and taking real action on the cost of living. This isn’t just about the election on November 7; it’s about how we build a just, thriving future for both our people and the planet.

Hope to see you there!

This event is an opportunity for you to hear a bit about who I am, why I’m standing, and what I believe our electorate deserves.
But just as importantly, it’s a chance for me to hear directly from you about what matters most to you and your family.
We’ll talk about the issues shaping everyday life across Kapiti, from good local jobs and access to quality healthcare, to affordable homes and taking real action on the cost of living.
This isn’t just about the election on November 7; it’s about how we build a just, thriving future for both our people and the planet.

Prophetiae Sibyllarum [Paraparaumu]
The Tudor Consort celebrates its 40th birthday in 2026 and we have an incredible season planned to celebrate. Collaborations with five different ensembles, a debut in Auckland, three premiere performances, and of course a performance of Thomas Tallis’ 40 part masterpiece Spem in alium. Make sure you visit our website to get all the details and secure your tickets!



We will be taking part in our third Aotearoa Festival of the Arts with SoundCathedral on Sunday March 1, an incredible re-composition of Orlande de Lassus’ Prophetiae Sibyllarum by Michael Norris, written especially for our anniversary and the 25th birthday of Stroma contemporary music ensemble. We celebrate going ‘over the hill’ in style in our May 2 concert XL, featuring two 40 part works by Tallis and Mäntyjärvi. We have two concerts with our friends Orchestra Wellington - Leonard Bernstein’s energetic Chichester Psalms as part of W:Ellington on 30 May, and Victoria Kelly’s brand new opera Ocean on 28 November. A debut in Auckland with NZ Barok sees us performing Lotti and Handel, and we finish the year with Messiah with Australian virtuoso harpsichordist and director Erin Helyard.




This is one of the most exciting seasons in our history, and I hope very much you can join us as we celebrate!

From sold-out arena performances across Europe, the celebrated Dire Straits Experience now heads to Wellington. Personnel for the Long Highway World Tour has been assembled by Dire Straits veteran Chris White, who toured with the original band in the 90s. Prodigious singer-guitarist Terence Reis is also on board, adding further clout to the musical genius on stage.
Delving into Mark Knopfler’s platinum catalogue, this world-class ensemble reignites Dire Straits’ greatest hits with skill and showmanship. Hear classics like Money for Nothing, Walk of Life, So Far Away, Brothers in Arms, Sultans of Swing, Tunnel of Love, Telegraph Road, and plenty more. A seven-piece ensemble will take you on a two-hour odyssey with full concert production values.
Formed in London in 1977, Dire Straits was active until 1988 and then again from 1990 to 1995. Across six studio albums and five live albums, they have sold more than 120 million units worldwide.

events.long_description:
Myths & Legends - Wellington
Arctic North meets Pacific South in a programme of heart-stirring Finnish works with conductor Pietari Inkinen and NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen.

Programme:
Sibelius Pohjola’s Daughter
Magnus Lindberg Violin Concerto No. 2 (NZ Premiere)
Sibelius Lemminkäinen Suite

Aotearoa New Zealand’s dramatic landscapes chime in kind with a country half a world away: Finland. In this concert, Arctic North meets Pacific South in a programme of heart-stirring Finnish works that resonate with audiences here.

Pietari Inkinen leads the Aotearoa New Zealand premiere of Finnish composer Magnus Lindberg’s Second Violin Concerto, with NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen as soloist. This duo of Finnish talent are the perfect team to evoke the work’s “massive, expansive ... panoramic vista ... of dark clouds over forests and lakes, of repressed passions and baleful desires” (Financial Times).

We pair this contemporary Finnish masterpiece with a past master. Sibelius’ Pohjola’s Daughter and Lemminkäinen Suite were both inspired by the ancient epic the Kalevala. The latter describes the mythological adventures of the wizard Väinämöinen, the hero Lemminkäinen and their entanglement with the primordial forces of nature, death and magic.

events.long_description:
Soundscape Series: Lisa Tomlins & Wade Reeve
Lisa and Wade are one of Aotearoa’s finest duos, with a rich and engaging sound. Together, they bring a chemistry that only comes from years of performing at the highest level. If you’re looking for a beautiful and unforgettable musical experience on a Saturday night, their blend of jazz and blues, contemporary pop and soul, and homegrown vibes is the perfect tonic.

Lisa Tomlins: One of New Zealand’s most versatile and sought-after vocalists. From her work with Fat Freddy’s Drop and Fly My Pretties to her powerful solo performances, Lisa’s voice is a force of nature - warm, velvety, and effortlessly soulful.

Wade Reeve: A master of guitar accompaniment, Wade’s intuitive playing seamlessly blends melodic, harmonic and rhythmic grooves, providing the backbone for an evening of musical exploration.

This is not your typical recital, but more of a musical living room session – intimate, authentic, and deeply grooving.

Opening act: Johnny Naisbitt – a singer/songwriter and guitarist from Kāpiti who plays regularly at venues in the wider Wellington region.

With thanks to Watson Integrity for their generous sponsorship of the Soundscape Series 2026!

About the Mostly Music Soundscape Series:
A curated series of intimate live music experiences showcasing the depth, texture and emotion of sound. Each performance invites you to immerse yourself in a new soundscape, informed by genre, sonic craft, and music as an art form. Designed for music lovers who want more than a background soundtrack, this series celebrates live performance with a diverse range of acclaimed performers.

Saturday 19 September — Ossia

Saturday 17 October — Michelle Scullion

Doors 7:30pm, with events starting at 8pm.

These events will take place inside at The Bond Store, Paraparaumu and are seated with general admission.

The Bond Store is located at 21 Birmingham Street, Paraparaumu. It operates as The Tasting Room which serves food and beverages.

events.id: Twin Peaks: The Return Part 7 and 8 'Gotta Light?'-Newtown Community Centre Theatre, Columbo Street and Rintoul Street, Newtown, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Twin Peaks: The Return Part 7 and 8 'Gotta Light?'
events.venue: Newtown Community Centre Theatre, Columbo Street and Rintoul Street, Newtown, Wellington
events.long_description:
Get ready for the infamous halfway point of "The Return". The critically acclaimed Part 8: "Gotta Light?".

Widely considered the most experimental, provocative piece of art in the history of television, this cinematic masterpiece takes us on a surreal journey right back to the origin of the root of all evil.
So come join us at the Twin Peaks Townhall (aka: Newtown community centre). Bring some damn good joe, or a damn fine helmet, buckle up and strap yourself in for a stunningly beautiful and also horrendously horrific audiovisual maelstrom "through the darkness of future past that every fan longs to see."

We'll be playing Parts 7 and 8 from the "Z to A" Blu-ray projected from a 4K player onto a 5.5m x 3.7m screen. Written by Mark Frost, David Lynch and directed by David Lynch.

This is what we will be watching :

-David Lynch "Weather Report" and song of the day.
-"Previously on Twin Peaks"
-The Missing Pieces: "Cooper and Diane, Fire walk with me, Party girl, Don't forget, Laura's secret stash, The ring, Annie" (20mins)
-The Return: Part 7 - "There's a body alright" (57mins)
-Intermission
-"Parisienne Cigarette" commercial and the making of ---"Premonitions following an evil deed" short by Lynch, Next ep. of "Invitation to Love".
-The Return: Part 8 - "Gotta Light?" (55mins)
-Bonus collection deleted scenes from Blue velvet, Eraserhead, Wild at Heart, Mulholland Drive and Dune (15mins)

WHERE: Newtown Community Centre. 7 Colombo St. Newtown.
(nb: There is no onsite parking and parking on surrounding streets can be hard to find)

WHEN: Gather from 10:45am on Sunday 16th August 2026.
The screening shall start at 11:00am SHARP!

COST: A lucky $7.

Join us for more Twin Peaks community screenings at:
www.facebook.com/fishinthepercolator
www.instagram.com/fishinthe.percolator

events.name: Find Your Voice - the Throat Chakra
events.venue: Lotus Yoga Centre & RetreatParaparaumu, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview











Awaken authentic expression through Kundalini Yoga, breathwork, meditation and sound.
This workshop is part of an 8-part chakra journey across 2026. Each session stands alone or can be experienced as part of the full series.
Have you ever held back from saying what you really think, struggled to express your needs, or felt disconnected from your authentic voice?
The throat chakra, or Vishuddha, is associated with communication, self-expression, truth, and the ability to speak and listen with clarity. When this energy centre is balanced, we can express ourselves with confidence, authenticity, and ease.
Join us for Find Your Voice, a nurturing workshop combining Kundalini Yoga, breathwork, meditation, and the healing vibrations of the gong to explore and support the throat chakra.
Together we will:
✨ Use movement and breath to release tension and stagnant energy
✨ Explore practices that support authentic self-expression
✨ Cultivate clarity, confidence, and inner listening
✨ Experience deep relaxation through a restorative gong bath
You’ll leave feeling:
• Lighter and more open
• Calm and emotionally grounded
• More connected to yourself
• A deeper sense of inner softness and ease
This is a beginner-friendly, supportive space. No experience needed.
Come as you are and give yourself the opportunity to reconnect with your voice, your truth, and your inner wisdom. 💛
What to expect:
🧘‍♀️ Kundalini Yoga - to balance the throat chakra: 1.30pm – 3.00pm
☕ Break: Herbal tea, healthy snack & oracle cards
🎶 Gong Bath - a restorative practice to integrate and calm the nervous system: 3.30pm – 4.30pm

✨ Come for yoga or the gong bath, or enjoy the full workshop experience.

💫Open to all levels – no experience with yoga or sound healing needed.

💫 Bring an open heart, a yoga mat, blanket, water bottle and anything you need to feel cozy + supported.
Investment:
$35 Yoga | $30 Gong Bath | $55 Both
Special discounted ticket option: $100 two person special - bring a friend with you to attend the yoga and the gong session. Must select this ticket option for the discount to apply (i.e. both people must book together).
If you want to pay by cash on the day or by bank transfer, please send an email to mel@prosperityyoga.co.nz to book your place.

events.long_description:
If you enjoy the beautiful environment of Khandallah Park, join us for a working bee.

We are a very informal group who try to help the plants, birds and other native species in the park thrive by removing invasive plants and replanting with native plants.

Weather permitting, we meet on the third Sunday of each month for two hours of working at your own pace, after which we enjoy a picnic afternoon tea.

If you’d like to help on 21 June, contact us for where to meet up, what’s planned for the afternoon, and also so we can be sure there’s enough cake and cups for afternoon tea. Email Angus Napier: napiers.ace@gmail.com

Vietnamese-Australian pianist Luu Hong Quang has won prizes in several international piano competitions, including winning the Lev Vlassenko Competition in Brisbane. His recent recording of the Liszt Transcendental Études released by Rattle has received widespread acclaim. His recent performances include recitals across New Zealand, Australia, Vietnam, China, Hungary, and Austria, and orchestral appearances with the Queensland Symphony, Royal Philharmonic, and Metropolitan Orchestra of Australia. Luu is currently based in Wellington where he is pursuing his DMA degree under Associate Professor Jian Liu at Victoria University.

Frédéric Chopin Mazurka Op. 17 No 4 in A Minor
Ludwig van Beethoven Piano Sonata No 3 in C Major Op 2 No 3
Franz Liszt Années de pèlerinage III S163

Overview



This practical Business Continuity Planning workshop helps small and medium-sized businesses prepare for disruption before it happens.
Could your business keep operating if something unexpected happened tomorrow?
Disruptions don’t wait until you’re ready. Severe weather, supplier delays, cyber incidents, key staff absence, power outages, cash flow pressure or system failures can all stop normal operations fast.
This practical workshop will help you understand what a Business Continuity Plan is, why it matters, and how to start building one that works for your business.
You’ll learn how to identify your most critical business activities, understand the risks that could interrupt them, and put simple steps in place to keep operating, recover faster and communicate clearly when things go wrong.
What you’ll walk away with
A clear understanding of what a Business Continuity Plan should include
A practical framework to assess, prepare, respond and review
Tools to identify your critical processes, dependencies and recovery priorities
Simple steps to strengthen your business resilience over 30, 60 and 90 days
Confidence to start your plan without waiting for it to be perfect
Who should attend
This workshop is designed for New Zealand small and medium-sized business owners, managers and decision-makers who want to be better prepared for disruption.
Why attend
Because a simple plan started today could make all the difference when disruption arrives tomorrow.

events.name: Introduction to Acceptance and Commitment Therapy Workshop - August 2026
events.venue: Naumi Hotel, 213 Cuba Street, Wellington, New ZealandWellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview




A 2-day introductory, experiential ACT workshop for clinicians.
Over 1000 randomised control trials have clearly demonstrated ACT’s efficacy for a wide range of diagnoses and life problems. ACT helps people make space for their thoughts and feelings while moving towards the life they value. At this experiential workshop you will establish a foundational understanding of Psychological Flexibility, develop skills for using ACT and learn about Relational Frame Theory (RFT).
Over the two days you will learn how to:
meet clients where they are and foster their willingness to change
help clients hold their painful thoughts and emotions gently; identify and actively move towards their values; and develop awareness of the present moment and their capacity to notice it
develop a therapeutic relationship in which support can be provided compassionately and flexibly
formulate life struggles from an ACT perspective
practice ACT exercises and relate the concepts back to your own life and clinical experiences.
This workshop is fully catered with vegetarian food.
Giselle Bahr and Ben Sedley are clinical psychologists and co-founders of ACT Wellington. Since being trained and supervised by many of the world’s leading ACT therapists and researchers, ACT has been the foundation of their practices for many years. Giselle and Ben have both worked at Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services, in Private Practice with adults and adolescents, and trained clinical psychology students at Victoria University of Wellington. Giselle has developed and facilitated groups introducing ACT to parents and adults, and served on the Board of ANZ ACBS. Ben wrote Stuff That Sucks: Accepting what you can’t change and committing to what you can, Holding the Heavy Stuff: making space for critical thoughts and painful emotions, and Stuff That’s Loud: A teen’s guide to unspiralling when OCD gets noisy (with Lisa Coyne). He is also an ACBS Peer Reviewed ACT Trainer.


QUESTIONS AND MORE INFORMATION
How can I contact the organiser with any questions?
Please get in touch if you have any questions about this training. You can email us at:
training@actwellington.co.nz

Can I have a GST Receipt?
If your employer requires a GST receipt from you, please email us and we will send you one.

What's the refund policy?
A refund is available until 30 days before the workshop. This includes all costs except for the eventbrite nonrefundable fee.
A 50% refund is available until 14 days before the workshop.
From 14 days before the workshop, your ticket is non-refundable but fully transferrable. To transfer your ticket to another attendee contact us with the new details.
Full refunds will be made if the event cannot proceed due to Covid19 restrictions, or attendees are unable to travel to the event due to Covid19 restrictions.

events.venue: Te Marae, Te Papa Tongarewa, 55 Cable Street, Wellington
events.long_description:
WHO’S THAT GIRL?: KATE CAMP AND NOELLE MCCARTHY
For one year in 1986, Kate Camp kept a daily diary. In her new book Leather & Chains, she writes back to that thirteen-year-old self. Encountering the pages from the distance of forty years, Kate finds iconic 80s touchstones, swaggering bravado, vulnerability and the linguistic fireworks of the proto-writer. Noelle McCarthy’s new book Stakes brings her Irish Catholic girlhood obsession with Dracula into collision with the world of the 2020s, #MeToo and the horrors emerging from Irish soil. These two memoirists join Kate Duignan for a conversation about hungry girls, and the ones who get invited through the door.

Writers on Mondays is open to the public and free of charge.

events.name: Thriving As a Nation of Readers: Strengthening Reading Communities
events.venue: National Library of New Zealand, 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington
events.long_description:
As part of NZ Children’s Book Week 2026, Te Awhi Rito Reading Ambassador Kate De Goldi will chair a Panel session on why reading for pleasure matters and why strengthening our school reading communities is so important.

Having the skill to read is much more powerful when it’s paired with the will to read. Reading for pleasure is the foundation for full literacy. It builds vocabulary, knowledge, critical thinking and imaginative power.

It also develops an understanding of self and others and contributes to wellbeing. However, in Aotearoa New Zealand there is a steady decline in the numbers of young people reading for pleasure.

Join us at this free event where the panel will explore the current reading landscape. They will discuss the ways schools, libraries, families and whānau, and other organisations can collaborate to build reading communities that support and inspire life-long reading for pleasure.

The event is for educators, librarians, researchers, and anyone interested in engaging young readers.

events.id: RIVERS OF NIHIL - NZ TOUR-Valhalla, Wellington-Valhalla
events.name: RIVERS OF NIHIL - NZ TOUR
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
Pennsylvanias progressive death metal progenitors Rivers of Nihil make their first voyage to Aotearoa New Zealand.
The quartets musicianship has been honed to a fine point thanks to an unrelenting touring schedule over the past few years, including headline tours of the U.S. and EU/UK, as well as touring with Cattle Decapitation, Carnifex, Lorna Shore, Between the Buried and Me, and touring with titans of progressive death metal Cynic, Beyond Creation, and Dååth.
Life on the road for Rivers is a treat for fans and band members alike. For the most part, its very mellow, with a lot of laughs and a lot of ball-busting. Andy (Guitar, Vocals), and I have been friends for over 15 years, and Jared (Drums) has been in the fold since 2017 says founding member/guitarist Brody Uttley. Founding bassist Adam Biggs became the bands new lead vocalist/bassist in 2023, which upped the ante and led to the release of self-titled album Rivers of Nihil (2025). Traditionally, a self-titled record can signal a return to basics and/or a fresh beginning, and in 10 powerful songs, its clear that both those factors are in play. I feel like these songs are the perfect blend of all our albums, with all the fat cut away, says Uttley.
River of Nihil have riffs, big choruses, the prog, the solos, the sax and now it will have Aotearoa New Zealand

events.long_description:
Join us this winter as our community cast brings fireside tales of Norse mythology to life. Blending contemporary dance and physical theatre, Winter’s Saga follows the legendary paths of Loki, Odin and Thor beneath the branches of mighty Yggdrasil. Battles will rage, heroes will rise and fall, and the worlds of gods and mortals will collide in an epic live performance event.
Choreographed by Kate Avery, James Burchell, Joana Joy, Trinity Maydon and Hanna Hairil with support from Sacha Copland
Costume design by Ella Malcolm
Lighting and sound design by Lucas Zaner
Set design by Miho Aragane
Props design by Sherise Ho
Featuring original music by Anna McBride
Produced by Shereen Capper
Winter's Saga is brought to you by Wellington Community Ballet Theatre - a group of community dancers and performers staging dance theatre productions. The company supports emerging choreographers and freelance artists as well as creating opportunities for the community to dance on stage.
The company premiered its first production, "Four Questions" at the New Zealand Fringe Festival in March 2026 to near sold-out audiences. It was nominated for "most promising emerging company" at the Fringe Festival. The audience said: "What a great show! Loved it!"; "It was really lovely to see people truly enjoying dance. I hope to see more like that."; "I really enjoyed it. I heard it's the first performance of the company, which is really impressive, it was super well put together." Winter's Saga will be Wellington Community Ballet Theatre's second production.
Content warning: This production contains flashing lights. It includes depictions of physical violence and death. Parent discretion is advised.

events.name: Pub Choir — Just Think About It
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
You’ll definitely feel better if you come and have a sing with a few thousand strangers. That’s what New Zealand-born vocalist, conductor, and composer Astrid Jorgensen thinks. Astrid is the brainchild behind the touring show Pub Choir — Just Think About It. The premise is simple — come to the Michael Fowler Centre on 19 August and learn one popular song in three-part harmony. What began as a small gathering in a pub has now grown to fill concert halls around the world. No prior training is required — just bring your voice and a sense of humour. 
Astrid established Pub Choir in Brisbane in 2017. Her work associated with the show has gone on to win her several awards. This includes one of the 40 Under 40 Most Influential Asian-Australians by the Asian-Australian Leadership Summit in 2021 and a Medal of the Order of Australia (OAM) in 2023.
