The Bay Express to the Hastings Blossom Festival
Welcome spring in style and climb aboard The Bay Express for a magnificent full-day rail adventure. We are heading to Hawke's Bay for the spectacular Hastings Blossom Festival!

Sit back and relax as our majestic steam locomotive takes you through changing landscapes, winding its way toward the sunny Hawke's Bay. There is no better place to experience the sights and sounds of mainline steam than from our open-air viewing platform. It is the ultimate vantage point for taking stunning photos, hearing the thunderous echo of the engine, and catching the fresh spring breeze.

Throughout the entire journey, our onboard licensed café carriage will be open. You can purchase a range of alcoholic and non-alcoholic refreshments, hot espresso coffees, and sweet treats right from your seat as the scenery rolls by.

Our tracks lead straight into the heart of the action. The train will be stopping right in the middle of Hastings, putting you directly in the center of the festival. Upon arrival, you'll step off the train and straight into the vibrant celebrations of the annual Hastings Blossom Festival. Enjoy a fantastic afternoon exploring the famous public parade, live entertainment, market stalls, and beautiful spring blooms. It’s a proud local tradition celebrating the region's rich orchard heritage, and you are perfectly positioned to enjoy it all at your leisure before our return journey home.

What's Included
Your ticket covers your return journey to Hastings in beautifully maintained premium carriages alongside unrestricted access to the open-air viewing platform for unbeatable sightseeing and photography. You will also have full access to the onboard licensed café carriage selling refreshments, espresso coffees, and snacks. Best of all, you get direct arrival right into the heart of Hastings for the Blossom Festival celebrations with plenty of time to enjoy the festival parade, markets, and entertainment.

events.venue: San Fran,171 Cuba Street, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Debt Club - Foothold Release Tour W/ First Reserve & Dillon Jo - Live @ San Fran
Following the release of their recent single, “I Do Mine”, Debt Club announce their first Aotearoa nationwide tour. The tour will celebrate the release of their debut album “Foothold” which is out August 12th & available for vinyl pre-order now!

Debt Club are a Pōneke based indie / folk rock six piece who blend jangling indie rock, folk, alt-country and emo into a sound defined by rich arrangements, soaring saxophone melodies, and emotionally direct songwriting. Since forming in 2023, the band has quickly become a notable presence in Aotearoa’s underground music scene through their dynamic live performances and textured, heartfelt songs. Debt Club have shared stages with Marlin's Dreaming, Phoebe Rings and Australia’s Floodlights, while appearing at festivals including Rhythm and Vines, Twisted Frequency, CubaDupa and Newtown Festival. Following the release of their debut EP, “Taste For Stout,” the band recently unveiled “I Do Mine,” the first single from their forthcoming debut album “Foothold,” due out on August 12th.

Joining Debt Club for the Wellington date is First Reserve & Dillon Jo!

First Reserve is inevitable. Before adopting the moniker in 2023, Ryan Connaghan had been prolifically writing music that communicated their experiences in life, love, and loneliness. These themes are all approached on songs like “Last One” and “Me & My Friends” – the first offerings from First Reserve’s debut EP “There’s A God” set for release on November 14th, 2025. Thanks to their exhilarating live performances joined by a four-piece band, First Reserve has amassed a cult of devoted supporters both in their hometown of Te Whanganui-a-Tara and beyond. On stage, their sound is both intimate and larger-than-life, combining influences from alt-rock, indie-folk, and pop. First Reserve has supported visiting internationals Hot Mulligan (US) and Keli Holiday (AUS), and have toured with Kiwi favourites PARK RD, There’s A Tuesday, and Wet Denim.

Te Whanganui-a-Tara’s staple, Dillon Jo, is a queer, female-fronted four-piece band formed at Massey University in Wellington. Describing their sound as “Dreamy Droppy Rock Pop,”. ‘Dillon Jo’ is the project of Wellington Based artists Betty Smith and Georgie Levien, building paths between the elements of dream pop, shoegaze, folk, alt rock, and indie pop to create their genre defying sound. They have discovered vibrant chemistry over the past few months since making quite a stir in Wellington, playing numerous shows including opening for The Rions, Foley, Wet Denim, Hemi Hemingway and Coast Arcade only to name a few. Having heard of each other through the Reality music TV show Take The Mic 2022 which they were both contestants on, they formed Dillon Jo in early 2025. Releasing their first acoustic single ‘It was you (she’s been waiting for)’ in April 2025 and releasing two more singles later in the year, including ‘Shiver’ and ‘Jo’. The band also consists of Kahu Sanson-Burnett, (a multi-talented musician, producer, and previous member of Parallel Park) and Ruadh Munro, (Drums and previous member of Scarlett crush) Dillon Jo has transformed their live sets into an unbridled big-sound shoegaze experience

Social Sewing Saturday - September
Come join us for a day of sewing and socialising. Bring your latest project or start something new.

About this Event

Come join us for a fun-filled day of sewing and socializing at Karori Arts & Crafts!
Come join us for a fun-filled day of sewing and socializing at Karori Arts & Crafts! Whether you're a seasoned pro or just starting out, this event is perfect for anyone who loves to sew. Bring your latest project or start something new - either way, you'll have a blast chatting with fellow sewing enthusiasts. Bring your current project or get inspired by others' creations at our friendly gathering. Share tips, tricks, and stories while working on our projects together.
Don't forget to pack your sewing machine, fabric, and any other supplies you'll need. We can't wait to see what you create! You will need to bring your own machine and materials. Please bring an extension lead and multipoint box if you have one. (Don't worry, though—we have some in the centre, too!) We'll supply an iron and ironing board to share, as well as a table and relatively comfy chair each. There are also spare cutting-out tables at a taller height. You are welcome to come along and work on hand-sewing projects.

Cost: Free for members of the Karori Arts Centre or $15 per person payable directly to KACC. (Membership of the centre is $115 annually and also gives you reductions on classes and access to other groups)
Please do NOT attend if you are sick (even just a little bit!)

events.long_description:
The Trinity Hill Vintage Escape
The Trinity Hill Vintage Escape 🍷

Welcome spring in style and step aboard The Trinity Hill Vintage Express for a magnificent, all-inclusive rail and epicurean adventure. We are heading to Hawke's Bay for an exclusive winery experience at one of New Zealand's most prestigious estates.

Sit back and indulge as our majestic steam locomotive sweeps you through changing landscapes, winding its way through the dramatic scenery of the Manawatū Gorge toward sunny Hawke's Bay. There is no better place to experience the romance and grandeur of mainline steam than from our open-air viewing platform. It is the ultimate vantage point for taking stunning photos, capturing the thunderous echo of the engine, and taking in the fresh spring breeze.

Throughout the entire journey, our onboard licensed café carriage will be at your service. You can purchase a range of premium alcoholic and non-alcoholic refreshments, fresh hot coffees, teas, and sweet treats to enjoy right from your seat as the scenery rolls elegantly by.

Our tracks lead straight to Hastings, where a private coach awaits to escort you directly to the legendary Trinity Hill Vineyard in the globally acclaimed Gimblett Gravels district.

This exclusive afternoon centers completely around celebrated viticulture:
- Behind the Cellar Door: Go on an insider's tour to discover their world-class winemaking craft and rich heritage.
- Curated Artisan Lunch: Unwind on the stunning estate grounds with a premium lunch box featuring your choice of a hand-crafted sandwich (such as the bold Beef and Kraut with pickles and cheese, an elegant Chicken and Tarragon, or a vibrant Salad and Hummus with salsa verde).
- Perfect Pairings: Accompanied by a savory scone, sweet slice, and fresh fruit, your estate lunch is paired perfectly with a complimentary glass of Trinity Hill's flagship Hawke's Bay Collection Wine.

Your ticket covers your return rail travel behind a genuine steam locomotive from Kapiti, Horowhenua, or Manawatū, complete with reserved premium carriage seating offering panoramic views. You will have full access to our open-air viewing platform for unbeatable sightseeing and photography, alongside entry to our fully licensed café carriage throughout the rail journey. Seamless coach transfers will also be waiting in Hastings to transition you smoothly from rails to vines.

Once at Trinity Hill, you will enjoy an exclusive winery tour exploring Trinity Hill’s history and winemaking craft. To complement the afternoon, you will receive a curated estate lunch box featuring a premium sandwich, savory scone, sweet slice, and fresh fruit, paired perfectly with a complimentary glass of Trinity Hill's premium Hawke's Bay Collection Wine (or a non-alcoholic alternative).

events.long_description:
Dare to Lead™ | Wellington | 23-25 September 2026
Dare to Lead is the ultimate starting point for brave leaders, courageous cultures, and organisational change.

About this Event


The ultimate starting point for brave leaders, courageous cultures and organisational change.


"Highly recommend."
"Inspiring."
"An amazing experience."
"One 'aha moment' after the other."

Founded on the research of Dr. Brené Brown, Dare to Lead™ is an empirically based courage-building programme, delivered by Boma New Zealand CEO and Certified Dare to Lead™ Facilitator Kaila Colbin.
Brené has spent two decades studying shame and more than seven years specifically looking at leadership. During her research, she interviewed leaders from all over the world — from Fortune 100 companies, non-profits, public sector entities, and more — and asked one question: what is the future of leadership?
Remarkably, their answers pointed to one thing: we need braver leaders.


We need more courage.

The most significant finding from Brené’s latest research, and the foundation of Dare to Lead™, is that courage is a collection of four skill sets that are teachable, measurable, and observable.


After completing the three-day Dare to Lead™ programme you'll understand how to:
Effectively navigate vulnerability and unlock change
Turn values from fluffy language into tangible, practical behaviours
Build a common culture of trust in your team
Cultivate the skills to rise from setbacks and be more resilient


This curriculum is essential for teams who want to:
Be better equipped to deal with difficult conversations
Reduce unhealthy and unproductive behaviour
Be more creative and innovative
Build resilience and improve alignment
Foster a culture of accountability and trust


This experience is for you if:
You're in a position of leadership within your organisation
You see the potential in people and processes, and are willing to take responsibility for achieving that potential
You’re passionate about accelerating performance in yourself and others
You have to navigate organisational change as part of your role



Need help with the cost?
If you are an Educator or at a Not-for-Profit, you can automatically access a special price of $1,995 + GST when you register.
We also have partial scholarships available to attend the programme. Apply here and we’ll be in touch.
Boma is a Regional Business Network Provider. Your organisation may be eligible for funding support to attend this programme. Find out more at regionalbusinesspartners.co.nz


Our Health and Safety Plan
Boma is committed to delivering safe events. We follow best practices suggested by the New Zealand health authorities and work closely with our suppliers to prioritise health and wellbeing.
Our comprehensive health and safety plans ensure you can book with certainty and attend with confidence.



Our refund policy
For details on event refunds and transfers, please see our refund policy.


Contact us
Please email with any questions.

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Mental Health First Aid Aotearoa
NZ Citizens and residents pay $219 with ID.  f you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $499 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register..
Mental Health First Aid is an evidence-based workshop which gives people the skills and confidence to have supportive conversations with their whānau, co-workers and community and help guide them to professional help if needed.
You will learn to recognise common mental health challenges, how to provide initial help to someone experiencing a mental health challenge using a practical, evidence-based action plan, and how to respond in a crisis situation. During the workshop you will have the opportunity to practice new skills in a safe environment.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.
Mental health challenges covered in the course include:
Depression
Anxiety
Psychosis
Substance use problems
Mental Health Crisis Covered:
Suicidal thoughts and behaviours
Non- Suicidal self-injury
Panic attack
Traumatic events
Severe effects from Alcohol or other substance use
Aggressive behaviours
People who attend Mental Health First Aid training can complete a short online assessment to be accredited as a Mental Health First Aider. You must attend the full two days to be able to do the online assessment for accreditation. The accreditation is valid for three years.
If you choose not to be accredited, you will receive a certificate of participation if you attend the full course. You will also receive a workbook as part of your course fee.
A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Biker Breakfast
Bikers Breakfast is on again this year.
Closer to the date will advise details of a ride, but RAC wgtn will also have a stand there to share what we are about.
Open to some people to be available to help on the stand.

Other details of the Bikers Breakfast are:-
"We are organising our second annual Bikers Breakfast on Saturday 26 September from 8:30 am – 12:30 pm. This motorcycle safety event will be held in collaboration with Kapiti Coast District Council and Southwards Car Museum. Last year the Ulysses Club participated, and this year we would like to have a few more clubs in attendance, if possible.
Ride Forever course providers will be attending to speak with motorcyclists about the merits of learning to ride safely by signing up for ACC’s Ride Forever courses. The Motorcycle Collective will be setting up a safety gear Op Shop with a range of motorcycle apparel and equipment, and we will be giving away hot drinks and bacon butties.
A blind zone demonstration will show how easily a motorcycle can be invisible to large trucks – riders can sit in the cab of the truck and see if they can spot the bikes. There will be a helmet cleaning station and free rider safety packages that include important safety items like screen cleaners and re-usable hand warmers."

events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre,111 Wakefield St, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Four Last Songs - Wellington
One of the world’s most acclaimed conductors, Sir Donald Runnicles, returns to the NZSO in a programme of pure luxury and ravishing beauty.

Programme:
R Strauss Rosenkavalier Suite
R Strauss Four Last Songs
Brahms Symphony No. 3

The sensuous, glittering raptures of the Rosenkavalier Suite evoke the decadence of 18th century Vienna in a dazzling array of complex waltzes.

Then delve deeper into Richard Strauss’ most personal, revealing and achingly beautiful music with his sublime Four Last Songs. These profound songs, performed by silver-voiced soprano Madeleine Pierard, sumptuously evoke a sunset portrait of a wife well loved and a life well lived.

We balance this decadence with the crystalline Symphony No. 3 from Johannes Brahms. In music that plays between light and shadow, the work takes on as its organising motto frei aber froh — free but happy.

Sir Donald Runnicles appears with generous support from Dame Bronwen Holdsworth DNZM.

Live, Razorlight animate the entire room.

‘’The rhythm drove through the room like a heartbeat, and the connection between the band members was electric. Each note and lyric lands with precision and passion.’’ – At The Barrier

New Zealand, prepare to surrender to the might of AUGUST BURNS RED this October, with the GRAMMY Award-nominated stalwarts set to return to our shores joined by special guests BLOOM,
“We are so excited to headline and return back to New Zealand after a decade! We are bringing along our new friends in Bloom to make this a can’t miss show. This tour will also be the first place in the world where we do a tour celebrating the release of our brand new record Season of Surrender. We hope to see you all soon!” - August Burns Red
Crafting their signature brand of metalcore for over two decades, AUGUST BURNS RED have ferociously established themselves as one of the foremost acts in the genre. Hailing from Lancaster, Pennsylvania, the band's milestones and legacy spans everything from multiple top 10 placements on the Billboard Top 200 and tours with everyone from Bullet For My Valentine through to A Day To Remember and countless more. Also with two GRAMMY Award nominations in their wake, nominated for Best Metal Performance in 2016 for Identity and again in 2018 for Invisible Enemy, AUGUST BURNS RED have never rested on their laurels or stopped pushing the limits of their sound; a fact that has loudly carried into 2026 with the upcoming release of a their tenth studio album Season Of Surrender due out on June 5 via Fearless Records. 
On a live front, AUGUST BURNS RED's reputation is as formidable as their creative output, renowned for their visceral performances across the globe, most recently stupefying Australian crowds in 2023 supporting Polaris nationally on the Fatalism Tour. Praised by Scenestr for delivering "a raging masterclass in pure American metalcore with a 20-year, career-spanning set list that resonated spectacularly" of the Adelaide show supporting Polaris, X-Press Magazine also declared of the band's 2023 Perth performance on the same run that ABR demonstrated "why they have cemented themselves as one of the most respected names in the scene." 
One of Australia's most prolific rising heavy acts, BLOOM wield an open-veined take on melodic hardcore that has seen them tour the globe, release two full-length albums and cultivate an army of dedicated fans along the way. Emerging in 2017, BLOOM released their 2024 debut full-length, Maybe In Another Life, before swiftly turning their gaze to their 2025 sophomore album, The Light We Chase. Wowing with their multi-faceted and matured collection of songs on album #2, also expanding their creative reach further than ever before, BLOOM kicked off 2026 with their biggest headline performances to date, touring Australia nationally to celebrate The Light We Chase. Whether sharing stages with the likes of Silverstein and Thornhill or enamouring as headliners, you can definitely count on one thing when it comes to a BLOOM live show: it is seriously not to be missed.

events.id: Cornelia Parker-City Gallery Wellington-Wellington NZ
events.name: Cornelia Parker
events.venue: City Gallery Wellington
events.long_description:
After three years of closure, the newly renovated and strengthened City Gallery Wellington Te Whare Toi will host the art of Cornelia Parker. The British visual artist is best known for her innovative and contemporary sculpture and installation art. Her large-scale, immersive installations explore themes of destruction and reconstruction, transformation and metamorphosis. Objects are exploded, crushed, and suspended in a world upended and remade anew.
Curated by independent UK-based curator Andrea Schlieker and City Gallery Wellington’s Senior Curator Aaron Lister, City Gallery Wellington’s exhibition will encompass Parker’s long career as an artist. This includes an immersive sound-and-light installation, ‘Stolen Thunder’. The work gathers the sounds of approaching storms from around the globe and across time. The exhibition will also showcase her paintings, photos, films, and sculptures.
“I have always said this is the one exhibition I want to do before I die,” said Charlotte Davy, Ringatohu Toi Director, Art and City Gallery Wellington. “I have been following Cornelia Parker’s work for the last twenty years. Bringing her mischievous, dark, and literally explosive work to Wellington is incredible.” 
Parker’s work often fills entire rooms and invites the viewer to move through and around the art. Given its physical scale, the blank canvas of the reopened gallery offers the perfect opportunity to host the exhibition. The exhibition will kick off in October 2026 and run through March 2027. 
Charlotte notes the exhibition’s themes are also of particular relevance to Wellington. “I hope that the exhibition and our return to Te Ngākau Civic Square will reflect our city and also help remake it. We are looking forward to opening with a bang.”

events.name: Effective Business Analysis
events.venue: Venue To be Confirmed | Wellington CBD,Level 5, 111 The Terrace, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Effective Business Analysis
Defining change with clarity and agility. Discover how to apply the core skills and techniques of elicitation, analysis, and communication.

About this Event


Description
The business world is demanding faster change, the ability to adapt and solutions that are fit for purpose. As a business analyst, you're counted on for your skills as a conceptual and practical thinker, a relationship builder, and a translator. You're relied upon to identify and describe the change required to address business issues. Sometimes there are problems that require a fix, opportunities that need to be realised or situations where the business simply doesn't know but is prepared to "give it a go" and experiment to gain insights to what it should do next.
In this course, you'll be introduced to a series of context aware, business-focussed approaches that you can apply to:
Work with stakeholders to uncover the business issue that needs to be addressed
Define the change required within its context
Prioritise and scope the requirements based on business value and
Specify requirements clearly to those delivering the solution
Designed and delivered by our Equinox IT team of practicing business analysts, this course covers how to structure your analysis activities based on the context and the issue at hand to describe requirements that fully represent the change required.




Outline
Day 1
Overview and concepts
What is business analysis?
Requirements analysis framework

Discover – understanding context
Understanding a business domain
Adjusting to different types of initiative
Stakeholders – identification, classification and engaging
Techniques (root cause analysis, 5 whys, diverge, converge, etc.)
The discovery canvas

Focus topic: Elicitation –gathering information and understanding
Purpose and context
Selecting the right technique (interviews, workshops, research, observation, brainstorming, etc.)
Planning a session
Running a session
Post session activities
Main exercise - role play

Day 2
Define – understanding the change required
Introduction to capabilities
Information and data – concept/domain Modelling
Business process – tips on modelling
Business rules – their relationship with other business concepts
Scenarios – use cases
Change strategy map
Change aspect map
Defining user and other stories

Scope – understanding priority and value
Helping the business to assess value
Techniques
User story maps

Day 3
Focus topic: Workshop Facilitation–gaining consensus
Being self-aware
Facilitation
Preparation
Group dynamics
Handling various situations
Main exercise - role play

Deliver – packaging for delivery
Backlog refinement
Developing good acceptance criteria
Understanding various types of solution requirements and contributing elements

Focus topic: Communication – telling the story
A brief overview of the difference between specification and communication




Learning outcomes
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to;
Analyse and understand the kind of business issue that needs to be addressed
Engage stakeholders and analyse their business needs
Define a change strategy
Define the aspects of change required
Understand various business models e.g. business process, information, business rules
Define a user story and associated requirements
Use effective techniques to elicit requirements
Understand how to plan and facilitate a requirements workshop
Understand scoping based on business value
Analyse, document and review solutions and detailed requirements
Define acceptance criteria
Understand how to communicate with a variety of audiences




Accreditation and certification
This course aligns with the Business Analysis Body of Knowledge v3.0®.




Audience
The primary audience for this course is business analysts, systems analysts and enterprise analysts of all experience levels. The course will also be of value to any project team members involved in requirements definition activities.




Prerequisites
There are no prerequisites for this course, however, some experience in business analysis will help.

About this Event Description The business world is demanding faster change, the ability to adapt and solutions that are fit for purpose.
In this course, you'll be introduced to a series of context aware, business-focussed approaches that you can apply to: Work with stakeholders to uncover the business issue that needs to be addressed Define the change required within its context Prioritise and scope the requirements based on business value and Specify requirements clearly to those delivering the solution Designed and delivered by our Equinox IT team of practicing business analysts, this course covers how to structure your analysis activities based on the context and the issue at hand to describe requirements that fully represent the change required.
Requirements analysis framework Discover – understanding context Understanding a business domain Adjusting to different types of initiative Stakeholders – identification, classification and engaging Techniques (root cause analysis, 5 whys, diverge, converge, etc.)
Planning a session Running a session Post session activities Main exercise - role play Day 2 Define – understanding the change required Introduction to capabilities Information and data – concept/domain Modelling Business process – tips on modelling Business rules – their relationship with other business concepts Scenarios – use cases Change strategy map Change aspect map Defining user and other stories Scope – understanding priority and value Helping the business to assess value Techniques User story maps Day 3 Focus topic: Workshop Facilitation–gaining consensus Being self-aware Facilitation Preparation Group dynamics Handling various situations Main exercise - role play Deliver – packaging for delivery Backlog refinement Developing good acceptance criteria Understanding various types of solution requirements and contributing elements Focus topic: Communication – telling the story A brief overview of the difference between specification and communication Learning outcomes Upon completion of this course, students will be able to; Analyse and understand the kind of business issue that needs to be addressed Engage stakeholders and analyse their business needs Define a change strategy Define the aspects of change required Understand various business models e.g. business process, information, business rules Define a user story and associated requirements Use effective techniques to elicit requirements Understand how to plan and facilitate a requirements workshop Understand scoping based on business value Analyse, document and review solutions and detailed requirements Define acceptance criteria Understand how to communicate with a variety of audiences Accreditation and certification This course aligns with the Business Analysis Body of Knowledge v3.0®.
The course will also be of value to any project team members involved in requirements definition activities.

events.id: English in the Community: Johnsonville - Elementary (ESOL Level 2)-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington-Wellington High School

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
English in the Community: Johnsonville - Elementary (ESOL Level 2)
English in the Community courses help you to learn more English, get to know your community and meet new people. The groups aim to help you use what you already know, learn more from your tutor and the other students and feel more at home in your local community. 
To enrol in these courses, please contact the CEC office on 04 385 8919 or cec@whs.school.nz.
By the end of the course, you'll: 
• Be more confident in speaking English in everyday situations
• Be able to understand more English, especially “New Zealand English”
• Have increased your vocabulary
• Be able to talk more about living in New Zealand and your local community
The courses are free for NZ residents and citizens. The course fee for non-residents is $155.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.id: Sewing - All Levels-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington-Wellington High School
events.name: Sewing - All Levels
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Sewing - All Levels
All levels welcome! Beginning sewers will learn basic skills and techniques and those with some experience will improve their skills and learn tips and tricks.
Beginners - If you're a beginner, you'll start by making a lined bag, which teaches all the basic skills involved. After that you'll move on to a project of your choice, in consultation with the tutor.  Please bring: 1 metre of firm cotton fabric for your bag outer and 1 metre of a lighter cotton fabric for the lining. You'll also need to bring scissors, a Bernina bobbin (this can be purchased from the CEC office on the day of the course for $7), pins, thread to match your outer fabric, an 18 cm zip and tape measure to the first session.
 If you're a returning student, or have already mastered the basic skills, you'll work on your own project so please bring along whatever you're currently working on (or something new) and your sewing kit. 
Please note PDF patterns are not suitable for this course unless you are very experienced in using them;  we strongly recommend patterns from the following companies:  Simplicity, Butterick, New Look or Quicksew.
By the end of the course, you'll have been introduced to basic skills in dressmaking, if beginners, or further skills for the more experienced.
You'll be able to:
• Use all sewing machine equipment and demonstrate basic sewing techniques (basic seams and finishes)
• Begin to read a commercial pattern and select appropriate materials for task
• Cut out and construct a garment using techniques learned
• (In addition), use a variety of advanced sewing techniques e.g. rolled hems, various zip insertions (invisible and standard), make buttonholes or line garments. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.name: Cooking: More Tastes of Vietnamese Street Food
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Cooking: More Tastes of Vietnamese Street Food
Come along and learn how to create wonderful Vietnamese dishes bursting with fresh flavours. 
Depending on what's seasonally available, dishes taught may include some of the following: green papaya prawn salad (Nộm tôm đu đủ xanh), lemongrass chicken stir fry with steamed rice (Cơm Gà rang sả) , grilled pork noodle and fried rolls (bún nem thịt nướng) and beef noodle soup (Phở bò). 
All ingredients provided but bring an apron, dish cloth, tea towels and containers to take food home.
Note:  Our cooking courses are designed to provide a collaborative and immersive learning experience where learners often work in pairs and/or groups. While we wish to create an inclusive environment for all participants, it is important to note that our courses are unable to accommodate specific food allergies or deviate from the preplanned dishes and menus.
Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Scottish Country Dancing
Why do Scottish Country Dancing? Great music and amazing ‘brain gym’ for body and mind! Scottish Country Dancing is a very social form of dancing, danced in "sets" usually with four "couples" - unlike Highland Dancing which is usually solo dancing. Have fun and meet new people, while getting fit!
It’s suitable for all levels of fitness, and is a great way of meeting and socialising with new people. Scottish country dancing is a common pastime for thousands of dancers in many countries, whether you’re in Japan, Germany, the US or Scotland itself.
Wear soft flat shoes and loose clothing and bring a bottle of water. No partner is needed – we change partners for every dance!
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
• Name and perform to beginner level the five major steps of Scottish Country Dancing
• Name and perform ten simple formations
• Participate in five simple Scottish Country dances, in strathspey (slow) and reel/jig (fast) tempo
• Clap rhythm to reel, jig and strathspey tempo
• Have the confidence and skills to join a club to progress your social dancing 
[This is a physical activity that involves an element of risk.  While all possible measures are taken to prevent accidents or injury, please note that participation is at your own risk]. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.id: Crochet for Calmness-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington-Wellington High School
events.name: Crochet for Calmness
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Crochet for Calmness
The repetitive movements of crochet help the brain make more serotonin, which can decrease tension and feelings of depression. We’ll move through all the steps from the starting slipknot to reading patterns and diagrams and making your first crochet projects.
You’ll learn to make a granny square, change colours and how to increase and decrease. You’ll also find out more about the notations and abbreviations of crochet stitches so you can make those awesome crochet projects you've been waiting to make!
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
• Discuss the benefits of crochet for relaxation and alleviation of mood
• Read a basic crochet pattern and recognise crochet terminology
• Choose yarns and hooks for projects
• Use a range of stitches with confidence
• Complete at least one project of your choice (granny square, keychain, garden decoration)
Suitable for all beginners, both left and right-handers and those who may have struggled to learn to crochet. Initial materials provided but please bring along any yarn or crochet hooks you would like to work with.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Make Your Own Roman Blinds
Roman blinds are a perennial favourite because they use a lot less fabric than the usual pencil pleated or gathered curtains - as well as making your rooms look streamlined and uncluttered.
During the four weeks you will learn how to accurately measure your window to enable you to create very own customized roman blind. 
Some hardware included in course fee but a list of all other materials (fabric, etc) will be sent out to you when the course is confirmed.
Please choose a narrow window for your first project - max 150cms wide.
By the end of the course you'll be able to
Accurately measure your window 
Calculate how much fabric to purchase
Measure and cut out your curtain
Use appropriate machine skills to sew your curtain fabric
Use finishing skills to apply rings and cords to your curtain
Identify appropriate method to hang Roman Blind
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. events.id: Songwriting: How to Write Your Own Songs-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington-Wellington High School
events.name: Songwriting: How to Write Your Own Songs
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Songwriting: How to Write Your Own Songs
The course is ideal for anyone who wants to write better songs - whether you’ve got a few songs under your belt or you’re a complete beginner. Take a song idea through to a finished song you can be proud of. Split into easy-to-follow steps, this course walks you through everything from finding titles to writing chord progressions and ensuring your lyrics and melodies fit together. You’ll share your creations with fellow songwriters and get personalised feedback. You’ll see exactly how to turn theory into practice and write your best songs yet.
This course includes:
-  Practical tips and techniques for songwriting
-  Ideas for making your songs stronger, more expressive and more appealing to your audience
-  How to overcome writer’s block, be an inspired and prolific songwriter who writes authentic songs
-  An opportunity to share your songs with fellow students, bounce off ideas and learn from one another
-  Learn how to structure a song effectively
-  The pillars of songwriting and how to use them
-  How to write better lyrics
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
-  Discover the exact steps to successfully write your own original songs; expanding a song from a verse and chorus, to a complete song while keeping your listeners engaged using transitions and dynamic contrasts between sections
-  Come up with ideas, write lyrics, melodies, chord progressions and instrumental grooves that have an emotional impact on you and your audience
-  Identify the structure of a great song, including how to combine melody, chords, lyrics and rhythm that create magic for your listeners
-  Possess the confidence and skills to find inspiration and get past common creative hurdles and blocks so you can develop an initial spark of creativity into a complete song
-  Stay inspired and find your authentic voice as a songwriter. r
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.id: Macy Gray Live-St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Macy Gray Live
events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
The rasp in her singing voice is as immediately recognisable as her talent for entertaining. Nobody puts on a show like R&B/soul singer Macy Gray. The Ohio-born artist came to fame in 1999 with her triple-platinum debut album ‘On How Life Is’. Her concert at Wellington’s St James Theatre will deliver a jaw-dropping celebration of chart-topping hits I Try, Still, Do Something, Sexual Revolution, and Sweet Baby. You can also expect her new single I’m Too Sexy from her upcoming album, The Trouble With Truth. 
Presented in association with the Wellington Jazz Festival, this is a rare chance to see one of the great R&B and soul artists of a generation. Macy Gray has sold over 25 million albums worldwide and won a GRAMMY Award along with two BRIT Awards. She has collaborated with everyone from Ariana Grande to Maino and Galactic. Her music consistently resonates throughout pop culture, transcending many genres and building a devout and diverse fan base.

NextGen Ministry Leaders Gathering - Kids, Youth and Young Adult Leaders
A Weekend That Shapes the Future.

If you care about the next generation—kids, youth, or young adults—this weekend is for you. Next Gen leaders know the power of a single caring adult in a young person’s life.
You know partnering with parents matters. You know smooth transitions between age groups matter. And you know that the best way for a kid or young person to know Jesus…
is to know someone who knows Jesus.

That someone could be you.

Across the weekend we will:

Cast a united vision for how we serve the next generation
Learn practical skills for each age group
Share stories of impact and transformation
Worship and pray together
Strengthen the relationships that make ministry work
Get equipped, inspired, and refuelled for the season ahead

Whether you’ve been serving for years or you’re simply curious about getting involved, come and experience a weekend that will grow you, stretch you, connect you, and help you discover how God might use you to shape the next generation.

Next Gen is more than a ministry. It’s a movement.
And we’d love for you to be part of it.

This won’t be another conference to attend — it’s a tribe to belong to.

Schedule:
Thursday 15th 4:00pm - Connect and conversation
6:00pm - Dinner
7:30pm - Session 1

Friday 16th - Sessions and team time

Saturday 17th - Sessions and team planning
1:30pm - Social fun time

Sunday 18th - Visit with LifeSwitch Church (If you have to head off on Saturday plan to do so as late into the day as you can!

events.name: Calligratherapy - Beginners
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Calligratherapy - Beginners
Many of us live sedentary lifestyles, sitting for up to eight hours or more a day hunched over our keyboard - all the while rarely taking a proper breath! Even if we wanted to take a deep enriching breath into the lower lobes of our lungs, we are limited due to our posture. Often due to the stresses and strains of a busy work and life balance, our unconscious brain can develop a pattern of holding, irregular and shadow breaths.
Does this sound like your experience? 
Not being able to breathe properly is the key cause of many chronic respiratory diseases (Nestor, 2020)
Calligratherapy combines science journalist James Nestor's theory on proper breathing with the philosophy of ancient Chinese calligraphy to promote a state of optimal wellbeing.
Calligratherapy has been developed specifically for those who have never practiced calligraphy before and who are interested in deriving the benefits without having to learn the language or all the characters. It integrates the simple and intuitive act of inhaling and exhaling into calligraphy practice with Eastern philosophy behind it.
A range of different breathing exercises are embedded into each 90 minute session focusing on different calligraphy scripts.  Over the five weeks, you will develop and practice the awareness of healthy breathing, while learning new techniques of Chinese soft brush calligraphy covering five different scripts. 
All materials included in course fee.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
Start a new creative practice in Chinese soft brush calligraphy
Develop your own mindfulness strategy
Better manage everyday stress levels and access a calm, empowered and positive state of mind
Find ways to explore eastern philosophy and develop deeper connections with your spiritual self. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.id: How to be a DJ - An Introduction-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington-Wellington High School
events.name: How to be a DJ - An Introduction
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
How to be a DJ - An Introduction
Always wanted to try being a DJ but not sure where to begin? Experienced and professional DJ Shan (Shannon Chng-Rawiri) will teach you all about the technical aspects, equipment and terminology, as well as the industry in general, and enable you to put together a confident short performance.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
Gain an understanding of the work content and career opportunities in this industry
Learn the difference between what a DJ is required to deliver in the following situations: Mobile, Club, Radio, Turntablist and Hobby
Participate in various practical activities: Slip Cueing and Baby Scratch, basic beat matching and song structures
Gain a good understanding of the equipment used and terminology including: - Tables: pitch control - Mixer: crossfader, input faders, EQ, gain, cue system - Needles: back tracking - Slip Mats
Learn about Counting Bars and Matching Tempos - The difference between a Bar, Phrases and BPM - Techniques to Count, Hand position and movement etc
Confidently present a 5 minute performance in class
The course will be held at DJ Shan’s studio at Shop 21, 73 Cuba Street, Wellington.  Bring headphones, a USB with your favourite music and a laptop, if you have one. Limited to eight participants.
Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Life Drawing - Beginners
This course will help artists and designers at all levels to develop their life-drawing skills. Starting with an exploration of structure, form, shape and proportion, we will progress through foreshortening while creating illusions of depth and atmosphere using light sourcing. You will also learn to draw using a range of media.
Please bring an A2 sketch pad, 2B and 4B pencils and an eraser.  Cost of model included in course fee.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to: 
- Draw the human form
- Comprehend structure and shape
- Demonstrate fundamental drawing skills
- Be familiar with proportion
- Use drawing media to create tonal range
Please note this course uses live models to draw from. It may include some nudity, including draped models and possibly completely unclothed models. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.name: Scriptwriting
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Scriptwriting
During this course, you will develop and build on your writing skills so you can confidently produce scripted narrative. You will learn how the basics of scriptwriting work, whether it be for stage or screen.
 Topics discussed and practised include the three act structure, script format, the differences between writing for film, theatre and television, creating dialogue, world building and more.
 We’ll take part in exercises, watch clips and have group discussions. In workshops, you’ll give and receive feedback, developing your scriptwriting skills through both. By the end of the course, you’ll be ready to finish your script, and take the next steps toward bringing it from page to stage (or screen!).
 Bring pen and paper.
 By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Analyse film, television, and theatre with a new lens for the way scripted stories work
- Develop character arcs and dynamics
- Create and build worlds
- Write effective dialogue and work with subtext
- Develop and implement a writing routine that works for your life
- Give and receive constructive feedback on your writing
- Have the confidence to put your work out into the world
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Improv is theatre without a script and a fun way to build your skills in many areas, including team work, public speaking, storytelling and on-your-feet creative thinking.
This is the perfect place for absolute beginners to get acquainted with the joy and art of improvisation, inspired by the generous creative philosophy of Keith Johnstone. It's also a great place to get back into improv if you've been away from it for a while.
WIT has been teaching this course in association with the CEC for almost 20 years now. It uses fun games and structured exercises to teach the foundation skills of improv. These are a prerequisite for further courses and membership of WIT (www.wit.org.nz), as well as useful in themselves.
If you have questions about the course, please contact WIT directly on info@wit.org.nz.
By the end of the course, you'll have: 
• Explored basic principles of improvisation
• Enjoyed interacting in a friendly, positive and supportive environment
• Developed more confidence, presentation and communication skills
• Experienced joyful moments of improvisation
The course will end with a directed demonstration of class exercises for invited friends and family.
[This is a physical activity that involves an element of risk.  While all possible measures are taken to prevent accidents or injury, please note that participation is at your own risk]. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Presented by: TEG Live
TEG Live is proud to present Secret Screenings with Beau Miles, an intimate live touring show bringing Beau’s unreleased and unfinished film collection — none of it yet on YouTube — to venues across Australia and New Zealand in 2026.
The premise is straightforward: three or four of Beau’s new films, shown somewhere between a first and final draft. The audience won’t know the titles before they see them. The films aren’t finished, but are entirely watchable. And in between screenings, Beau tells the stories behind them - why they exist, why they look the way they do, and why a man who lives on a small farmlet in Victoria keeps putting himself through things that are, by his own admission, sometimes remarkable, often mundane, and occasionally disgusting.
It’s an evening that moves between film and live performance - part director’s commentary, part stand-up tangent, part confessional. The stories may or may not connect to the films. The Q&A that closes the evening has been independently verified as world-class by one audience member. That audience member was Beau. He’s confident.
Beau Miles has built a devoted following through a body of work that resists easy categorisation - adventure films that aren’t really about adventure, mundane experiments that turn out to mean something, and a stubborn commitment to doing things slowly and in person. Secret Screenings brings that sensibility into the room: unmediated, unfinished, and told by the person who made it.

events.long_description:
Elegance - Wellington
Dynamic British Isata Kanneh-Mason make her NZSO debut in a concert featuring Mozart, Brahms and Andrée.

Programme:
Andrée Andante Recitative
WA Mozart Piano Concerto No. 27
Brahms Serenade No. 1

Isata Kanneh-Mason, the eldest sibling in a dynasty of extraordinary musicians, is being lauded as a pianist who is “the real deal” (classical-scene.com). What a treat to hear her bring such intelligent elegance to Mozart’s last piano concerto. Praised by BBC Music Magazine as capable of making “lines sing beautifully and virtuosic passages dance, finding intimacy and eloquence at telling moments”, Kanneh-Mason is the perfect performer to bring this mature, serenely lovely concerto to Aotearoa New Zealand audiences.

To round out this programme, the NZSO performs two works that deserve a wider audience. Brahms’ Serenade harks back to Mozart’s own delightful serenades, while Elfrida Andrée’s Andante Recitative, written in 1878, was only rediscovered in the 1980s, and “open[s] in broody darkness, but quickly blossom[s] into optimistic, songful melody” (Michael Clive).

Secret Screenings with Beau Miles (Wellington)
Beau Miles is taking his Secret Screenings on the road - bringing a collection of new, unreleased films to intimate venues across Australia and New Zealand in 2026. None of them are on YouTube yet. You’ll see them first.

The idea is simple: three or four of Beau’s films, shown somewhere between a first and final draft. None of them fully finished, but are entirely watchable. None of them named in advance. You won’t know what you’re watching until it starts - and each one has a story to tell beyond what’s on screen.

In between films, Beau tells a bunch of stories about why the films are the way they are. Why he loves finding things. Why he needs to shower more. Why a man living on a small farmlet in regional Victoria keeps dragging himself into rivers and eating spotty bananas and filming it all. The stories may or may not have anything to do with the films being shown. That’s part of the deal.

The evening finishes with a Q&A - voted the best thing ever witnessed by one audience member. That audience member was Beau. He stands by it.

events.name: Financial Planning for Retirement
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Financial Planning for Retirement
Massey University's annual Retirement Expenditure Guidelines study (2019) found:
Just 40% of pre-retirees believed they were well-prepared for retirement, and 57% considered retirement to be a concern.  They also confirmed, New Zealand Superannuation is not sufficient to fund the retirement most people want.
Ministry of Social Development (2020):
22% of all people receiving New Zealand Superannuation also receive additional support payments, with over 44,000 superannuants receiving additional accommodation support,
And if you needed to obtain Government assisted accommodation, at the end of March 2020, more than 16,300 households were waiting for state or social housing.
Living in a motel or boarding house with strangers (who may have other vulnerable backgrounds) is not an ideal or safe location to spend your retirement years.   But for many, it is the only option they can afford.
If you have not planned for your retirement, then this course is you! 
This course has been developed for people in their 50’s or 60’s that are looking at retirement and have no idea if they can financially survive it: what to do, what $’s they need, how or where they can generate additional income, or even where to go to get help. 
It is targeted towards those that still have some time (for some - not much) to make adjustments, learn some basic financial skills, make some big decisions, and positively influence the quality of their pending retirement. 
You will be introduced to a simple step by step guide to developing a financial plan for retirement. 
You will work though a case study in class, and can then go away and repeat the process with your own data/details.  You will be provided with comprehensive course notes to enable you to update the case study information with your own information. 
At each step, key considerations and financial concepts will be defined, explained and discussed to help you understand the financial requirements of retirement.  
Are you ready for the retirement lifestyle you hoped or dreamed of?  If not, then this course is for you.
A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
Disclaimer:  The tutors are not financial advisors.  No investments, products nor specific recommendations will be provided.  A step by step planning process will be taught by working through a case study.  Key considerations that should be used by the participants when looking at their own options to bridge the financial gap between what is available through superannuation and what is required to meet lifestyle goals will be provided and discussed.  Product names may be used in examples and explanations to help participants understand the financial concepts and the planning process.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Genealogy - Basics of ancestry.com DNA tests
Got your test results back and still wondering what a centiMorgan or a shared match is?  Find out what the size of your match means and the tools available to help you work out possible family relationships.
We'll start by looking at Clustering and how the Grouping tool on Ancestry.com can help with this.  We'll also look at the ThruLines and Common Ancestors tools to see how they can provide suggestions for knocking down brick walls in your research.
Also covered during this course are other websites you can upload your results to, how to manage other family member's DNA test results and other tools available when you get a bit more advanced - and just in case you need help in the future, we'll look at some of the places you could get this from.
Please note:  this course will only cover DNA tests taken through Ancestry.com  All computer courses are run in the school computer labs and you are required to use the school desktops for the duration of the course (you are not able to use your own laptop).  Some of the courses may require you to login onto the network. 
Bring a USB stick and your Ancestry.com login details.
 By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
-  Understand the information provided by Ancestry.com about your DNA matches
-  Use the Grouping, ThruLines and Common Ancestors tools on Ancestry.com
-  Use the Shared CentiMorgan tool on DNAPainter.com
-  Understand where to find other tools
-  Understand the options for using other DNA websites
-  Understand where to get further help
 Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

From their album debut in 1968 to their last album in 1972 the band produced some highly memorable songs. Many of them are still regularly played today. events.long_description:
Fly Fishing
An introduction to fly fishing for trout, which includes choosing gear, finding the fish, fly tying and casting and a practical fishing session.
By the end of the course, you'll be able to: 
• Apply the basics of fly fishing
• Choose the appropriate tackle
• Have an appreciation of the entomology associated with trout
• Demonstrate practical aspects of casting, knot tying, tying of flies and stream craft
• Present an appropriate fly to the water with a reasonable chance of catching a trout
There are three sessions at the high school, plus a session at the Capital Trout Centre and a choice of two river sessions (times and dates to be discussed at the class). Tutors from Wellington Flyfishers Club.   There may also be additional opportunity before class (from 6pm) for casting practice before sessions 2 and 3.
[This is a physical activity that involves an element of risk.  While all possible measures are taken to prevent accidents or injury, please note that participation is at your own risk]. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.name: Understanding and Supporting Your Neurodivergent Child: A Practical Parent Course
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
This course is designed for parents and caregivers of neurodivergent tamariki who want practical, evidence-informed strategies to better support their child’s wellbeing, behaviour, and participation at home and school.
Across three sessions, we will explore the foundations of neurodiversity, including different neurotypes, strengths-based perspectives, and neuroaffirming language. You will gain insight into sensory processing, regulation, and the critical role of connection and co-regulation in supporting your child.
The course also provides guidance on navigating Aotearoa New Zealand’s health, education, and disability systems, including how to access supports and advocate effectively for your child. We will explore common challenges such as school refusal, burnout, and meltdowns, with practical strategies for prevention, in-the-moment support, and recovery.
There will be opportunities for discussion, reflection, and shared learning, as well as a Q&A-style panel session incorporating both professional and lived experience perspectives.
This is a group-based learning environment (not individual therapy), with an emphasis on practical tools, connection, and empowerment.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.name: Mudhoney tickets
events.venue: Meow Nui, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
DUE TO OVERWHELMING DEMAND, MUDHONEY HAS UPGRADED VENUES TO MEOW NUI.
For the first time in over a decade, Mudhoney return to New Zealand for a run of intimate shows. Renowned for their ferocious live performances, the band continue to deliver the same high-voltage mix of sludgy riffs, pounding rhythms and Mark Arm's unmistakable snarl that made them one of the most influential rock bands of their era.
Formed in Seattle in 1988, Mudhoney helped define the sound that would become known as grunge, combining garage rock, punk and heavy distortion into something raw, loud and entirely their own. As one of the cornerstone acts of legendary independent label Sub Pop, the band became a crucial influence on the explosion of alternative rock that followed, with tracks like 'Touch Me I'm Sick' and 'Suck You Dry' remaining enduring underground classics.
More than 35 years on, Mudhoney remain as vital as ever, continuing to release acclaimed new music and proving night after night why they are regarded as one of the greatest live rock bands of their generation.
"When it comes to grunge, or even just Seattle, I think there was one band that made the definitive music of the time. It wasn't us or Nirvana, but Mudhoney. Nirvana delivered it to the world, but Mudhoney were the band of that time and sound." – Eddie Vedder (Pearl Jam)
A rare chance to experience genuine grunge royalty up close.

events.long_description:
Posture Perfection is Possible!
Are you a computer slouch, feeling stiff and tense at work? Do you find it difficult to maintain a good posture?  Does your posture cause back, neck or shoulder tension?  Would you like to enjoy more freedom in everyday activities?
Under the guidance of an experienced teacher, we'll explore movement in ways that help you reduce tense unhelpful habits.  Movement lessons are done on the floor or sitting on a chair and are based on the pioneering work of Israeli physicist and engineer Dr. Moshe Feldenkrais.
This workshop is suitable for all ages (over 16) and fitness levels.
By the end of the workshop, you'll be able to:
• Identify and reduce muscle tension
• Move with more lightness and freedom
• Improve your posture
• Describe some basic anatomy
• Have tools to use at home and at work
Bring two blankets (or a mat and a blanket) and wear loose, warm and comfortable clothing. Tea and coffee provided but bring your lunch. Please note that instructions are given verbally rather than by demonstration, so good hearing and understanding of English is required.
Feel free to contact the tutor, Sue Field on 027 466 7123, if you have any questions. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Cheesemaking - Brie and Queso Fresco
The ultimate class in practical cheese making!   Learn all you need to know to replicate making NZ style Brie and Queso Fresco at home.  You will be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of Brie. Then, while the Brie is ripening and setting (don't worry, all terminology will be explained!), we will make Queso Fresco together.  
All ingredients are provided as are recipes and detailed handouts to take away with you. Bring an apron, a dishcloth, 3 or 4 tea towels, a pen to take notes and a 2 litre container and plastic re-sealable food bags to take your cheese home.
During the workshop, the following topics will also be covered: Milk and where to source it, hygiene and sanitation, equipment required and the origins of the cheeses you are about to make.  You will also receive comprehensive instruction on how to mature your Brie cheese over the next few weeks.
A small break will be provided and you will have the opportunity to purchase equipment and cheesemaking ingredients after the workshop should you wish to replicate the experience at home.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
-  Make Brie and Queso Fresco
- Recall the best milk to use and where to source it from
- Name and identify what equipment and ingredients you need to make Brie and Queso Fresco
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.name: The Cake Club Picnic 3.0✨️
events.venue: Bellevue Gardens Hotel,140 Woburn Road, Lower Hutt, New Zealand
events.long_description:
The Cake Club Picnic 3.0✨️
Love cake? So do we! Join us at The Cake Club Picnic – a one-of-a-kind gathering dedicated exclusively to cake. You don't want to miss it!

About this Event

Welcome to The Cake Club Picnic! 🍰
By popular demand and our first cake picnic was a success, we are happy to host another epic Cake Picnic!
Join us for a deliciously fun day out at Bellevue Gardens Hotel on Sunday, November the 8th, 2026.
Whether your a professional baker, a passionate home baker, or simply someone with a sweet tooth, The Cake Club Picnic is the perfect event to indulge your love of all things cake!
Entry requires both a ticket and a cake - one per person.
Everyone attending must bring a cake of their own. No cake, no entry - no exceptions. This rule keeps things fair and fun for everyone involved.
Even if you're bringing a guest under tickets you have purchased, they must bring a cake too. Sharing one cake between two people won’t cut it. We appreciate your understanding and commitment to the cake-loving community!
🎂 What to Expect:
A relaxed indoor and outdoor garden setting - enjoy the space rain or shine!
A shared cake table filled with baked goodies brought by everyone attending - taste, share, and show off your creations!
Chill vibes and great company - meet fellow cake lovers, swap stories, and make sweet memories.
Picnic-style seating - bring a blanket, find a sunny spot, or grab a seat indoors.
A self-service tea and coffee station to keep your cup full as you sample cakes.
Cake Size Requirement:
Please bring a cake that can generously serve at least 12 people. Think full-sized bakes -enough to share and make sure everyone gets a proper slice (or two)! 🎂✨ - REMEMBER - CAKE ONLY!
Cake Set-Up:
You’re welcome to do final touch-ups at the venue, but please avoid full setups or major decorating on-site. Display tables will be shared with other guests, so we want to keep things smooth and stress-free for everyone.
Serving Tools, cake detailed label & Cake Stands:
Please remember to bring your own serving tool so guests can easily cut and enjoy your cake.
We will provide you with a cake label card and card insert stick for everything to look uniformed!
Want to show off your creation? Feel free to bring a cake stand to elevate your cake-literally and visually! 🍰🔪✨
Boxes & Utensils:
We've got you covered! The host will provide boxes for you to pack up cake slices during the event, along with forks, spoons, napkins, and water to keep things easy and enjoyable. 🍴📦💧
Rubbish:
Let’s keep the vibes sweet and the space clean! Please use the bins provided on-site and help us leave the venue just as lovely as we found it. We also kindly ask that you take any leftover rubbish or personal items with you when you head out. ♻️🧼💛


Disclaimer & Event Guidelines
This is a community-friendly event, and all participants are expected to behave in a respectful and responsible manner toward others. By attending, you agree to be patient, follow the event rules, and respect everyone's space, time, and contributions.
If you are bringing a homemade cake, you confirm that it has been prepared in a clean and safe environment to the best of your ability. Please note that food is consumed at your own risk, and the event organisers and venue accept no responsibility for allergic reactions or food-related illnesses.
Cakes that contain common allergens (e.g. nuts, dairy, eggs, gluten) must be clearly labelled to help others make informed choices.
This event will be photographed and filmed for use in future marketing, content, and social media promotion. By attending, you grant permission for your image and likeness to be used across both online and offline platforms by the event organisers.
You attend this event at your own risk. The organisers, volunteers, and venue are not liable for any injury, loss, damage, theft, or illness that may occur. Please keep an eye on your personal belongings - you are responsible for them.
Thank you for helping us keep this a fun, safe, and inclusive experience for all! 🍰💛
Bring your appetite, your friends, and your best bake. Everyone is welcome - just come ready to relax, connect, and enjoy a truly sweet day out!


Agenda


🕑: 11:00 AM - 03:00 PM
How the Cake Club Picnic Work
Info: You’re welcome to arrive from 11AM to set up your cake and take some time to admire everyone else’s beautiful creations before the event officially begins. Cake Cutting & Group Rotation-

To keep things fun and relaxed, all participants will be grouped by coloured wristbands, which you’ll receive at the registration table.

When it’s your group’s turn, you’ll have 5 minutes to browse and slice a piece from any cakes you’d like to try. This helps make sure everyone gets a fair and enjoyable experience sampling all the amazing creations.

Once all groups have had their turn, feel free to go back and enjoy any leftover cake! ?


Important: Please don’t take or use other people’s serving utensils or display stands - these belong to the cake owners and need to be returned to them. Thank you for being respectful and keeping the cake vibes sweet!

events.long_description:
Photography: Unlocking the Secrets to Captivating Images
Elevate your photography from ordinary to extraordinary and ensure your work stands out in the digital age. Creating captivating photographs and understanding what makes a photograph engaging is something every photographer should master. Camera settings are essential, but once you know them, you need to learn how to take photographs that stir emotions, impact your audience, and leave a lasting impression. After all, isn’t that the true purpose of photography? People don’t want to see the same landscapes or flowers they’ve seen thousands of times. But how do you turn what you love into something that makes people go, "Wow"?
Captivation in photography means stopping a viewer in their tracks, making them look, feel, and connect. It’s about delivering a photograph that enthrals, evokes profound emotions, and shifts perspectives.
In a world brimming with images, only a few have the power to truly captivate and linger in our memories.
 This pioneering course is your gateway to mastering the art of creating captivating photographs at a time when AI-generated images are saturating our visual landscape. Create something genuine and memorable—images that spark curiosity, evoke emotions, and inspire changes in perception. It's time to define your unique style, refine your vision, and make your mark.
 Course Outcomes
 By the end of the course, you’ll be able to: 
Identify the foundational elements that transform an ordinary image into a captivating one.
Create photographs that make people say "Wow" by applying techniques that add a spark of wonder to your shots.
Infuse your photographs with curiosity, making each frame a source of intrigue and interest.
Understand why some images linger in memory and how to make your photographs unforgettable.
Develop a unique style and vision that sets your work apart in the crowded digital landscape.

events.long_description:
Enigma - Wellington
NZSO Artistic Advisor and Principal Conductor Gemma New with legendary pianist Sir Stephen Hough present a concert of charm, mystery and bold vision.

Programme:
Ross Harris Concerto for Orchestra (World Premiere)
Saint-Saëns Piano Concerto No. 5 Egyptian
Elgar Enigma Variations

Edward Elgar’s greatest masterpiece remains swathed in mystery.

His Enigma Variations, a set of 14 variations on a theme you never actually hear, has been the subject of both intense scrutiny and great love, thanks to the compositional genius and throbbing heart pulsing in these compelling variations.

Similarly, Saint-Saëns’ Fifth Piano Concerto has beguiled audiences with its Eastern-inspired sounds — hence its Egyptian nickname. To weave his own spell on us, legendary pianist Sir Stephen Hough returns to our shores. Praised by Limelight for possessing “an other-worldly stillness and strength [and] the perfect technique combined with the utmost poetic fluency”, Hough promises to transport us to another world.

We proudly premiere Ross Harris’ Concerto for Orchestra. A four-time winner of the SOUNZ Contemporary Award, Harris’ artistry and bold vision electrifies this newly commissioned work, driving the orchestra to new heights.

Cheesemaking - Farmhouse Cheddar Cheese Workshop
During this hands-on workshop, you’ll be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of farmhouse style cheddar.
The fee includes a cheese press (value $95.00) which can be used every time you want to make a hard cheese. It holds up to 6 litres of milk and this is what you’ll be taking your cheese home in to press for 12 hours after the workshop. All ingredients, recipes and a full set of course notes are provided.
You’ll also receive comprehensive instruction on how to wax (if you choose to) and then mature your cheese over the next five weeks. Alexis will also demonstrate how to make halloumi cheese which will then be grilled for you to enjoy! There’ll be a short lunch break and cheese making supplies such as wax will be available to purchase.
